title: Americans don’t have to choose between our AI future and ripping off copyright owners
description: The DOJ's embrace of fair use for AI training breaks with the White House's own framework, as OpenAI, Microsoft and news groups battle over copyright.
fullContent:
One of the biggest court battles over artificial intelligence (AI) is putting an age-old legal principle to the test — and raising important questions about the Trump administration's AI policy.

Several news organizations, including The New York Times, are suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using millions of newspaper articles to train AI systems. The newspapers argue that the tech firms violated basic copyright protections. The tech firms contend that training their models on those articles qualifies as "fair use," a longstanding principle that allows copyrighted material to be used in certain ways without permission from or compensation to the copyright owner.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has sided squarely with OpenAI's position — breaking with the administration's previously more balanced stance on the issue. The DOJ filed a statement of interest embracing an extreme vision of fair use that would grant AI companies virtually unfettered access to copyrighted material for commercial training, without obtaining permission from or compensating the creators whose works fuel these systems.

MIKE DAVIS: THE TRUMP DOJ SHOULD WITHDRAW ITS STATEMENT OF INTEREST IN THE OPENAI LAWSUIT

This expansive interpretation threatens to turn a narrow copyright exception into a blanket exemption for the world's most powerful and profitable industries.

The DOJ's reasoning is that requiring a copyright license for material used in AI training would impose high costs on AI developers. It claims those costs could make it harder for small companies to compete and hamper U.S. AI leadership and national security.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Those concerns deserve consideration. But the DOJ's aggressive arguments in the brief depart from more measured guidance elsewhere in the administration. The White House's official AI framework acknowledges valid arguments on both sides of the copyright debate.

Likewise, the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, adopted by G20 ministers at the Commerce Department's recent Innovation Ministerial, recognize that the intersection of AI and copyright poses "complex legal and policy questions." The principles note the "essential role" of copyright protections in supporting creators and call for respecting IP as a pillar of G20 AI policy.

MUSIC INDUSTRY FENDS OFF FLOOD OF AI MUSIC 'STEALING' THE CHARTS

The DOJ statement also overlooks how its stance could favor larger AI companies over smaller firms and startups. Several AI startups have argued that paying for the material they use provides more reliable access to training material, reduces legal uncertainty and improves models. Other companies have emerged to aggregate copyrights and make licensing easier.

It's particularly problematic for large AI companies to complain about paying for access to copyrighted materials. They are among the best positioned to pay for those materials, and doing so would help develop the kind of licensing markets they claim are lacking.

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

And even if national security were a legitimate justification, the government could not simply disregard property rights. The Constitution and other laws require just compensation when private property is taken for public use, and intellectual property rights are still property rights. Letting AI firms appropriate creators' IP without permission or compensation would be akin to letting data center builders seize private land without paying fair value.

If courts adopt the DOJ's position that fair use protects AI developers in virtually all circumstances, it would reduce incentives to create new works. Copyrights encourage creative work by assuring writers, artists and other creators that their work can't be easily stolen or copied. Licensing those rights allows creators to earn a living and underpins over $1 trillion in U.S. economic activity.

Weaker copyrights could result in fewer human-created books, articles, research papers, films and songs. Ironically, that could eventually leave AI systems with fewer and lower-quality materials to train on – a scenario that serves no one's interests.

All of this is why the Trump administration would be wise to follow its own AI framework and let the court system evaluate AI copyright disputes case by case, rather than arguing for unfettered fair use exceptions.

Policymakers also have a role to play. One promising bill is the bipartisan CLEAR Act. Introduced in February by California Democrat Sen. Adam Schiff and Utah Republican Sen. John Curtis, the CLEAR Act would require AI developers to publicly disclose the copyrighted works used in each new generative-AI model's training dataset.

The proposal would not settle whether any particular training practice qualifies as fair use. But it would give creators more information about whether their work helped train an AI system, enabling them to pursue appropriate compensation or other remedies when they believe their rights have been violated.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That kind of targeted reform offers a useful model for copyright enforcement in the age of AI. Rather than treating licensing as an obstacle to innovation, policymakers should foster a market where AI developers can efficiently license copyrighted material while respecting creators' rights.

AI innovation is vital to America's future. But America's creative industries still depend on strong copyright protections. Policymakers need to promote both.

title: Cardinals may start their fourth QB in four weeks as Carson Beck has injury after first career start
description: Carson Beck's back spasms could push the Arizona Cardinals to 40-year-old Josh Johnson, their fourth starting quarterback in four weeks, versus the Chiefs.
fullContent:
The Arizona Cardinals quarterback carousel is still spinning.

After just one start, Cardinals rookie Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms and may not play Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs. If the 25-year-old cannot play, the Cardinals will turn to 40-year-old Josh Johnson.

If Johnson starts, it will be the Cardinals' fourth different starting quarterback in four weeks. Head coach Mike LaFleur reported Friday that they will see how Beck responds to treatment tomorrow, and that he doesn't think Beck will be out multiple weeks.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"You go with the people who know what they’re doing to treat it. It’s not like this is the first time he’s dealt with it," LaFleur said. "We’ll see more tomorrow."

Beck had dealt with back spasms earlier in the season. The former Miami star quarterback went 11 for 18 for 108 yards with two interceptions in the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in his first career start Sunday.

For LaFleur, he has familiarity with Johnson, as he was the offensive coordinator with the New York Jets in 2021 and called plays for the journeyman quarterback then.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Cool part is, if it is Josh, I’ve called plays for him before and had a really great experience calling plays for him," LaFleur said. "So, we’ll go shoot our shot and I expect nothing less from our guys."

If you told Cardinals fans a month ago that the team might be on its fourth different starting quarterback in four weeks, they'd be pretty surprised. In Week 8, the Cardinals started Jacoby Brissett against the Dallas Cowboys. He was benched in the second half for Gardner Minshew II, and the former Jacksonville Jaguars starter led the team to a thrilling comeback.

In the aftermath of that, the Cardinals named Minshew the starting quarterback and traded Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. In Week 9, Minshew's first start, he suffered a UCL injury that required season-ending surgery.

With Brissett in Baltimore and Minshew hurt, the Cardinals started Beck in Week 10 and now might be turning to Johnson in Week 11. Adding to the chaos, Johnson only joined the Cardinals on Nov. 10, when the team signed him off the Cincinnati Bengals practice squad.

The 3-7 Cardinals play the 7-2 Chiefs on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET.

title: Robert Kiyosaki Cheers the Bitcoin, Gold, and Silver Crash. Here is Why
description:
Robert Kiyosaki is once again welcoming a market crash. The “Rich Dad Poor Dad” author says he is most excited about Bitcoin’s slide and cannot wait to buy more. However, not everyone shares his optimism, as some analysts warn of a deeper correction ahead. Why Kiyosaki Welcomes the Market Crash The sell-off hit hard. Bitcoin
The post Robert Kiyosaki Cheers the Bitcoin, Gold, and Silver Crash. Here is Why appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Robert Kiyosaki is once again welcoming a market crash. The “Rich Dad Poor Dad” author says he is most excited about Bitcoin’s slide and cannot wait to buy more.

However, not everyone shares his optimism, as some analysts warn of a deeper correction ahead.

Why Kiyosaki Welcomes the Market Crash

The sell-off hit hard. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 and now trades near $58,200. It lost 31% over the past month.

Meanwhile, gold and silver shed roughly $1 trillion in six hours after Fed minutes signaled further rate hikes.

Kiyosaki blamed problems at the Federal Reserve, banks, and bond markets, along with US federal debt near $40.6 trillion.

In contrast, Bitcoin’s hard cap of 21 million coins makes it unique money, he argued.

His stance is consistent. Kiyosaki has long targeted $250,000 Bitcoin and openly uses debt to buy assets. Not everyone shares that confidence, however.

Is the Crash Really a Buying Opportunity?

Some analysts agree. Ash Crypto listed six reasons why November could prove a strong entry point.

These include past cycle bottoms after US midterms and possibly completed pre-IPO selling. The analyst also cited rising bank holdings of Bitcoin ETFs, which already control about 1.24 million BTC.

Lower oil prices, improving US manufacturing, and typical post-midterm stock gains round out the list.

Still, caution remains. Veteran trader Peter Brandt noted that every major Bitcoin bull market has ended with a correction of at least 75%. Measured from the recent high, that move would imply roughly $31,500.

With Bitcoin down about 54%, that scenario would require a much deeper slide.

Other traders watch intermediate support near $55,000, now just 6% below current prices. Meanwhile, long-term holders like Michael Saylor keep emphasizing accumulation.

“I began buying Bitcoin at $20,000 a coin… after the last crash. Will wait for Bitcoin bottom again. Lesson: ‘Your profit is made when you buy…not when you sell’,” Kiyosaki said in another post.

Ultimately, the debate remains open. Kiyosaki sees a chance to buy scarce assets, while history leaves room for a deeper correction first.

The post Robert Kiyosaki Cheers the Bitcoin, Gold, and Silver Crash. Here is Why appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Stocks continue steep dive as AI worries fuel punishing sell-off
description:
US stocks tanked on Friday as a punishing sell-off deepened after Anthropic's (ANT) successful initial public offering failed to quell broad uncertainty about artificial intelligence safety and financing. 
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) dropped 1.9% after the blue-chip index fell below 50,000 and neared a correction. The S&P 500 (^GSPC) declined by 3.6%. Both the Dow and S&P 500 closed in correction territory, or more than 10% off their peaks.  
The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) fell nearly 5.3%, with the tech-heavy index closing negative for the year. 
Investors went risk-off on Friday as semiconductor stocks led an AI trade sell-off. Nvidia (NVDA) shares extended losses, falling 14%. AMD (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO), and Micron (MU) stocks also suffered double-digit drops. 
Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre finds the damage beneath the Nasdaq Composite index is even worse. Seventy-one of the 101 stocks in the narrower Nasdaq-100 (^NDX) were in bear market territory on Friday, including 20 of the 20 semiconductor and memory chip stocks in that index. 
A day after its record-breaking debut, Anthropic shares fell 8%, though they remain narrowly above their IPO price of $83. After a big pop on its IPO day, Anthropic faces a test in the markets to see whether it can sustain the momentum.

Other assets slid on Friday as well. Gold futures (GC=F) dropped nearly 4%, while the price of so-called digital gold — bitcoin (BTC-USD) — dropped below $59,000 to trade at its lowest price since July. 


This article originally appeared on Yahoo Finance at https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-friday-november-19-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-anthropic-nvidia-141644188.html

title: NEAR Sinks 12% Onto Its 200-Day SMA: Three Paths Ahead
description:
Key Takeaways Friday’s high stopped under the 0.618 level. Price sits about 3% above the 200-day. RSI near 31.7, not […]
The post NEAR Sinks 12% Onto Its 200-Day SMA: Three Paths Ahead appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • Friday’s high stopped under the 0.618 level.
  • Price sits about 3% above the 200-day.
  • RSI near 31.7, not yet oversold.
  • Heavy selling volume, two hours before the close.

Two days ago, Coindoo’s analysis of NEAR’s three-level squeeze marked the 0.618 retracement near $3.23 as the floor of a 29-cent band. Friday’s candle ended that setup.

Out of the Bottom of the Band

NEAR traded at $3.34 when that analysis ran, with the 0.618 below, the 100-day average above and the upper edge of its descending channel pressing down on price.

On Thursday, a push higher poked above the channel line and then closed back inside, at $3.21, just under the 0.618. Friday opened at that level and reached $3.226, less than a cent below the 0.618 at $3.229, before the selling started. The low came at $2.76. As of 21:42 UTC, with about two hours left in the session, NEAR traded at $2.83, down 11.94% on the day and about 15% below where it stood on November 18. The drop came as the broader crypto market sold off.

Resting on the 200-Day

The November 18 piece laid out what losing the 0.618 would expose: the rising 200-day average, then the 0.786 retracement beneath it. NEAR is now at the first of those. The 200-day has crept up from $2.72 to $2.74 since then, and Friday’s low stopped just above it.

The averages above price point in different directions. The 50-day, at $4.34, is falling and sits near the 0.382 retracement at $4.28, making that the highest resistance band on the chart. The 100-day at $3.55 is still rising, as is the 200-day. There has been no bearish crossover between any of them yet, but the 50-day has dropped about eight cents in two days and is closing in on the 100-day from above. NEAR now trades 53% below its mid-October high near $5.99.

Inside the Channel

The descending channel that began in late October is still intact. Every rally since then has stopped at its upper line, Thursday’s included, and Friday’s high came where that line runs just under the 0.618. Price now sits in the lower half of the channel. The channel’s lower line runs below the 200-day and is sloping down toward the 0.786 level, so the two will be close together within days if the channel holds its shape.

What Sits Below the 200-Day

The levels under the 200-day map to two phases of the rally. The 0.786 near $2.48 sits in the September shelf where NEAR traded between $2.40 and $2.50 before its mid-September breakout. $2.20 sits at the lower part of that consolidation. The full retracement near $1.52 marks the August low the whole Fibonacci grid starts from.

Three Ways From Here

The 200-day breaks
daily close < $2.70
The rising average stops acting as support, and the 0.786 near $2.48 becomes the next reference, with $2.20 below it if the channel floor gives way. Rebounds into the $3.00–$3.15 zone would be the first test from underneath.
The break fails
dip < $2.74, fast reclaim > $2.80
A quick move back above $2.80 after a dip under the 200-day would leave sellers trapped below the average. The deeper version is a washout into $2.45–$2.50, where the 0.786 meets the September shelf, with RSI falling into the low-to-mid 20s.
The channel breaks upward
daily close > $3.30–$3.35
NEAR would be back above the 0.618 and outside the channel, with the 100-day at $3.55 and the 0.5 near $3.76 next. The November 17 close near $3.40, which unwound within two days, shows that a single close up there isn’t enough on its own.

For now, the nearest support is the 200-day, about 3% below price, and the nearest resistance is the 0.618, about 14% above.

title: Knicks star Jalen Brunson reveals how he really feels about 'King of New York' nickname
description: Jalen Brunson reacted to "King of New York" talk after leading the New York Knicks to their first NBA title in 53 years during a recent interview.
fullContent:
When you help lead the New York Knicks to its first NBA title in 53 years, in a city that hasn’t seen a "Big Four" team win their championship since the New York Giants in 2011, you get called the "King of New York."

After all, ask anyone around the five boroughs and they’ll tell you: New York City is a basketball town when the Knicks are on top.

Jalen Brunson, the NBA Finals MVP and Knicks superstar point guard, has been hearing "King of New York" thrown around from friends and fans alike since the victory over the San Antonio Spurs this past summer. It’s a moniker synonymous with greatness in a city that begs for it with all its teams and superstar athletes.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

To hear it means you’ve accomplished greatness in a city that demands it each season, or else the year is a failure. There’s pressure enough to play in the "World’s Greatest Arena" in Madison Square Garden as the face of the Knicks, but how does Brunson handle being called "King of New York?"

His answer tells you exactly where his mindset is this season, and the many to come.

"To be honest with you, I don’t want to say it’s annoying. It’s more of like when people say that, it’s cool to hear," he told OutKick in a recent interview, while highlighting his partnership with Lowe’s ahead of their big Black Friday activation. "A lot of people who I know, know I don’t like it. So, they’ll just say it to annoy me."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Brunson doesn’t have to explain why he doesn’t like it. The Villanova product has always gone about his business, staying humble and never being boisterous, though he has every reason to be considering what he’s accomplished alongside his Knicks teammates.

Yes, he’s won a championship, perhaps the one title that meant more than the rest in this great city. But his answer says many things, including one isn’t enough.

However, to be called "King of New York" — the same nickname Babe Ruth, Mickey Mantle, Lawrence Taylor, Mark Messier, Eli Manning, Derek Jeter and many others have worn over the years — is something Brunson appreciates.

Even if he doesn’t feel that way himself.

"The one thing that I’ll always think about is when you’re working to achieve something, like a goal to win a championship, you’d be surprised of all the little things that come with it," he explained. "The things that are cool, the things that are not. The pros and cons to it.'

"So, just to be thrown in that conversation with a lot of New York athlete greats, I mean, it’s a real honor. It’s something I don’t take lightly. I would never proclaim myself that."

KNICKS STAR JALEN BRUNSON IS A MAN OF THE PEOPLE, REVEALS THE ONE THING HE CAN'T LIVE WITHOUT

He may not call himself "King of New York," but that’s not going to stop the scores of Knicks fans who can’t help themselves if they see him outside The Garden.

He’s earned it, but in Brunson’s mind, there’s more to be accomplished, including defending that title this season.

Brunson will be in the midst of his back-to-back title pursuit with the Knicks on Black Friday, but as Lowe’s "Bucket Expert," he’s also spreading the word about the company’s exciting deals including a customer-favorite "Black Friday Mystery Bucket."

On Nov. 27, the first 150 MyLowe’s Rewards members at participating Lowe’s stores will receive exclusive giveaways, and additionally, more than $15 million in prizes will be available for four lucky MyLowe’s Rewards members at every store.

The first 50 members at each store will receive a free Lowe’s Black Friday Mystery Bucket packed with 10-plus products and offers, and four members of the first 50 will win one of the day’s top prizes: A free appliance under $2,000, an EGO Outdoor power tool, a Blackstone grilling package or a CRAFTSMANtools package.

With deals abundant, Brunson is excited to be involved.

"It’s a really cool thing to be a part of. I’m just honored to be associated with Lowe’s and this deal. Happy to be a part of it," he said.

Brunson added, "You’re doing yourself a disservice," if you intend on hitting Lowe’s on Black Friday and not signing up for MyLowe’s Rewards, as those who are not members can sign up for free ahead of Nov. 27.

After those first 50, the next 100 members will receive an exclusive Lowe’s Golden Mini Bucket, plus $5 in MyLowe’s Money, 20% off a purchase the following weekend, a free paint sample and a HomeCare+ offer.

title: Trump floats an unexpected name to be his successor as powerhouses Rubio and Vance stand by
description: Donald Trump stunned the White House press briefing room by asking Stephen Miller if he wants to run for president, as JD Vance and Marco Rubio looked on.
fullContent:
During a lighthearted Friday afternoon moment with the media inside the White House press briefing room, President Donald Trump floated a new name to succeed him as president, while two expected 2028 hopefuls stood by.

The president asked the media if they'd like to continue with the press conference — where Trump provided updates on his trip to China where he met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. This prompted laughs from Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who flanked him on either side during the briefing.

Then, he asked newly-minted Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, whom he called the "most powerful man in the world," to speak with members of the press.

MAGA VOTERS REVEAL WHO THEY WANT TO SEE LEAD GOP IN 2028

Miller took the podium and launched into a more than two-minute speech listing Trump's accomplishments from the first two years of his second term in office.

"I just wanted to say that what President Trump has achieved over the last two years is more than any president has achieved by far in American history. We can stand up here for four hours and go through achievement by achievement by achievement," Miller said.

He then rattled some of them off, including:

"Under his leadership, the next two years are going to be the greatest two years in American history," Miller said. "And I'm so proud to be his chief of staff to oversee on his behalf the staff in this building to keep delivering wins for this extraordinary American leader."

Trump was clearly impressed with Miller, who stepped in to replace Susie Wiles earlier this month following sweeping midterm losses for Republicans.

"We have breaking news! Breaking news!" Trump said. "He was better than these two guys," he added, turning towards Vance and Rubio, who both also spoke at the press conference.

"Do you want to run for president?" Trump asked Miller as he was leaving the podium, prompting laughter from the group.

STEPHEN MILLER'S INTERNAL MEMO UNLEASHES TRUMP AGENCIES AFTER 'ABSOLUTE CONTROL' UNDER WILES' REIGN

No major names from either party have yet to announce their intentions to run for president in 2028. But with the midterms finished, rumors have swirled about who will toss their hats in the ring.

Vance and Rubio are widely viewed as the two most viable options for Republicans.

Miller's name has not been previously floated as a contender for launching a White House bid.

title: LSU's $40 million football roster may have been a mirage, according to CFB expert Josh Pate
description: Josh Pate says LSU's $40-50 million roster under Lane Kiffin missed at quarterback, and the Tigers' 6-4 record could leave them out of the CFP race.
fullContent:
It's safe to say things aren't going the way anyone had planned for the LSU Tigers' football team in 2026.

Most fans and rivals agreed that when the Bayou Bengals went out and poached Lane Kiffin from Ole Miss and paired him with a roster that was reported to be between $40-50 million, year one was already being tagged with sky-high expectations.

Fast forward to mid-November, and not only are Kiffin and the Tigers out of the running for the SEC Championship, they are projected to miss the College Football Playoff entirely thanks to their shocking 6-4 record.

LANE KIFFIN BLAMES LSU'S $40+ MILLION ROSTER AFTER LOSS TO TEXAS: 'WE'LL HAVE BETTER ROSTERS’

Even potential wins against top-ten Tennessee this weekend and Golden Boot rivals Arkansas after Thanksgiving would do little to improve LSU's standing in the CFP polls.

So, what went wrong?

They hired the best available coach, paired him with an all-star staff that included one of the best defensive coordinators in the game in Blake Baker and armed him with one of the most expensive rosters in college football.

Shouldn't that be enough to expect a home run in year one?

College football commentator Josh Pate isn't buying the idea that an expensive roster guarantees success in this day and age.

JOSH PATE WAS EVICTED WHILE EARNING $27K. NOW, HE RUNS A COLLEGE FOOTBALL MEDIA EMPIRE

"I guess he enters next year on the hot seat," Pate said sarcastically while replying to a question from one of his viewers.

"I'm not asking anyone to feel sorry for Lane Kiffin," he continued.

Pate would go on to explain that giving someone unlimited resources doesn't always equate to leveling up, and Kiffin is no different.

"People kept throwing around that same data point: $40 million roster... What it was (was) LSU going and hiring their dream candidate at head coach, and then them just recklessly throwing around as much money as they could in the portal to put together a team to compete for a national title in year one."

It sounds like a simple formula, even to those who have been paying attention to the sport for a few years now in the NIL era, but it might not be that cut and dry.

"If this same exact roster was paid $28 million, would it be different? No, it's the same roster," he points out.

Plain and simple, the Tigers might have overpaid for some of the talent on their two-deep.

"You just paid a lot of money for 'average.'"

As Pate explains, LSU's pickups in the portal were great, but they only papered over deficiencies rather than provided quality depth, and, more importantly, they missed at the most important position: quarterback.

ARCH MANNING TURNS DEATH VALLEY INTO LSU’S FUNERAL AS TEXAS BURIES LANE KIFFIN’S CFP HOPES

"They didn't whiff on this portal class, by the way," he argues. "A lot of these dudes have been studs. It's just the most important position, there's not a stud at."

To his credit, Pate has been consistent with his takes on Kiffin and LSU.

The popular YouTube host said back in July that he thought the Tigers would miss the playoff outright in year one, and that caused some consternation among the LSU faithful.

Where LSU goes from here remains a mystery, but you can rest assured that Pate's words will fall on deaf ears.

Kiffin is making too much money and has been given too many resources to fail this badly in year one.

He will be going into a pivotal year two with the expectations ratcheted up considerably.

Should he miss the CFP again in 2027, it might be time for Kiffin to start looking for a good realtor in southern Louisiana.

title: Anthropic Stock—The Bull, Base And Bear Case Into Nasdaq-100 Entry
description:
Anthropic PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) fell from a $115.10 high on Nov 19 to an $83.15 low on Nov 20, a 27% drop in 2 sessions.
Underwriters fully exercised their option on 147 million extra shares, so the overallotment short that normally funds a price-support bid is already closed.
The Dec 15 lockup step makes up to 303 million shares, about $25.1 billion at $83, eligible for sale. That is about 5 times Bloomberg Intelligence’s $4.6 billion Nasdaq-100 buying estimate.
SpaceX, the last mega-IPO, first closed below its IPO price 5 weeks after listing and bottomed 22% lower before recovering.
Anthropic PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) is trading within cents of its $83 IPO price after one of the fastest reversals ever seen in a mega-listing.
The stock opened at $111.50 on Nov 19 and hit $115.10 intraday. It then closed at $97.17, up 17% on the day. On Friday, however, the selling resumed. Shares opened at $89.86 and fell to a low of $83.15. That is a 27% drop from the high in under 2 trading days.
The timing made it worse. The S&P 500 and the Dow both entered correction territory on Friday, and the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for 2026. As a result, the largest IPO on record is now trading as a high-beta proxy for the whole AI trade.
Most coverage now treats $83 as “support” simply because it is the IPO price. That assumption deserves a closer look. The deal mechanics suggest the usual safety net is already gone.
Chart 1: Anthropic gave back its entire IPO pop in 2 sessions. Day 2 is intraday as of about 12:50 p.m. ET, Nov 20.



How The Greenshoe Removed The Bodyguard
In a typical IPO, underwriters sell more shares than the base deal. Anthropic’s base offering was 980 million shares, and the pricing release granted the banks a 30-day option on 147 million more. That extra 15% creates a short position for the syndicate.
The short then becomes a tool. If the stock trades below the offer price, underwriters buy shares in the open market to cover it. 
That buying is the familiar “stabilization bid,” and it is permitted under SEC Regulation M, Rule 104. If the stock trades above the offer, the banks simply exercise the option and buy the extra shares from the company at $83.
Anthropic’s closing announcement confirmed the second path. The deal closed at 1.127 billion shares, including full exercise of the 147 million-share option. Gross IPO proceeds reached about $93.5 billion, or about $119.5 billion including a concurrent $26 billion private placement.
That detail matters for anyone treating $83 as a floor. Full exercise means the syndicate covered its short through the option. 
Consequently, there is no remaining short position that obliges the banks to buy shares on a dip. Stabilization is still legally possible during the window, but the economic reason to do it is gone.
In plain terms, $83 is now a psychological level, not a defended one.
The Float Math Works Against A Quick Bounce
Anthropic sold 1.127 billion shares against roughly 13.1 billion shares outstanding. That puts the IPO float near 8.6%. Under the registration filings on SEC EDGAR, non-founder employees could also sell up to 10% of their holdings from day one, about 315 million shares. 
Together, roughly 1.44 billion shares, or about 11% of the company, can trade today. A small float usually supports a new issue. 
Here, though, turnover was extreme. More than 846 million shares changed hands on day one, equal to about 75% of the entire IPO. In other words, much of the first-day buying came from fast money, and fast money leaves fast.
The supply calendar is also front-loaded. The staggered lockup in the S-1/A releases up to 303 million shares on Dec 15, another 303 million on Jan 5, 353 million on Jan 19, and 353 million on Feb 2. The Dec 15 step alone is worth about $25.1 billion at $83.
By comparison, Bloomberg Intelligence estimates about $4.6 billion of buying from Nasdaq-100 trackers under the index’s fast-entry rule. 
Broader estimates of first-month passive demand run near $19 billion. Either way, potential supply on a single unlock date exceeds the best-known source of mechanical demand.
Chart 2: The Dec 15 unlock alone outweighs Nasdaq-100 buying about 5 to 1. Eligible shares are a ceiling, not a sales forecast.




What Happened To Mega-IPOs That Broke Issue
History offers three useful templates.
SpaceX (2026). SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) priced at $135 in June, closed day one at $161 and hit $225.64 intraday on June 16. It joined the Nasdaq-100 on July 7, yet the index buying did not stop the slide. The stock first closed below its IPO price on July 16 at $131.11 and bottomed at $104.83 on Aug 3, about 22% under issue. It then recovered after its first lockup expiry and closed at $162.57 on Oct 9.
Meta Platforms (2012). Facebook priced at $38, closed its first session at $38.23 and broke issue on day 2. It went on to bottom near $17.55 in September 2012, more than 50% below the offer, before becoming one of the best-performing large caps of the following decade.
Uber Technologies (2019). Uber priced at $45 and closed its first day at $41.57, below issue from the start.
The pattern is consistent. Breaking the IPO price says more about positioning and supply than about the business. Even so, the drawdowns that follow can be deep. Notably, SpaceX’s slide happened after index inclusion, which suggests passive demand gets priced in early.
Chart 3: SpaceX broke issue 5 weeks after listing, bottomed 22% lower, then recovered.



Where The Real Floors Are
If the IPO price is not defended, then the next 4 weeks of share flows matter more than the $83 line. Six dated events stand out.

DateEventLikely effect on ANT

Nov 23Listed options open; Tradr 2x long (ANTT) and 2x short (ANTZ) ETFs begin trading on CboeDealer hedging can amplify moves either way
Nov 30Nasdaq-100 fast-entry ranking date under the index methodologyConfirms or delays passive demand
Dec 9Federal Reserve decision, with markets pricing a hikeHigher rates pressure long-duration growth stocks
About Dec 14Underwriter quiet period ends; syndicate analysts can initiateBullish initiations are customary, but not guaranteed
Dec 15First scheduled lockup step, up to 303 million sharesThe largest single supply event of the year
Dec 18 to 21Triple witching, then Nasdaq-100 inclusion at the Dec 21 openIndex buying, likely partly front-run





The options launch deserves attention first. Listed options and leveraged ETFs bring hedging flows that can turn a slow drift into a fast move. If puts dominate early, dealers hedging those positions may sell into weakness. If calls dominate, the reverse can trigger a squeeze.
After that, the quiet-period expiry is the strongest potential support. Syndicate banks rarely initiate with Sell ratings on their own deals. 
Still, several independent firms have already published views, ranging from a Morningstar fair value near $92 to Buy targets of $150 to $155 from Needham and Melius.
Is ANT Cheap At $83? The Valuation Check
The business case remains extraordinary. According to the amended S-1, Anthropic generated $16.96 billion of revenue in the third quarter of 2026, up 1,127% from a year earlier and 47% from the second quarter. Trailing 12-month revenue stands near $35.3 billion.
However, the margin picture moved the wrong way. Anthropic swung from a $974 million operating profit in Q2 to a $567 million operating loss in Q3. 
Compute and infrastructure costs rose to 58% of revenue from 48%, partly because the company bought pricier short-term capacity. It also carries roughly $895 billion of compute and infrastructure commitments.

Valuation lens (at about $83 to $84)Multiple

Trailing 12-month sales, basic share count (about $1.1 trillion market cap)About 31x
Q3 revenue annualized ($67.8 billion), fully diluted value near $1.5 trillionAbout 22x
Consensus 2027 revenue near $128 billion, fully dilutedAbout 12x





So the answer depends on the time frame. On trailing numbers, ANT is priced like a scarce asset. On 2027 estimates, the multiple compresses quickly, provided growth holds and margins recover. That proviso is exactly what a market in correction is now questioning.
The competitive read-through also cuts both ways. Michael Burry recently argued that Anthropic is taking enterprise share from Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR). Yet that same disruption story raised the bar Anthropic must clear every quarter.
ANT Technical Levels And 3 Scenarios To Dec 21
Two sessions of data cannot support moving averages, RSI, or MACD. Those indicators need weeks of history. Instead, the reliable levels come from the IPO itself and from a Fibonacci retracement of the $83 to $115.10 range.

LevelPriceWhy it matters

Day-1 high$115.10The top of the debut; heavy trapped supply
Fib 38.2%$102.84First retracement target on any squeeze
Fib 50%$99.05Midpoint of the IPO range

  • Underwriters fully exercised their option on 147 million extra shares, so the overallotment short that normally funds a price-support bid is already closed.

  • SpaceX, the last mega-IPO, first closed below its IPO price 5 weeks after listing and bottomed 22% lower before recovering.

Anthropic PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) is trading within cents of its $83 IPO price after one of the fastest reversals ever seen in a mega-listing.

The stock opened at $111.50 on Nov 19 and hit $115.10 intraday. It then closed at $97.17, up 17% on the day. On Friday, however, the selling resumed. Shares opened at $89.86 and fell to a low of $83.15. That is a 27% drop from the high in under 2 trading days.

The timing made it worse. The S&P 500 and the Dow both entered correction territory on Friday, and the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for 2026. As a result, the largest IPO on record is now trading as a high-beta proxy for the whole AI trade.

Most coverage now treats $83 as “support” simply because it is the IPO price. That assumption deserves a closer look. The deal mechanics suggest the usual safety net is already gone.

How The Greenshoe Removed The Bodyguard

In a typical IPO, underwriters sell more shares than the base deal. Anthropic’s base offering was 980 million shares, and the pricing release granted the banks a 30-day option on 147 million more. That extra 15% creates a short position for the syndicate.

The short then becomes a tool. If the stock trades below the offer price, underwriters buy shares in the open market to cover it. 

That buying is the familiar “stabilization bid,” and it is permitted under SEC Regulation M, Rule 104. If the stock trades above the offer, the banks simply exercise the option and buy the extra shares from the company at $83.

Anthropic’s closing announcement confirmed the second path. The deal closed at 1.127 billion shares, including full exercise of the 147 million-share option. Gross IPO proceeds reached about $93.5 billion, or about $119.5 billion including a concurrent $26 billion private placement.

That detail matters for anyone treating $83 as a floor. Full exercise means the syndicate covered its short through the option. 

Consequently, there is no remaining short position that obliges the banks to buy shares on a dip. Stabilization is still legally possible during the window, but the economic reason to do it is gone.

In plain terms, $83 is now a psychological level, not a defended one.

The Float Math Works Against A Quick Bounce

Anthropic sold 1.127 billion shares against roughly 13.1 billion shares outstanding. That puts the IPO float near 8.6%. Under the registration filings on SEC EDGAR, non-founder employees could also sell up to 10% of their holdings from day one, about 315 million shares. 

Together, roughly 1.44 billion shares, or about 11% of the company, can trade today. A small float usually supports a new issue. 

Here, though, turnover was extreme. More than 846 million shares changed hands on day one, equal to about 75% of the entire IPO. In other words, much of the first-day buying came from fast money, and fast money leaves fast.

The supply calendar is also front-loaded. The staggered lockup in the S-1/A releases up to 303 million shares on Dec 15, another 303 million on Jan 5, 353 million on Jan 19, and 353 million on Feb 2. The Dec 15 step alone is worth about $25.1 billion at $83.

By comparison, Bloomberg Intelligence estimates about $4.6 billion of buying from Nasdaq-100 trackers under the index’s fast-entry rule. 

Broader estimates of first-month passive demand run near $19 billion. Either way, potential supply on a single unlock date exceeds the best-known source of mechanical demand.

What Happened To Mega-IPOs That Broke Issue

History offers three useful templates.

SpaceX (2026). SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) priced at $135 in June, closed day one at $161 and hit $225.64 intraday on June 16. It joined the Nasdaq-100 on July 7, yet the index buying did not stop the slide. The stock first closed below its IPO price on July 16 at $131.11 and bottomed at $104.83 on Aug 3, about 22% under issue. It then recovered after its first lockup expiry and closed at $162.57 on Oct 9.

Meta Platforms (2012). Facebook priced at $38, closed its first session at $38.23 and broke issue on day 2. It went on to bottom near $17.55 in September 2012, more than 50% below the offer, before becoming one of the best-performing large caps of the following decade.

Uber Technologies (2019). Uber priced at $45 and closed its first day at $41.57, below issue from the start.

The pattern is consistent. Breaking the IPO price says more about positioning and supply than about the business. Even so, the drawdowns that follow can be deep. Notably, SpaceX’s slide happened after index inclusion, which suggests passive demand gets priced in early.

Where The Real Floors Are

If the IPO price is not defended, then the next 4 weeks of share flows matter more than the $83 line. Six dated events stand out.

The options launch deserves attention first. Listed options and leveraged ETFs bring hedging flows that can turn a slow drift into a fast move. If puts dominate early, dealers hedging those positions may sell into weakness. If calls dominate, the reverse can trigger a squeeze.

After that, the quiet-period expiry is the strongest potential support. Syndicate banks rarely initiate with Sell ratings on their own deals. 

Still, several independent firms have already published views, ranging from a Morningstar fair value near $92 to Buy targets of $150 to $155 from Needham and Melius.

Is ANT Cheap At $83? The Valuation Check

The business case remains extraordinary. According to the amended S-1, Anthropic generated $16.96 billion of revenue in the third quarter of 2026, up 1,127% from a year earlier and 47% from the second quarter. Trailing 12-month revenue stands near $35.3 billion.

However, the margin picture moved the wrong way. Anthropic swung from a $974 million operating profit in Q2 to a $567 million operating loss in Q3. 

Compute and infrastructure costs rose to 58% of revenue from 48%, partly because the company bought pricier short-term capacity. It also carries roughly $895 billion of compute and infrastructure commitments.

So the answer depends on the time frame. On trailing numbers, ANT is priced like a scarce asset. On 2027 estimates, the multiple compresses quickly, provided growth holds and margins recover. That proviso is exactly what a market in correction is now questioning.

The competitive read-through also cuts both ways. Michael Burry recently argued that Anthropic is taking enterprise share from Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR). Yet that same disruption story raised the bar Anthropic must clear every quarter.

ANT Technical Levels And 3 Scenarios To Dec 21

Two sessions of data cannot support moving averages, RSI, or MACD. Those indicators need weeks of history. Instead, the reliable levels come from the IPO itself and from a Fibonacci retracement of the $83 to $115.10 range.

title: Court blocks Army's planned explosive detonation near Iowa-Illinois border
description:
A red barn with a stone foundation stands next to a tall brick silo covered in ivy. Photo: Grace David / The Center Square
(The Center Square) – A planned detonation of 9,700 pounds of explosives in Iowa is on hold, according to media reports.
The Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals on Friday temporarily blocked an emergency permit that would have allowed the Army to detonate the explosives that could disperse lead into surrounding Iowa farmland.
A Purdue University professor says the public still hasn't seen the testing plans that will determine where the contamination goes or whether it poses health risks.
Andrew Whelton, a professor of civil, environmental and ecological engineering at Purdue University, told The Center Square questions remain about how the Army will monitor and address potential contamination following the controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown.
The Army plans to detonate about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an explosive compound primarily used in military munitions. The aging munitions have deteriorating exterior casings, raising concerns that moving them could trigger an accidental explosion.
Whelton says the explosion will release heat and pressure, causing the shells to detonate and dispersing lead into the surrounding environment.
"Lead is on the periodic table, and so the explosion simply disperses the lead," Whelton said.
Lead does not break down into another substance, making post-detonation monitoring particularly important, he said.
Whelton previously worked for the U.S. Army's public health command from 2002 to 2005, helping military units evaluate potential chemical exposures.
For about 15 years, he has also helped communities respond to chemical contamination following disasters, including the East Palestine, Ohio, train derailment.
He said protecting human life must remain the priority when evaluating the risks of moving or detonating unstable explosives.
"If moving that material could cause the loss of life and detonation of that material does not, and there's no other option, then that's how you would evaluate the risk," Whelton said.
He emphasized that he is not questioning the Army's decision to detonate the material because he does not have access to the information needed to evaluate the explosives safety risks.
Instead, Whelton's concerns center on what happens after the explosion.
He said he has not seen a publicly available plan explaining how officials will determine how much lead is released, where it travels and whether sampling methods will adequately identify potential health risks.
Whelton said the EPA's permit to the Army outlines requirements for soil sampling, wipe sampling and other testing procedures. However, he said residents, elected officials and researchers have not been given sufficient access to the details.
He said officials should make those plans public so property owners, business owners, farmers and independent researchers understand how potential contamination will be evaluated.
Whelton cited an Iowa Department of Agriculture estimate of about 50,000 horses, cattle and pigs in the area potentially affected by the contamination plume.
Lead entering livestock drinking water at sufficiently high concentrations could cause acute toxicity, he said.
The Iowa Department of Agriculture has advised farmers to clean animal watering containers, keep animals indoors and watch for potential health symptoms.
A Nov. 19 letter signed by Illinois Gov. J.B. Pritzker, U.S. Sens. Dick Durbin and Tammy Duckworth, U.S. Reps. Darin LaHood, Mary Miller and Eric Sorensen, and Iowa officials urged the Army and EPA to delay the planned detonation until safer alternatives could be explored.
The officials raised concerns about potential lead contamination in surrounding communities and farmland, particularly the risks to children and pregnant women.
The letter requested detailed information about the anticipated contamination plume, mitigation efforts, post-detonation monitoring and sampling, and alternative disposal procedures. It also raised concerns about communication between federal agencies and state and local officials.
Whelton said alternative disposal methods for hazardous waste can sometimes include chemical neutralization, which can make materials inert or less dangerous.
He also said open burning and open detonation have historically been used in military munitions disposal but are generally considered options of last resort.
However, he cautioned that attempting to handle or process unstable explosives could create additional risks to human life.
The Army, Department of Health and Human Services and EPA issued a joint statement Nov. 20 defending the operation, saying agencies have been planning for it since March.
"The entire interagency is working together to ensure that the controlled detonation in Middletown, Iowa is conducted in the safest fashion possible," the statement said.
Federal officials said they are prepared to take what they described as the most extreme mitigation measures available to protect the public and minimize disruptions.
Whelton said the central issue is whether those measures will adequately identify contamination and determine what steps are necessary if lead is discovered on nearby properties.
He said residents and business owners should not have to guess about the potential risks or how officials intend to address them.
His recommendation is for the Army to make its environmental testing plans publicly available so communities can understand how officials will determine whether their properties are safe following the detonation.
This article originally appeared on The Center Square at https://www.thecentersquare.com/illinois/article_11ef1e02-2851-4373-b684-7423c5dfad71.html

title: Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%
The bitcoin price slipped to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, briefly dipping under its summer low, as a chip-led selloff sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and dragged crypto stocks and miners sharply lower.
This post Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5% first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%

The bitcoin price slid to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, down about 6.2% over the past 24 hours, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a deepening selloff in chip and artificial intelligence stocks sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and pushed bitcoin just under its summer low.

Bitcoin broke below $60,000 late Friday morning, a few hours after this morning’s report had it near $61,500. Over the past 24 hours, the bitcoin price has traded between $57,655 and $62,562, a drop of about $3,880. Bitcoin is down about 25% in November, on pace for its worst month since June 2022.

Chip stocks drag Wall Street lower

Selling on Wall Street sped up through the afternoon. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% in late trading and the S&P 500 dropped about 3.5%. Yahoo Finance said the Nasdaq was on pace to close negative for the year, while the S&P 500 was poised to close in correction territory.

Chipmakers led the drop. Nvidia (NVDA) fell about 12.5% to near $128, and AMD, Broadcom and Micron also posted double-digit losses. Gold futures dropped nearly 5%. Treasury yields fell as traders rotated into bonds and defensive sectors such as consumer staples and healthcare, Reuters reported.

Anthropic (ANT) fell nearly 12% to around $86 on its first full day of trading, leaving it just above its $83 IPO price. The stock had closed its Thursday debut at $97.17 after raising $81.3 billion in the largest IPO of all time, CNBC reported.

Liquidations and outflows weigh on the bitcoin price

Leveraged traders were forced out as the bitcoin price broke support. About $1.53 billion in crypto bets were wiped out over 24 hours, with long positions making up $1.4 billion of that total. Bitcoin alone accounted for around $540 million, while ether fell more than 8% to around $1,600.

Bitcoin funds have been sellers, too. Investors have pulled roughly $3.5 billion from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs so far this month, including $582 million on Thursday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest one-day outflow on record.

Rate worries are adding pressure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a half-point Federal Reserve hike in December. Traders still saw a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point increase, and some strategists warned that further hikes could deepen the selloff.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop looks driven more by the AI stock selloff than by problems inside crypto. Bitcoin has increasingly traded alongside other growth assets that depend on easy money, he said.

The dip to $57,655 briefly took bitcoin just under its summer low near $57,700. It is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, its longest losing streak since 2022.

Crypto stocks extend losses

Strategy (MSTR) fell about 8.4% to near $78.90, adding to the losses after the stock fell for a sixth straight day on Thursday. Coinbase (COIN) dropped about 5.5% to near $103. Robinhood (HOOD) lost about 9.6% and Circle (CRCL) fell about 7.9%.

Bitcoin miners fared worst. MARA Holdings (MARA) sank about 17% to near $5.17, IREN (IREN) fell about 17% and CleanSpark (CLSK) dropped about 16%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) lost about 8.4%, and Galaxy Digital (GLXY) fell about 9.4%. Many miners have expanded into AI data centers, tying their shares to the chip selloff.

The bitcoin price is now down more than 50% from its record above $126,000, set in October 2025.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $58,300.

This post Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5% first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

fullContent:
Could 2027 finally be the year Cardano (ADA) overtakes Ripple (XRP) in the cryptocurrency rankings? Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta AI predicts that, despite XRP’s established position among the industry’s largest digital assets, network upgrades, renewed institutional interest, and a shift in investor sentiment could make it more likely than it first appears.

Both cryptocurrencies have spent years competing for attention, albeit with very different propositions. XRP has built its reputation around cross-border payments and financial infrastructure, while Cardano has focused on research-driven development, decentralized applications, and a carefully structured ecosystem.

However, market leadership can change quickly during a cryptocurrency bull market. If Cardano delivers on its ambitious development roadmap while XRP struggles to maintain its momentum, the gap between the two could narrow considerably.

And while flipping XRP would require an extraordinary rally, ADA could climb to a valuation few investors currently anticipate.

Meta AI Predicts Cardano’s 2027 Roadmap Could Be a Major Catalyst for the Flippening

One of Cardano’s biggest opportunities heading into 2027 is its ongoing push to improve network scalability.

The planned Ouroboros Leios upgrade is particularly important. Designed to increase transaction throughput without compromising Cardano’s decentralized architecture, Leios could address a longstanding criticism: its ability to compete with higher-throughput blockchain ecosystems.

Cardano’s Dijkstra development cycle also introduces further improvements, with Peras activation targeted for the second quarter of 2027. Peras is designed to improve transaction settlement speed by reducing the time needed to achieve stronger confirmation confidence.

Meanwhile, developments around programmable tokens, decentralized finance, and real-world asset tokenization could help Cardano attract applications that generate genuine demand for ADA.

These upgrades won’t automatically translate into higher token prices, but successful implementation could give investors a compelling reason to reconsider Cardano’s long-term valuation.

XRP has several advantages that Cardano cannot easily replicate. Ripple has spent years building relationships across the financial sector, while the XRP Ledger continues to expand into institutional decentralized finance, stablecoins, and tokenized real-world assets.

The network processed an average of approximately 2.48 million daily transactions during the first quarter of 2026, while its real-world asset market capitalization reached $2.25Bn. These are meaningful indicators of ecosystem activity.

However, XRP’s enormous market capitalization also creates a challenge for investors seeking outsized returns. With a much larger valuation than ADA, XRP needs substantially more capital inflows to achieve the same percentage gains.

Recent market comparisons have placed XRP’s valuation at roughly ten times Cardano’s, highlighting the scale of the challenge. If capital rotates toward smaller, established layer-1 networks during the next bull market, ADA could benefit disproportionately.

ADA previously reached an all-time high around $3.10 during the 2021 bull market, demonstrating that the cryptocurrency can attract substantial speculative demand when market conditions are favorable.

A sustained recovery towards its previous peak would be an important psychological milestone. However, a genuine breakout beyond that region would potentially open the door to a much larger valuation.

For XRP, the challenge is maintaining its market leadership while competing with an expanding range of payment-focused blockchain networks. Its established institutional presence provides a strong foundation, but continued adoption growth will be necessary to justify a substantially higher valuation.

A decisive break above previous cycle resistance, followed by a successful retest, could signal that a longer-term trend reversal is underway.

title: Semiconductor Stocks Heading for Worst 2-Month Slump Since 2001 as Nvidia, Anthropic and the AI Trade Crack: This Week on Wall Street
description:
Semiconductor stocks are closing out a two-month collapse with only one precedent, and it was written in the autumn of 2001.
The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SOXX) fell 10% on Friday alone and is down 34.5% since Sept. 30. In 25 years of trading, the only worse two-month stretch ended in September 2001, at 35.1%, when the dot-com bust met the Sept. 11 attacks. The worst two months of 2008 took 33.2%.
Chart: iShares Semiconductor ETF two-month rate of change since 2001. Source: TradingView




For the fifth week in six, the AI trade lost ground, and this time the blow came from Washington.
A Friday That Belongs in the Record Books
Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) fell 13% on Friday to $127, its lowest since May 2025 and 48% below its Oct. 6 record. The week’s 22% loss is its seventh straight weekly decline, the longest run since July 2008, and November’s 38% drop is its worst month since that same July. Roughly $1 trillion of market value vanished this week alone, and about $3.2 trillion since the peak.
SanDisk Corp. (NASDAQ:SNDK) dropped 16%, Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) 14%, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) 12.7%, Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) 12.4% and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. (NYSE:TSM) 9%. For the week, SanDisk is down 28% and Micron 23%. The VIX jumped 20% to 34.
The S&P 500 Enters a Correction
The S&P 500 fell 3.2% on Friday to 6,949, its seventh straight loss. The streak has cost 8.7%, the deepest seven-session slide since February 2020. At 11% below its Oct. 6 record close, the index is in a correction for the first time since April 2025, down about 8% for the week and 8% for November, its worst month since September 2022.
The Nasdaq 100 fell 4.7% on Friday and 9.5% for the week, and turned negative for 2026, erasing a gain that stood at 24% six weeks ago. Its 17% drop since Sept. 30 is the steepest two-month decline since November 2008, and it sits within a point of a bear market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1.5% on Friday and 7.6% for the week.
Nothing offered shelter. Gold slid 3% to a 14-month low and Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) fell 5.6% to $58,400.
Washington Draws the Line at 16 Nanometers
Anthropic PBC (NASDAQ:ANT) raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO on record and opened at $111.50 on Thursday, 34% above its $83 offer price. By Friday it was back near $88. Nvidia beat estimates on Tuesday and guided to $130 billion in revenue. Investors sold anyway, because the story had moved from demand to permission.
A Commerce Department rule that took effect on Wednesday bars Chinese chip designers from buying 16-nanometer and more advanced chips without a license. Taiwan Semiconductor suspended orders from some Chinese customers, and Nvidia halted H200 shipments to China and removed the country from its forecast.
On Thursday, California Attorney General Rob Bonta served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena over former CEO Jensen Huang‘s China ties, and House Democrats opened a probe into whether the company tried to influence a federal investigation into chip smuggling.
President Donald Trump, back from meetings with Xi Jinping, took questions at the White House on Friday and drew the line himself. “We want only older chips,” he said of exports to China, adding that “in two years, Blackwell will be obsolete.”
He then turned to Huang. “He made some bad decisions, but he is a brilliant person,” Trump said, and compared him to Elon Musk: “I came to Elon’s defense in my first term very strong.” He “would love to see Jensen be given a second chance” after “a big apology.”
A Fed That Wants to ‘Shock People’
The Federal Reserve offered no cushion. Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC on Wednesday that inflation is “kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out,” and that to bring it down, “you might need to, like, shock people” with a half-point hike at the Federal Open Market Committee’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.
Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, long a dove, told reporters on Thursday, “I do not see that at this moment we are on path back to 2%.”
Treasuries drew safe-haven buying. The 10-year yield fell to 4.92% from 5.14% a week earlier, the 2-year to 4.62% from 4.85%, and the 30-year to 5.31% from 5.47%.
Michigan consumer sentiment rose to 51.5 in November from 48.0, with year-ahead inflation expectations down to 3.7% from 4.7%. Detroit did not share the relief: General Motors Co. (NYSE:GM) fell about 7% and Stellantis N.V. (NYSE:STLA) about 12% to a new low.
Dell, Then Thanksgiving
Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL), down 12% on Friday, reports its latest quarterly earnings Tuesday after the close, with consensus at $6.55 a share on $49.48 billion in revenue and options pricing a 15.7% move, according to Benzinga Pro data.
After September 2001, the semiconductor index needed more than 12 years to recover the ground it lost that summer. After this week, the question for Dell’s call is not how many AI servers customers ordered. It is how many of them Washington will let them ship.

title: Wells Fargo Led Wall Street’s Bitcoin Buying Spree in September as Institutional Holdings Hit a Record
description: The figures reflected holdings until the end of September. The market structure has shifted significantly since then.
fullContent:
The third quarter of 2026 marked a major shift in institutional demand for US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products, as investment managers returned to buying after three quarters of net selling.

According to Galaxy Research, 2,166 institutional managers reported holdings of 356,491 BTC-equivalent worth $29.78 billion as of September 30, a record level.

Big Institutions Loaded Up

Their net additions reached 49,229 BTC-equivalent, or roughly $4.11 billion, the largest quarterly increase since Q2 2025. The buying was led by major financial institutions. Wells Fargo added 14,636 BTC, followed by Brevan Howard, Bank of America, Millennium Management and Jane Street. The most notable development, however, was the continued rise of advisors and wealth management platforms, which added 24,838 BTC-equivalent during the quarter, accounting for roughly half of institutional net buying.

Their total holdings climbed to a record 144,307 BTC, representing 40.5% of all Bitcoin held by 13F-reporting managers, reflecting growing access to the crypto asset exposure through traditional investment channels.

The number of institutions reporting positions also increased by 191 to 2,166, and ended up reversing declines in the first half of the year. But much of the new participation came from relatively small positions.

Bitcoin exposure remained concentrated among a handful of large institutions. Galaxy found that the 25 biggest holders accounted for 60.8% of reported holdings and the 50 largest controlled 71.2%. Wells Fargo emerged as the largest holder, as it overtook Jane Street with 30,553 BTC-equivalent, while hedge funds continued to lose ground as a share of institutional ownership. Their combined share fell to 19%, down sharply from 50.6% at the end of 2024, while advisors and wealth platforms continued to expand their presence.

September Holdings, November Uncertainty

There are also differences in how institutions use Bitcoin ETPs, as positions held by wealth managers may represent client allocations, while hedge funds and market makers may use them as part of hedged trading strategies, Galaxy stated.

Despite the strong accumulation during the quarter, the figures reflect holdings as of September 30, which is well before BTC’s subsequent decline. By November 16, total Bitcoin held by the funds had fallen to 1.25 million from 1.29 million at quarter-end, leaving the market’s response to the downturn unclear until the next round of institutional filings.

title: Court halts Army plan to detonate nearly 10,000 pounds of explosives in Iowa
description:
A federal appeals court has temporarily blocked an emergency permit allowing the U.S. Army to conduct a controlled detonation of nearly five tons of lead azide at a military ammunitions plant in Iowa.
In an order filed late Thursday night, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals granted an administrative stay of the permit, issued by the Environmental Protection Agency, while the court considers an emergency request from two Iowa environmental groups to formally halt the detonation, which the Army postponed until early next week amid public concern.
Army postpones plan to detonate nearly 10,000 pounds of lead azide until Monday
The temporary stay pauses the emergency permit until the appeals court rules on the request from the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club Iowa Chapter for a longer-term halt.
The environmental groups asked the federal appeals court to halt the plan in an emergency motion filed earlier Thursday -- alleging that the EPA approved the permit for the detonations without adequately considering the potential health and environmental consequences or fully evaluating alternatives -- as some officials, including Iowa Sen.-elect Josh Turek and Gov.-elect Rob Sand, also expressed concerns about the Army's plan, how it was communicated to the public and risk of potential lead exposure.
Scott Olson/Getty Images - PHOTO: A sign identifying the facility sits inside a fence surrounding the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Nov. 19, 2026, in Middletown, Iowa. 
Two rapid, controlled detonations were initially scheduled to take place at the Middletown plant midday Friday to safely dispose of degraded lead azide, according to the U.S. Army.
Army officials announced Thursday that the detonation of nearly 10,000 pounds of lead azide would be pushed until Monday.
"Public communication is essential to public trust. Therefore, the Army will continue to actively engage with state and local officials throughout the region to distribute accurate, up-to-date information," Army Secretary Adam Telle said in a post on social media announcing the postponement.
Telle said Monday is the "latest possible moment prior to a forecasted temperature drop, which would risk further destabilization of the material."
Lead azide is the primary explosive used to initiate munitions. The controlled detonation is to dispose of degraded lead azide, which is highly sensitive and extremely unstable, the Army said. Due to the risks of accidental detonation in packing and transporting it, "safely destroying it in place is the only responsible option," the Army said.
According to the EPA, the "recrystallization of the stored lead azide has increased the material's sensitivity to friction and shock, and disturbing the containers of lead azide could create an unacceptable risk of unintentional detonation."
Man indicted by grand jury in connection with Peoria, Illinois bomb threat
The Department of Health and Human Services, the EPA and the Army said Friday the agencies are taking "extreme mitigation measures" to ensure the safety of the detonation, which the Army said will cause a dust plume containing some lead, loud noises and ground vibrations and possibly broken windows.
"The entire interagency is working together to ensure that the controlled detonation in Middletown, Iowa is conducted in the safest fashion possible," the agencies said in a joint statement released Friday.
The statement said officials had been preparing for the event since March and "agencies involved are prepared to take the most extreme mitigation measures available to ensure there is no risk to the public and any disruptions are minimized."
"The entire Trump administration will continue to engage with state and local officials, as well as the broader community, to keep all apprised of updates as they arise," the statement continued.
Scott Olson/Getty Images - PHOTO: A sign hangs from a fence at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Nov. 19, 2026, in Middletown, Iowa. 
In their emergency motion seeking to halt the detonation, the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club argued that the detonation could spread lead dust across a large area, potentially reaching communities more than 100 miles from the plant. The Army's latest modeling projects that lead dust could settle across an area approximately 25 miles long and 5 miles wide, including homes and waterways, according to the filing. The groups further argue that people, livestock and wildlife could also continue to face exposures to lead once it settles into the ground.
The filing also questioned the Army and EPA's handling of public notification, alleging that some of the potentially impacted communities were not given direct or timely notice.
When reached for comment on the emergency motion, the EPA referred ABC News to the joint statement released on Friday.
The Department of Justice said in a filing on Friday that it plans to file a response opposing the emergency motion by Sunday. The filing noted that the EPA permit authorized the Army to "conduct a controlled detonation of unstable and dangerous explosives -- lead azide waste -- upon EPA’s finding that the waste and other attendant circumstances pose an imminent and substantial endangerment to human health and the environment."
This article originally appeared on ABC News at https://abcnews.com/US/federal-appeals-court-temporarily-blocks-controlled-detonation-iowa/story?id=138321357

title: Bitcoin sinks below $60,000 as investors pull billions from crypto funds
description:
Bitcoin (BTC-USD) plunged below $59,000 on Friday, deepening a November sell-off that is shaping up to be the cryptocurrency's worst monthly decline in more than four years. 
Bitcoin fell as low as $57,957 in late Friday morning trading before recovering some of those losses to trade at $58,500 by the afternoon. At its current price, the digital coin is down more than 20% so far in November, putting it on pace for its worst monthly performance since June 2022, according to Yahoo Finance data. That would be  bitcoin's eighth-worst month since Yahoo Finance's daily records began tracking the digital asset in September 2014. 
The sell-off comes as chips and other tech stocks are tumbling on the heels of Anthropic's public debut, which investors largely viewed as the AI trade's "Super Bowl moment" for 2026. 


US spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds have also added to the selling pressure. So far this month, net investors have withdrawn roughly $3.5 billion, according to asset manager Farside Investors, which tracks the product flows. That includes $582 million in outflows on Thursday alone.
Thursday's monster Anthropic listing has also ushered some soul-searching among crypto's longtime believers. 
"I said back in May that most of the crypto industry was dead and it was never coming back. I believe that even more today," investor Anthony Pompliano said in a Friday post on X, where he remarked on the "enormous benefits" and " impressive revenue growth" of AI companies. 
(Reuters/Dado Ruvic/Illustration)
Reuters / REUTERS

Pompliano added that he views bitcoin, stablecoins, and certain infrastructure projects as exceptions that will inevitably stick around. 
"It is a sign of intelligence to change your mind, or evolve your thinking, when the facts change," Pompliano wrote. "I remain bullish on bitcoin, but there are a lot of ways up the mountain too." 
Along with intensifying competition from this year's biggest IPOs and the broader AI trade, which has prompted some bitcoin mining firms to sell their holdings at a faster pace, analysts have pointed to the toll that higher interest rates are taking on investor appetite for riskier assets.
Fundstrat digital asset strategist Sean Farrell said Thursday evening that crypto exchange Coinbase Global (COIN) continued to lead bitcoin selling. He added that while signs of a bottom were beginning to emerge, the selling pressure hasn't yet reached past levels for a compelling buying opportunity. (Disclosure: Yahoo Finance has a partnership with Coinbase.)
Follow David Hollerith on X @DsHollers.
This article originally appeared on Yahoo Finance at https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bitcoin-plunges-below-59000-on-pace-for-its-worst-month-since-june-2022-192922111.html
