title: Wall Street Had a Big Week. Why are AI and Tech Stocks Still Crashing?
description:
AI and tech stocks are crashing despite Anthropic's record IPO and Nvidia's beat. Here is what investors fear instead.
The post Wall Street Had a Big Week. Why are AI and Tech Stocks Still Crashing? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
AI and tech stocks kept falling on Friday, despite Anthropic’s record IPO and Nvidia’s earnings beat. Anthropic alone shed nearly $200 billion in market value from its first trade to Thursday’s close.

Investors had hoped the pair would revive the AI trade, but neither did. So, what is happening to the tech stock market?

Wall Street’s Big Week Couldn’t Lift Tech Stocks

Anthropic opened at $111.50, 34% above its $83 offer price, before dropping.

The IPO itself pulled cash from other stocks. Funds sold other holdings to pay for Anthropic orders, then got far fewer shares than they sought.

Of about 1,200 institutions that placed orders, more than half got no shares. Cramer expected that cash to flow back into other stocks. Instead, the S&P 500 fell 2% on Thursday.

Nvidia’s revenue beat Wall Street’s forecast by $6.5 billion. However, more than 90% of its revenue came from AI chips and servers sold to cloud companies.

That ties chipmakers to a handful of big spenders. In November, 52% of fund managers polled by Bank of America expected a cloud spending cut within six months.

Microsoft and Amazon, two major AI spenders, slipped 1.65% and 1.84% on Friday. Chip and data center names such as AMD, Micron and CoreWeave fell more than 4%.

China added a fresh scare. Short seller Hunterbrook alleged AMD software reached a blacklisted Chinese server maker, which AMD denies.

AMD closed down 7.72% on Thursday.

Interest rates are squeezing all of tech, not only AI. Federal Reserve meeting minutes pointed to more hikes, and traders now treat a December rate hike as nearly certain, CME data shows.

So why are AI and tech stocks falling?

  • Doubts that AI spending will last. In November, 52% of fund managers polled by Bank of America expected a major cloud company to cut AI spending within six months.
  • Big investors are leaving tech. Fund managers cut tech holdings at the fastest monthly pace since 2006, the same survey showed.
  • The Anthropic IPO drained cash. Funds sold other stocks to pay for orders, and more than half of about 1,200 institutions got no shares.
  • A rate hike looks likely. Traders treat a December Federal Reserve rate hike as nearly certain.
  • China risk is back. A short seller targeted AMD’s China ties, and Nvidia’s forecast assumes no AI chip sales to China.

Is This Panic or the Start of Something Worse?

Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co called the selloff panic, not a broken AI thesis.

“This is strong appetite for this major AI IPO in Anthropic, and it’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia,” he said.

Joachim Klement, a strategist at UK investment bank Panmure Liberum, disagrees. His team turned fully defensive after the S&P 500 broke below its 200-day average, a long-term trend line.

The damage is already serious. AI cloud provider CoreWeave sits 76% below its record high and Oracle 68%.

What Could Turn AI and Tech Stocks Around?

Much of the selling may already be done. Hedge funds have sold much of their net AI stock purchases made since early 2025.

History offers bulls some hope too. The S&P 500’s last six-day losing streak, in April 2024, ended the next session. A record rally followed 26 days later.

This streak has left S&P 500 index fund holders 8.2% below October’s record.

title: Large PEPE Holders Pull Their Tokens, and the Meme Coin Pays With a Near 12% Drop
description: Pepe fell nearly 12% after whales pulled large amounts of the token. Sellers control the chart, and support near $0.0000033 is the level traders now watch.
fullContent:
Large holders moved sizable amounts of Pepe out of their wallets this week, and the meme coin sank hard as other traders rushed to sell.

The move hit during a market-wide retreat, so PEPE now faces whale risk and weak sentiment at once. Traders want to know if this was a one-time flush or the start of a bigger exit.

Whale Withdrawals Trigger a Sharp PEPE Slide

Pepe (PEPE) fell nearly 12% after whales pulled the token from their wallets. On-chain data showed the withdrawals came first, and selling pressure built quickly once traders spotted the moves. Big transfers like these often unsettle meme coin markets, where a few wallets can hold a large share of supply.

The timing made the hit worse. The drop landed during a broad sell-off that dragged down most of the top 50 coins over seven days. Bitcoin lost 13.2% in that stretch, while Ether shed 11.8%.

PEPE fared far worse than both. The token now trades near $0.0000035, down about 6% in a day. Weekly losses reach roughly 23%, and the monthly loss is about 24%. Almost all of the monthly decline came in the last seven days, which shows how fast sentiment turned.

Both Sides of the Argument

Traders read the same withdrawals in two very different ways.

  • Bears: They see big holders heading for the exit. Tokens pulled from wallets can reach exchanges and add fresh supply, which keeps pressure on the price and hurts anyone who bought the recent bounce.
  • Bulls: They note that PEPE held above long-term support even after a large wallet moved its tokens. If that floor survives, buyers gain a clear level to defend and a reason to stay in.
  • Smaller holders: They are caught in the middle. A whale exit can trigger cascading sell orders, and retail wallets usually react last.
  • The broader market: PEPE's slide reflects more than whale activity, since the whole market fell. A market-wide recovery could lift the token whatever the big wallets do next.

Sellers Keep Control as $0.0000033 Comes Into View

Pepe (PEPE) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

The chart sides with the bears for now. PEPE trades below its 50-day average near $0.0000043. It also sits under its 200-day average near $0.0000040. Both lines now act as ceilings overhead. Trend strength readings show a real downtrend, and sellers are the ones driving it.

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits at 32. That puts PEPE close to oversold territory, where selling often starts to tire. Momentum still points down, though, so buyers have not yet shown up in force.

On the daily chart, the nearest support sits around $0.0000033. That is the floor the long-term support camp has to defend. A break below it would leave no clear level nearby. On the upside, first resistance waits near $0.0000038, and bulls need to reclaim it to signal a turn.

What Would End the Debate

Three signals will settle which camp is right.

  • A daily close below support: A session ending under that floor would hand the argument to the bears.
  • A reclaim of $0.0000041: A move back above that second resistance would suggest the whales flushed weak hands and may return.
  • Wallet flows: Fresh large withdrawals would add pressure. A pause would give buyers room.

title: Trump defends calling Putin a friend but won't say if he's a friend to the U.S.
description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump doubled down Friday on his description of Vladimir Putin as a friend but said he “can’t speak” to whether the Russian president is a friend to the U.S.
Trump also insisted during a White House news conference that Putin wants peace with Ukraine, despite Russia's continued aggression after invading more than four years ago. Asked about the most recent attacks — hours after Putin met with Trump in China — Trump suggested that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Putin share equal responsibility for the ongoing conflict. 
“He’d love to end the war,” the U.S. president said of his Russian counterpart. But “you have two guys that don’t know how to end it. We’re trying to help them. You have two people that hate each other, Zelenskyy and Putin. They don’t know how to end it. They want to end it. They’re both stuck in it.”
During a wide-ranging news conference, Trump praised both Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping after returning from China, where he participated in bilateral and trilateral meetings with his fellow heads of state. 
Trump raised eyebrows on the trip with his warm greeting of Putin and repeated references to him as his “friend.” He made no effort in the White House briefing room to walk back the comments. And he noticeably sidestepped a specific question about whether he views Putin as a friend to the United States. 
“I can’t speak to America,” Trump said, without expounding. 
He shifted immediately to his “very good” personal relationship with Putin and repeated longstanding grievances over the extended federal probe that concluded that Russian agents sought to influence U.S. voters in the 2016 presidential election on Trump’s behalf.
“I consider him to be somebody that I have a very good relationship (with),” Trump said. “It’s actually very good.”
“I’ve been dealing with Putin” since “the fake Russia, Russia, Russia hoax,” as Trump calls the Department of Justice investigation into the 2016 election. “It was a hoax made up by the Democrats” and “probably helped me win,” Trump said.
Trump praises relationship with Putin after major Russian attack on Ukraine
Trump spoke warmly of Putin just hours after Russia carried out a nighttime bombardment of Ukraine, killing at least eight civilians and wounding more than two dozen, Zelenskyy said. Russia fired more than 400 drones and over 110 missiles, 27 of them ballistic and some carrying cluster warheads that scatter dozens of smaller bomblets across a wide area, the Ukrainian president said.
Putin had vowed to retaliate for Ukrainian strikes this week that severely damaged the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with the Russian mainland, which is vital to Moscow’s war effort. The Russian attack fit the pattern of heavy responses to eye-catching Ukrainian attacks and added to uncertainty about the prospects for the talks brokered by Washington.
Meanwhile, two Russian missiles and a suspected drone also came down in Poland on Friday in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. There was no immediate comment from Moscow on the incursion or the drills.
Despite Moscow's latest aggression, Trump said Putin has expressed a desire to see the war between Russia and Ukraine end “by diplomatic means." Trump said “there's a real good chance” that a peace deal can be brokered. 
Russia rejects Kushner's claims of progress
U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said on Thursday that he believes Russia is “comfortable” with NATO-like security guarantees for postwar Ukraine. Ukraine has long sought entry into NATO, particularly for its common defense guarantee under the alliance’s Article 5, which holds that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all. 
“I think we’ve gotten the Russians comfortable with that concept where any security guarantee for Ukraine would be based on Article 5,” Kushner said. “And I think that that comes with at least what the Russians are saying, which is their intention is when this war is over to not have another war in the future.”
But Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said Friday that even a “quasi-membership” of NATO for Ukraine would be unacceptable, Russia's Interfax news agency reported. Ryabkov said: "We discuss security guarantees primarily in terms of ensuring the security of our own country, and that’s what we’re talking about." 
When a reporter noted Russia's pushback to Kushner's statements, Trump brushed it off, saying that Moscow was unlikely to publicly confirm details from ongoing negotiations. 
“It is also a public relations war. And we’ll say things and they’ll say things,” Trump said.
Trump said he didn’t want to talk about security guarantees for Ukraine “because we got to get a deal first.” He added that the U.S. will be involved when there is a deal. 
Rubio rejects criticism that Trump embraces autocratic leaders
Trump insisted his relationships with the other world leaders is key to an eventual peace.
“You know, you’re very lucky to have somebody that has a relationship with the heads of the most powerful countries,” he said.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who stood on stage during Trump's news conference and made brief remarks, echoed the president's sentiments, pushing back against criticisms that Trump was embracing autocratic leaders as trusted allies. 
“I want everybody to understand the relationships between heads of state are invaluable,” said Rubio, who traveled with Trump to Asia. “It sets the tone for the entire relationship. It sets the tone for our trade negotiators. It sets the tone for our diplomats.” __
Barrow reported from Atlanta. 
This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-defends-calling-putin-friend-182443750.html

title: Why Is Arista Networks Stock Plunging Friday?
description:
Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE:ANET) stock plunged about 10% on Friday as a broad technology sell-off weighed on AI infrastructure stocks amid mounting concerns over elevated valuations and heavy capital spending.
The decline came alongside sharp losses in semiconductor and technology shares, reflecting a broader retreat from AI-linked stocks.
The Nasdaq dropped 3.12%, the S&P 500 fell 1.56% and the Technology sector declined 4.65%.
       • Arista Networks stock is feeling bearish pressure. Why is ANET stock dropping?
Arista Networks, which provides networking solutions for AI data centers, cloud computing and enterprise environments, has benefited from accelerating infrastructure demand. However, concerns over the sustainability of AI spending and stretched valuations continue to pressure the sector.
At the end of the third quarter, Arista Networks reported purchase commitments of $11.4 billion, mostly representing purchases for chips related to new products and AI deployments.
During the earnings call, management anticipated strong demand in AI fabrics and campus networking, and provided a positive outlook on its AI-driven products, particularly the EtherLink portfolio and the autonomous virtual assistant, AVA.
Recent Results Highlights
On Nov. 3, Arista Networks reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, beating the $3.33 billion analyst estimate.
The company reported quarterly adjusted earnings of $1.20 per share, which beat the analyst estimate of $1.08.
The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $3.9 billion to $4 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.26 to $1.30, both exceeding Wall Street estimates.
Technical Analysis: Trading Below Short-Term Averages
From a longer-term trend view, ANET is still holding just above its 200-day SMA ($168.59), but it’s trading 6.5% below the 20-day SMA ($182.27) and 11.3% below the 50-day SMA ($192.06), which keeps the intermediate trend pointed lower.
The 20-day SMA is also below the 50-day SMA (a bearish crossover). That signals lingering short-term weakness.
Momentum has improved. The MACD is above its signal line, while the histogram is positive. Both indicators suggest buying momentum is strengthening.

Key Resistance: $191.00 — Round-number area that also lines up closely with the 50-day SMA/EMA zone.
Key Support: $158.50 — Nearby prior demand zone that sits below the 200-day trend area.
Analyst Outlook
The stock carries a Buy rating with an average price target of $233.38. Recent analyst moves include:

UBS: Maintained a Buy rating and raised its price target to $291 on Nov. 4.
JPMorgan: Maintained an Overweight rating and raised its price target to $270 on Nov. 4.
Piper Sandler: Maintained an Overweight rating and raised its price target to $261 on Nov. 4.
Benzinga Edge Rankings
Arista Networks scores highly for momentum, growth and quality on the Benzinga Edge Rankings.
Its Momentum score stands at 94.11, while Growth is 84.88 and Quality is 91.4. However, its Value score is just 7.61.
The combination reflects Arista’s strong price momentum and growth profile, alongside a valuation that leaves less room for disappointment.
ANET Price Action: Arista Networks shares were down 10.76% at $169.19 at the time of publication on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

title: Walmart Gets Bullish Rating Despite Pharmacy Deflation Headwinds
description:
Walmart Inc. (NASDAQ:WMT) shares are recovering on Friday after declining on Thursday following its third-quarter results.
It reported an adjusted EPS of 65 cents, exceeding analyst expectations of 64 cents. The figure excludes an after-tax loss of 3 cents per share related to equity and other investments.
Revenue rose 5.2% year over year to $188.835 billion, topping the consensus estimate of $187.271 billion.
However, Walmart’s weight-loss drug windfall is losing momentum despite rising prescription volumes.
Analyst Price Forecast Revisions
Several analysts raised their price forecasts following Walmart’s third-quarter results and increased guidance, while maintaining their existing ratings.
Morgan Stanley analyst Simeon Gutman maintained an Overweight rating and raised his price forecast to $135 from $125.
Piper Sandler analyst Peter Keith maintained an Overweight rating and increased his price forecast to $138 from $128.
TD Cowen analyst Max Rakhlenko maintained a Buy rating and raised his price forecast to $147 from $125.
Truist Securities analyst Scot Ciccarelli maintained a Buy rating and increased his price forecast to $134 from $114.
BTIG analyst Robert Drbul reiterated a Buy rating and maintained his $140 price forecast.
BTIG Analyst View
Drbul believes Walmart’s underlying U.S. business remains healthy, although Health & Wellness (H&W) is expected to weigh on reported comparable sales.
Walmart’s 2.9% U.S. comparable sales growth included an approximately 125-basis-point drag from Maximum Fair Price-related pharmacy deflation and brand-to-generic transfers, partly offset by a roughly 60-basis-point contribution from GLP-1 drugs.
Excluding H&W, comparable sales increased 3.6%, slightly accelerating from the second quarter of fiscal 2027 and improving on a two-year basis.
Looking ahead, the analyst expects healthy underlying demand but anticipates continued pressure on reported comparable sales from H&W.
MFP-related headwinds are expected to remain near current levels or increase slightly, while the contribution from GLP-1 drugs is likely to moderate.
However, improving H&W gross profit margins should help cushion the impact of weaker reported sales, according to the analyst.
Earnings Estimates And Outlook
Drbul maintained his fiscal 2027 EPS estimate at $2.90 but lowered his fourth-quarter Walmart U.S. comparable sales growth forecast to 2.9% from 3.1%. He expects comparable sales to increase 3.6% excluding H&W.
The analyst expects fiscal 2027 net sales of $748 billion, representing approximately 6% year-over-year growth, with operating income projected to grow faster than sales.
For fiscal 2028, Drbul raised his EPS estimate to $3.25 from $3.15.
WMT Price Action: Walmart shares were up 2.82% at $129.60 at the time of publication on Friday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

fullContent:
The past few weeks have been brutal for BTC, and quite frankly for the broader cryptocurrency sector, whose total market capitalization fell below $2.2 trillion, its lowest level since early summer.

title: Coinbase Eyes In-House US Prediction Markets by Mid-2027 After CFTC Clearinghouse Approval
description:
Coinbase is targeting the first half of 2027 to launch in-house event contracts in the US for retail and institutional customers, enabled by its new CFTC-approved clearinghouse.
The post Coinbase Eyes In-House US Prediction Markets by Mid-2027 After CFTC Clearinghouse Approval appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
Coinbase is preparing to launch its own prediction markets directly in the United States by the first half of 2027.

The company currently offers these event contracts through a partnership with Kalshi but says it plans to bring the offering in-house to gain greater control over product listings and capture more trading revenue.

Both retail and institutional customers are expected to have access once the service goes live.

This development is supported by recent regulatory progress including CFTC approval of Coinbase Clearing LLC as the first USDC-native derivatives clearing organization.

The approval completes Coinbase’s full stack of CFTC-regulated infrastructure including a futures commission merchant and designated contract market.

It enables direct creation and settlement of fully collateralized contracts with native USDC collateral and 24/7 settlement.

“Today’s CFTC approval completes Coinbase’s end-to-end derivatives infrastructure enabling us to bring more regulated derivatives products to market with native USDC collateral and 24/7 settlement.”

The company noted it will continue using partners for certain products such as margined derivatives and upcoming single stock perps.

The target timeline for the in-house launch is the first half of 2027.

title: Can You Cancel a Withdrawal at a Licensed Web3 Casino?
description: Can you cancel a withdrawal at a licensed Web3 casino? How pending withdrawals work, why Britain banned reverse withdrawals and what to check first.
fullContent:
Players often request a withdrawal and then want the money back in the game, a common moment at online casinos. Some platforms let players cancel a pending withdrawal and keep playing, while others lock the funds once the request goes in.

The difference matters more than it seems. Regulators have linked the option to reverse withdrawals with harm, and rules now vary widely between jurisdictions.

Here is how withdrawal cancellation works at licensed Web3 casinos, why some regulators have banned it and what players should check before requesting a payout.

Withdrawal Paths Compared

Platforms handle pending withdrawals in different ways, and the table outlines the common models.

Model

What happens after a request

Funds wait in a pending state and can return to the balance

Temptation to keep playing

Cleaner break from play

Direct on-chain

Pending window is short

Delays depend on the review

Britain banned the option outright. Its standard RTS 14B says operators must not give consumers the option to cancel a withdrawal request, effective from 31 October 2021.

Why Regulators Act on Reverse Withdrawals

Research and casework linked reverse withdrawals to risk for engaged and vulnerable gamblers. Players who see winnings waiting in a pending state may return them to play before the payout completes.

Offshore licences set their own rules, so players at Web3 casinos licensed outside Britain may find cancellation on offer. The withdrawal terms explain which model applies, and a guide to what withdrawal terms actually say covers the usual clauses.

Reviews and Holds

Some withdrawals pause for checks, which can tempt players to cancel and play on. Guidance on what triggers a check shows when reviews usually start.

Steps for a Clean Withdrawal

Decide on the amount before opening the cashier, confirm the network and address, and avoid browsing games while the request is pending. Players at risk can set deposit limits or self-exclude to support the decision.

Dexsport's Withdrawal Rules

Dexsport shows a separate Withdrawable figure in the wallet, and deposits become withdrawable after bets on the deposit amount at odds of 1.3 or above, or x2 in casino games. Dexsport's bonus terms state that a withdrawal cancels any active bonus, so confirm current terms before requesting one.

Withdrawals at Dexsport move across 26 networks with per-coin and per-network minimums, so confirm current options on the platform, and investigations can hold account operations for up to 14 business days. Dexapp LTD holds the platform's Anjouan licence.

Conclusion

Whether players can cancel a withdrawal depends on the casino and its licence. Britain banned reverse withdrawals in 2021 after linking them to gambling harm, while offshore licences set their own rules.

Players can protect themselves by deciding amounts in advance, avoiding games while a request is pending and using limits or self-exclusion when needed. Dexsport separates withdrawable funds in the wallet and states that a withdrawal cancels any active bonus.

Read the withdrawal terms before your first payout. Gambling law varies by country, so check yours, play only at legal age and remember that KYC or AML checks may apply.

title: Sent Crypto to a Sportsbook on the Wrong Network? What Happens Next
description: Sent crypto to a sportsbook on the wrong network? When recovery is possible, when funds may be lost and how to avoid the mistake on your next deposit.
fullContent:
USDT exists on more than a dozen blockchains, and sportsbooks list several of them at the cashier. Pick the wrong one when sending a deposit, and the funds may never appear in the betting balance.

Whether the bettor gets that money back depends on the networks involved, who controls the receiving address and the sportsbook's support process.

Here is what happens when crypto goes to a sportsbook on the wrong network, when recovery is possible and how to avoid the mistake in the first place.

Common Wrong-Network Scenarios

Outcomes vary by situation, and the table outlines the usual cases.

Scenario

Example

Usual outcome

Compatible address formats

USDT sent on BNB Smart Chain to an Ethereum deposit address

Funds remain at the address, recovery may be possible

Unsupported network

Token sent on a chain the sportsbook does not monitor

No automatic credit, support may help

Different address formats

Wallet blocks the send or the transfer fails

Usually no loss

Missing memo or tag

Deposit to a shared address without the required memo

Support must match the payment manually

Last verified: November 2026

Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and Polygon all use addresses starting with 0x, so wallets will send across them without warning. Whoever holds the private keys for an address can reach funds on any compatible network, which is why recovery depends on the platform.

Recovery Depends on Key Control

Sportsbooks that control their deposit address keys can, in principle, retrieve funds sent on a compatible network. Many treat recovery as a manual process that may fail, and some charge a fee.

Funds sent on an incompatible chain, or to an address whose keys the platform lacks, may be gone for good. Confirmed blockchain transactions are final.

Legacy Chains

Tether ended issuance and redemption of USDT on five legacy blockchains in 2025, including Omni Layer and EOS, which adds risk for anyone sending USDT on older networks.

Steps to Avoid the Mistake

Match the network in the wallet to the one shown at the sportsbook cashier, send a small test amount first and wait for it to clear before sending the rest. Check memo or tag fields on networks such as XRP and TON.

Network choice affects other coins as well, and a look at two DOGE networks shows why the chain matters.

Blank memo fields also strand many transfers.

Platforms with wide network support list more chains, which means more options to check at the cashier.

Dexsport's Cashier Networks

Dexsport supports 26 networks and more than 50 assets, with USDT on 15 routes and minimums set per coin and per network. Binance Pay is an exchange rail, so it uses an amount field and a handoff to Binance in place of a deposit address.

Players can review the full list at the Dexsport cashier before depositing, confirm current options on the platform and contact support about any transfer that does not appear. Dexapp LTD holds the platform's Anjouan licence.

Conclusion

Crypto sent to a sportsbook on the wrong network may end up at an address the platform does not monitor, and recovery depends on compatible formats, key control and the support process. Confirmed transfers are final, so prevention matters most.

Network checks, a small test amount and a look at memo fields prevent most losses. Dexsport lists 26 networks with per-network minimums, so checking the cashier before sending is essential.

Confirm the network and address before every deposit. Betting law varies by country, so check yours, bet only at legal age and remember that KYC or AML checks may apply.

title: Senate Approves Bill Banning Prediction Market Bets on War, Terrorism and Death
description:
The U.S. Senate passed the DEATH BETS Act to prohibit prediction markets from listing contracts on terrorism, assassination, war, military operations, or individual deaths.
The post Senate Approves Bill Banning Prediction Market Bets on War, Terrorism and Death appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
The U.S. Senate has approved legislation barring prediction markets from offering contracts tied to some of the most sensitive events.

The measure known as the Discouraging Exploitative Assassination, Tragedy, and Harm Betting in Event Trading Systems Act or DEATH BETS Act amends the Commodity Exchange Act to stop registered entities from listing or clearing such contracts.

It specifically prohibits agreements referencing terrorism, assassination, war, U.S. Armed Forces military operations, or similar activities.

The bill also bans contracts expected to resolve principally based on an individual’s death.

Senator Adam Schiff is highlighting the passage alongside Senator John Curtis.

“BREAKING: The Senate just passed my bill with @SenJohnCurtis to prohibit prediction markets from listing contracts involving terrorism, assassination, war, military operations, or an individual’s death. With this bill, Congress is making it clear that these bets should be illegal.”

The legislation includes a rule of construction preserving other permitted activities under existing law.

It was introduced on March 10, 2026, and passed the Senate with an amendment by voice vote on November 19, 2026.

The action targets event contracts on prediction platforms while leaving other trading unaffected.

title: ADA Pullback Likely to Trigger a Breakdown to $0.11 as Midnight's NIGHT Draws the Bids
description: Cardano lost its June floor near $0.144 while Midnight's NIGHT token draws fresh money. ADA is oversold, but $0.12 is the last mapped support before $0.11.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Cardano has lost its June floor while Midnight's NIGHT token keeps drawing fresh money away from ADA.
  • Momentum indicators flash oversold, yet sellers still control a trend that shows no sign of fatigue.
  • Traders are watching one last mapped shelf near $0.12, with no clear support beneath it.

Cardano broke below its summer low this week as sellers extended a steep autumn slide. Capital keeps rotating toward Bitcoin and toward Midnight, a sister chain whose token design adds no direct demand for ADA.

That leaves ADA short of buyers just as its chart turns fragile. Traders now watch whether a deeply oversold reading sparks a relief bounce or the selling pushes the coin below its final floor.

Midnight Rallies While Cardano Slides to Its Summer Floor

The token now trades roughly 95% below its all-time high of $3.09, set in September 2021. It has also lost about 54% since January, when it changed hands near $0.33.

Sellers drove ADA down to the one-year low of $0.144 from June 28. That level had held for months, and buyers have so far failed to defend it.

Money is flowing elsewhere within Cardano's own family. Midnight, a privacy chain built on Cardano technology, launched on March 30, 2026. Its fees are paid in DUST, which users generate by holding the NIGHT token. That design means Midnight's growth creates no direct demand for ADA.

The split showed in October. NIGHT rose 40% over 30 days, while ADA fell nearly 18%.

Bitcoin keeps pulling capital away too. Its market dominance stood at 59.5% in late October, a sign investors still favor BTC over altcoins.

Both Moving Averages Now Sit Overhead as the June Low Gives Way

Cardano (ADA) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

ADA now trades near $0.14, below the June floor. The token lost about 8% in the past 24 hours alone. That move turned a test of support into a clean break.

The weekly picture looks worse. ADA has shed roughly 20% over seven days, a steep drop for a top-20 coin.

October's recovery attempt has now vanished. ADA peaked near $0.225 on Oct 21, then slid steadily for the rest of the month. The past 30 days show a loss of about 37%, wiping out the entire bounce and then some.

Both key moving averages now sit above the price. A moving average smooths daily prices to show the underlying trend. The 50-day average stands near $0.19, which means recent buyers are mostly holding losses. Many of them may sell into any rally back toward that line.

The longer view offers no comfort. The 200-day average sits near $0.22, which puts the long-term trend firmly against ADA. When price trades under both lines, traders read it as a confirmed downtrend.

That 50-day average now works as a ceiling. ADA would need a rally of more than a third just to touch it.

Oversold Yet Still Sinking

The daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, has dropped to about 25. Readings below 30 count as oversold, meaning sellers have pushed price down faster than usual. Such stretched readings often spark short relief bounces as late sellers run out of supply.

An oversold reading does not mark a bottom on its own. In strong downtrends, RSI can stay pinned in that zone for days or even weeks. Price can keep falling the whole time.

Other gauges show no sign of seller fatigue yet. The MACD, a tool that tracks shifts in momentum, still sits below its signal line. That means downward momentum has not started to fade.

Trend strength readings confirm a real trend, and sellers are driving it. Until that balance shifts, any bounce from oversold levels looks more like a pause than a turn.

Why $0.12 Is the Last Shelf Before Open Air

The nearest support on the daily chart sits near $0.12. It is the only mapped floor left under the price.

If ADA closes under that shelf, buyers have no obvious line to defend. Price could slide toward $0.11 before anyone steps in with size.

Resistance tells the other half of the story. The first ceiling sits near $0.18. A close above it would be the first real sign that buyers are returning. The next barrier waits near $0.20, just under the 50-day line.

Even those gains would only repair recent damage. Analysts who track the coin point to the $0.27 high from Oct 5 as the level that matters. That threshold sits nearly double the current price, so a real recovery remains distant.

Two Paths for the Next Three Days

ADA's next move hinges on which side of its narrow range breaks first.

  • Bullish: An oversold bounce that reclaims the first ceiling on a daily close would put $0.20 in reach. A slide back below $0.14 would cancel this setup and hand control back to sellers.
  • Bearish: A close under the last shelf would open a move toward $0.11. A recovery above the first ceiling would invalidate this view.

Sellers Hold the Wheel Until $0.18 Breaks

The trend still favors sellers. With both averages overhead and momentum pointing lower, the likelier path runs down to the last mapped shelf, and possibly through it.

Late shorts face real risk, though. Deeply oversold coins can snap higher without warning. A sharp squeeze could punish anyone selling into the hole, at least until that first ceiling gives way.

CoreWeave Briefly Trades Below $40 IPO Price Amid Financing Worries
description:
CoreWeave stock briefly fell below its $40 IPO price as a rising interest bill outweighed 168% revenue growth.
The post CoreWeave Briefly Trades Below $40 IPO Price Amid Financing Worries appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Anyone who bought CoreWeave (CRWV) at its $40 IPO price was briefly underwater on Friday. The AI cloud company’s shares slipped to $39.96, as worries over its debt returned.

The drop came despite what the company called record third-quarter revenue. CoreWeave, which rents Nvidia chips to AI developers, grew sales 168%. Yet the stock has lost nearly 79% since peaking at $187 in June 2025.

Why Is CoreWeave Stock Back at Its IPO Price?

Shares fell almost 10% to an intra-day low of $39.96 on Friday morning, slightly below the $40 level set in CoreWeave’s March 2025 offering.

The pressure is coming from the balance sheet. CoreWeave borrows heavily to buy chips and build data centers. Its debt stood at roughly $47 billion at the end of September.

That debt is getting more expensive to carry. Net interest expense reached $846 million in the third quarter, roughly 23% of revenue. The company expects $1.05 billion to $1.15 billion in the fourth quarter.

Those costs drove a $709 million quarterly loss, up from $110 million a year earlier.

Co-founder Brian Venturo said this week he bought $30 million of CoreWeave’s bonds. However, the three co-founders have sold about $3.3 billion of stock since the IPO. Those sales overshadowed the bond purchase.

Can Demand Outrun CoreWeave’s Interest Bill?

The business itself keeps growing. CoreWeave’s backlog, meaning revenue already signed under contract, reached $132.5 billion at the end of September. It also lifted its 2026 sales forecast to between $13 billion and $13.3 billion.

On the Nov. 10 earnings call, CEO Michael Intrator ruled out unsecured debt at current yields. Unsecured debt is borrowing not backed by specific assets. Instead, the company expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits within three months.

The stock rallied nearly 25% the next day. Those gains have since vanished.

Truist reiterated a Buy rating and a $115 target on Nov. 19. DA Davidson cut its target to $45 from $100.

The selling also hit other neoclouds, the companies that rent out AI computing power. Nebius and IREN fell roughly 10% and 11% in Friday morning trading.

Meanwhile, investor Michael Burry said this week that he had warned about Nvidia, CoreWeave and Nebius. He is holding bearish options positions.

title: A Technical Guide to Mitigate Java4Shell with TruRisk Eliminate
description: Executive Summary Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a heap out-of-bounds write in HotSpot’s AVX-512 Base64 decoder on x86-64. Calif reported it and showed pre-auth RCE in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate. Nobody has reported exploitation in the wild as of November 17, 2026. CISA issued an alert that same day, urging everyone to patch now. […]
fullContent:
Executive Summary

Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a heap out-of-bounds write in HotSpot’s AVX-512 Base64 decoder on x86-64. Calif reported it and showed pre-auth RCE in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate. Nobody has reported exploitation in the wild as of November 17, 2026. CISA issued an alert that same day, urging everyone to patch now.

Your Java4Shell Response Plan 

  • Patch to Oracle 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, or 27.0.1.1, or to your vendor’s build with JDK-8393212. 
  • If you can’t patch today, start the JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics and restart it. 
  • You’re only exposed on an x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 VBMI. ARM64 isn’t affected. 

Tip for Qualys customers: you can apply the step 2 flag with TruRisk Eliminate, targeting only the hosts that need it and rolling it back in one click. 

Affected Java Builds and Their Fixed Releases

Oracle shipped the fixed builds on November 17, 2026. October’s builds are still vulnerable. 

Distro packages built before the fix are vulnerable even when the version looks current. Ubuntu’s 17.0.21.0.3 and Oracle Linux’s 17.0.21 are two examples. 

How the Java4Shell Attack Chain Works

This is a typical Java4Shell attack chain:

  1. The attacker needs a Base64 decode value they can control. Vulnerability discoverers were able to reach this pre-authentication condition via authentication in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, and after login in Kafka, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit and Spinnaker. A Java client that opens a TLS connection to a malicious server is exposed too. 
  2. The attacker then sends valid decodes until the server compiler compiles the fast path, then the bad input: 64 valid characters and one =, or 128 and one = on older 17 builds. 
  3. The target must pass the gates in the source. The JVM must see avx512_vbmi and avx512bw with UseAVX=3, the intrinsic must be on, and on 17u the input must be longer than 128 characters. 
  4. The stub’s tail handling goes wrong. The next section walks through it. 
  5. On a fixed build, or with the intrinsic off, nothing happens. Otherwise, 62 or 63 bytes land past the destination array on the Java heap. 
  6. Vulnerability researchers mentioned that they groomed the heap (G1 regions, thread-local allocation buffers) to turn that write into code execution. Unsuccessful exploitation will lead to a denial-of-service condition on the endpoint. 

This remote code execution chain has only been mentioned as achieved by the vulnerability researchers. Nobody has reported it in the wild yet. 

Tracing Java4Shell to Its Root Cause

Based on the jdk17u source at the fix commit, HotSpot generates the stub in generate_base64_decodeBlock (it shows up as implDecode at runtime), and C2 calls it from java.util.Base64$Decoder.decode0 once that method is hot. JDK-8268276 added the AVX-512 decoder in JDK 18 and JDK-8296735 backported it to 17.0.6, so 17.0.5 and older are clean. 

The whole vector decoder sits inside if (VM_Version::supports_avx512_vbmi() && VM_Version::supports_avx512bw()). Without both features HotSpot only builds the scalar 4-character loop, which is fine. 17u has no AVX2 decoder; the AVX2 tables in that file are for encoding. MIME input goes straight to the scalar loop. Basic and URL input take the vector path once it’s longer than 128 characters. 

The vector code decodes 64 characters a pass, and L_finalBit handles the last 1 to 63. Before the fix, a tail of 1 to 3 characters ending in = gave an output size of 0, and the padding step subtracted 1 from it. The output mask then came from bzhiq with an index of -1. bzhiq only reads the low 8 bits of the index, so -1 became 255, nothing got cleared and the mask stayed all ones. The final masked store wrote a full 64 bytes where it should have written none.  

The exact trigger condition on 17u follows from the control flow. The input must be longer than 128 characters and go through the basic or URL decoder, since MIME goes to the scalar loop. Inputs of 256 characters or more run through 256-character passes, then everything runs through 64-character passes, so the tail left at L_finalBit is the length modulo 64. Every character in those passes must be valid Base64; a = or any other bad character inside a pass makes the stub exit early and hand the rest to Java. The tail must be 1 to 3 characters ending in =, and any non-padding character in it must also be valid. Put together, the bad lengths are 64k + 1 to 64k + 3 for k of 2 or more: 129 to 131, 193 to 195, 257 to 259 and so on. Legitimate padded Base64 always has a length that’s a multiple of 4, so none of these inputs is valid anyway. Unpadded values such as JWT segments can have other lengths, but they never end in =. That makes length modulo 64 plus a trailing = a tighter hunting signal than “not a multiple of 4”. 

The fix, JDK-8393212, adds four lines at L_finalBit: if fewer than 4 characters remain, jump to L_bruteForce, the scalar path. The commit title is “Base64 optimization improvements”, which tells you nothing. 

The fix closes the underflow and causes no other change. The new check runs before the stub computes either the input mask or the output size. With 4 or more characters left, the output size starts at (length / 4) × 3, which is at least 3. Padding takes off at most 2, so the size stays at 1 or more and bzhiq always gets a valid index. A tail made only of = fails the validity check and drops to the scalar loop. Tails of 1 to 3 characters never reach the vector code at all. I checked memory safety only. I didn’t check whether the stub decodes every odd-length tail of 4 to 63 characters correctly, and the fix doesn’t touch that logic. 

No CWE is assigned yet. I’d file it as an integer underflow (CWE-191) that causes an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). Windows x64 gets the same vector code; the function only differs in how it reads its arguments there. I’ve only read the 17u source. Calif’s shorter trigger on newer lines suggests a lower threshold than 128 characters there, but I haven’t confirmed it. 

Confirm Exposure From Inside the Java Runtime 

A JVM is exposed only when all four of these conditions are true: 

  1. It runs on an x86-64 CPU with avx512f, avx512bw, avx512vbmi and bmi2. That covers Intel Ice Lake, Sapphire, Emerald and Granite Rapids, and AMD Zen 4 and newer. Skylake-SP and Cascade Lake have AVX-512 but no VBMI. 
  2. It’s OpenJDK 17.0.6 or later, or 18 to 27, below the fixed builds. Oracle’s 8u511 Enterprise Performance Pack counts too, because it ships a 17-based VM. 
  3. UseAVX=3 and UseBASE64Intrinsics=true, which are the defaults on those CPUs. 
  4. Attacker input reaches the basic or URL decoder in java.util.Base64. Basic auth and JWT parsing do this before login. 

A quiet service isn’t safe. The attacker warms up C2 with valid decodes first. 

The OS doesn’t change the bug. Windows x64 gets the same generated code as Linux, though only Linux has public testing. 

I wouldn’t rely on /proc/cpuinfo. It doesn’t exist outside Linux, and an empty result looks like “not affected”. Ask the JVM what it sees instead, on any OS: 
java -Xlog:os+cpu -version 2>&1 | grep -oE ‘avx512f|avx512bw|avx512_vbmi|bmi2’ | sort -u 
java -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal -version 2>/dev/null | grep -E ‘ (UseAVX|UseBASE64Intrinsics) ‘ 

All four flags, UseAVX = 3 and UseBASE64Intrinsics = true mean that runtime is exposed. Run the check with each java binary on the host, since each runtime reports its own settings. 

Turn the intrinsic off with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics and restart the JVM. With that flag HotSpot never generates the stub, which I confirmed in the source and on a live JVM. Oracle hasn’t published it as a workaround. 

Skip -XX:DisableIntrinsic=_base64_decodeBlock. Upwind reports it fails unless you also pass -XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions. 

CISA’s alert also suggests validating Base64 at the application boundary, enforcing input-size limits and limiting unauthenticated access. Boundary validation helps if it rejects padded input whose length isn’t a multiple of 4 before the decoder runs. Size limits won’t: the trigger is 65 characters on newer lines, shorter than most Basic-auth and JWT values. Limiting unauthenticated access works, but it means network ACLs or a VPN in front, because the vulnerable decode happens before login.  

Mitigate Java4Shell with TruRisk Eliminate 

For Qualys customers, the Java4Shell mitigation is available now with TruRisk Eliminate on Linux and Windows hosts, linked to QIDs such as 389494. As additional QIDs are released for different operating systems, we will test them and add support. The Cloud Agent runs it on the hosts you pick. Before it changes anything, it checks that the host has an AVX-512 VBMI CPU and an affected Java runtime, so hosts that can’t hit the bug are left alone. On the hosts that can, it adds -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics to JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS and keeps whatever value was already there. 

The setting takes effect when each JVM restarts, so plan restarts with the application owners. Windows services pick it up after a host reboot. After the change, the agent reports every running Java process with its effective setting, worked out in the order HotSpot applies options. A JVM it can’t read shows up as unknown, so you know where to look instead of assuming it’s covered. 

Rollback is one click in the console and restores the previous value. The mitigation doesn’t reach containers; set the flag in the image or pod spec for those. Treat it as a bridge to the patched builds, since Oracle hasn’t published the flag as a workaround. 

Code execution is not the only outcome. A successful exploit chain can read Java heap memory before it runs any attacker code. That memory can hold private keys, tokens, and personal data. CISA also warns that crafted input can crash the JVM, so availability is at risk too. Java clients are exposed as well. The researchers report a client-side exploit in which a Java program is compromised simply by connecting over TLS to a malicious server.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

What is Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)?
Java4Shell is a heap out-of-bounds write in the AVX-512 Base64 decoder of the HotSpot JVM on x86-64. A malformed Base64 value can make the decoder write 62 or 63 bytes past the end of an array on the Java heap. Researchers turned that into pre-authentication remote code execution in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate.

Which Java versions are affected by Java4Shell?
OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later, and versions 18 to 27, are affected below the fixed builds. Oracle’s 8u511 Enterprise Performance Pack is also affected because it uses a 17-based VM. Oracle released the fixed builds on November 17, 2026: 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1 and 8u513-perf. Vendor builds that include fix JDK-8393212 are also safe. Java 8 standard and Java 11 are not affected.

Is Java4Shell being exploited in the wild?
No exploitation in the wild had been reported as of November 17, 2026. Remote code execution has only been demonstrated by researchers. CISA issued an alert the same day urging organizations to patch now.

How do I know if my Java runtime is exposed to Java4Shell?
A Java runtime is exposed only when all four conditions are true. It runs on an x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 VBMI. It’s an affected version. UseAVX=3 and UseBASE64Intrinsics are on, which are the defaults on those CPUs. And attacker input reaches the Basic or URL Base64 decoder. Check by asking each Java binary what it sees, not by reading /proc/cpuinfo. ARM64 is not affected.

How can I close the Java4Shell vulnerability if I can’t patch yet?
You can mitigate it by starting the JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics and restarting it. With this flag, HotSpot never generates the vulnerable code. Oracle hasn’t published it as an official workaround, so treat it as a bridge until you can patch.

How do I mitigate Java4Shell with TruRisk Eliminate?
Apply -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics with TruRisk Eliminate through the Qualys Cloud Agent. It automatically targets only Linux and Windows hosts that have an AVX-512 VBMI CPU and an affected Java runtime. It keeps existing JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS values, reports the effective setting for every running Java process and offers one-click rollback.

title: Coinbase Eyes 2027 Launch for In-House Prediction Markets as Trading Revenue Surges
description: After partnering with Kalshi, Coinbase wants to run prediction markets itself as competition intensifies across the industry.
fullContent:
Coinbase is preparing to launch its own event contracts in the US in the first half of 2027. The American crypto exchange currently offers prediction markets through a partnership with Kalshi, but an in-house operation would give it greater control over the contracts available to customers while allowing it to retain a larger share of trading revenue.

The planned service is expected to cater to both retail and institutional investors, according to Bloomberg.

2027 US Expansion

Coinbase has already taken steps to build the infrastructure needed for the move. Back in December 2025, it announced an agreement to acquire prediction-markets startup The Clearing Company, while its existing derivatives exchange and September approval from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission for its own clearinghouse provide further support for the expansion.

Chief Financial Officer Alesia Haas had indicated in October that the company intended to introduce its own event contracts, although she did not provide a launch date.

The push comes as prediction markets emerge as an increasingly important source of revenue for the crypto exchange.

Prediction markets had their biggest quarter yet after trading volume reached a whopping $194.1 billion between July and September 2026, a 75% jump from the previous quarter, according to Predicted. Kalshi and Polymarket continued to dominate and accounted for 91% of total volume, while US-regulated platforms captured nearly nine out of every ten dollars traded.

Sports remained the main attraction, but parlays, which allow traders to combine multiple outcomes in one bet, overtook individual sports events. The report also highlights how young Americans are driving activity, as people aged 18 to 24 accounted for 30% of Kalshi’s card deposits.

Fresh Setbacks

Despite the sector’s rapid growth, both major players are facing challenges of their own. Polymarket has cut staff across its marketing, customer experience, and engineering teams as part of a wider restructuring.

title: Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal
Blockstream researchers published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a hash-based post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the community to review it for flaws.
This post Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal

Several researchers have published a 131-page security analysis of SHRINCS, a proposed post-quantum signature scheme for Bitcoin, and are asking the wider community to look for flaws in it. Researcher Mikhail Kudinov announced the first version Thursday in a thread on X, saying the paper reduces SHRINCS’ security to the properties of its underlying hash function.

The analysis, dated Nov. 18, estimates classical security of 121.4 to 122.7 bits for SHRINCS, though those figures rest on assumptions that include three unproven conjectures. Kudinov said the work is not finished. The team is still working on a new analysis of a property called SM-DSPR, whose bound has so far been conjectured, and on tightening a reprogramming step and improving a bound against quantum attackers.

How SHRINCS works

SHRINCS is a hash-based scheme, meaning its security rests on hash functions rather than the elliptic curve math behind today’s Bitcoin signatures. It places two designs under one key: a stateful part built on FXMSS with WOTS+C, and a stateless fallback built on SLH-DSA. Because both use the same hash function, Kudinov said, the proof has to cover both.

Signature size is the main cost. Under the draft proposal, stateful SHRINCS signatures run from 548 to 4,619 bytes, while the stateless fallback is 5,777 bytes. Schnorr signatures on Bitcoin today are 64 bytes, and ECDSA signatures typically come in around 71. Signatures take up scarce block space, so larger ones mean fewer transactions per block.

The risk of a stateful signature

The compact stateful path carries a danger. It relies on one-time keys, and if a wallet accidentally reuses one, an attacker can forge a signature for that address and steal the funds. Wallet software therefore has to track the state of every key. The stateless path avoids the problem, but at a much larger size.

Jonas Nick, Blockstream’s director of research, told Isabel Foxen Duke, head of the MARA Foundation, on MARA Foundation TV that wallets must automatically fall back to the stateless path whenever a state counter could be compromised. “It needs to be impossible for the user to behave in a way that this catastrophic event happens,” he said. “Wallet developers need to deal with this stateful component correctly.”

Nick also warned that heavy use of the larger signatures would weigh on the network. “We don’t know what the fee market will look like once we have these very big signatures,” he said. “And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin.”

Researchers ask for review

The authors are clear that the analysis needs scrutiny. Kudinov said it has not been sufficiently peer reviewed, and the project’s GitHub repository warns that the documents may contain errors and should not be the sole basis for deploying SHRINCS. “We tried to be careful, but a proof of this size can have mistakes,” he wrote, asking readers to open an issue if they find one.

The team also produced two results that are not specific to SHRINCS: a classical bound for a property called ITSR without reprogramming, and a quadratic quantum bound for undetectability. Kudinov said they also apply to SPHINCS+ and SLH-DSA, the hash-based schemes SHRINCS borrows from, and that they were published as separate papers.

The SHRINCS work lands as quantum risk climbs the agenda. A global securities regulators’ group this week warned that moving blockchains to quantum-resistant cryptography may be especially hard, and researchers recently built a post-quantum defense for the Lightning Network after Bitcoin’s first quantum-safe transaction was shown without a fork.

The draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal for SHRINCS is also open for comment. “We need all the possible feedback — engineers, cryptographers, protocol developers,” Kudinov, a post-quantum cryptography researcher at Blockstream, said of it. “There are a lot of things to check, test, complain about, or praise.”

This post Researchers Publish Security Analysis of Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum SHRINCS Proposal first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: SHIB Needs a 386% Climb for a $10 Billion Market Cap, and Burns Won't Get It There
description: Shiba Inu fell to a fresh one-year low as an analyst doubted a $10 billion valuation by 2030. See why burns fall short and where SHIB meets resistance.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • An analyst concluded that a $10 billion Shiba Inu valuation by 2030 looks unlikely, and token burns barely help.
  • SHIB has slipped below the yearly low cited in that analysis.
  • Resistance looms overhead, and no clear floor shows up beneath price.

Shiba Inu has fallen to a fresh one-year low just days after an analyst questioned whether the meme coin can ever reach a $10 billion valuation.

The drop widens the gap to that target and leaves SHIB tied to Bitcoin's weak tape. Momentum gauges look stretched, and buyers have not stepped in. Traders now want to know whether an oversold bounce can hold, or whether Bitcoin drags the token into open air below.

An Analyst Runs the Numbers on a $10 Billion Shiba Inu

Crypto analyst Sam Daodu asked on Nov 19 whether Shiba Inu could reach that valuation by 2030. His conclusion was that it is unlikely.

SHIB carried a market value of about $2.25 billion at the time and ranked 39th among cryptocurrencies. A $10 billion valuation would require a token price near $0.000017.

Supply offers no shortcut. About 589.2 trillion of the 589.5 trillion tokens already circulate, so the target rests on price alone. Daodu expects burns to remove roughly 3.7 billion SHIB by 2030. That is about 0.0006% of supply, too little to matter.

History offers little comfort. SHIB last traded above the target in May 2025, at $0.0000176. Its all-time high of $0.000086 dates back to Oct 27, 2021. A repeat of the 260% rally from March 2024 would lift it only to about $0.0000137.

Daodu tied any recovery to Bitcoin. The largest coin traded around $62,685 that day, down 31.8% over the year. It had lost 28.7% in 2026 alone.

A Fresh Low Puts SHIB Further From the Target

Shiba Inu (SHIB) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

SHIB has already broken below the low cited in Daodu's analysis. The token trades near $0.0000035. That sits under the $0.0000038 mark it first touched on Nov 18.

At today's price, SHIB would need a gain of about 386% to get there. That climb is steeper than the one Daodu measured a few days ago.

The moving averages show who is in charge. A moving average tracks the mean closing price over a set number of days. SHIB sits below its 50-day average near $0.0000046, so that line now acts as a ceiling.

Its 200-day average sits higher, around $0.0000053, and SHIB trades well beneath it. With price under both lines and the shorter one below the longer, the chart describes a clean downtrend.

Selling has also picked up speed. SHIB fell about 6% in the past 24 hours. Over seven days the loss reached roughly 19%.

The monthly picture is worse. SHIB is down about 31% over 30 days, a sharper drop than the one Daodu reported. Losses are growing in every window, so sellers are pressing harder.

Oversold Readings Have Not Slowed the Sellers

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 23 on the daily chart. Readings below 30 count as oversold, so SHIB has fallen faster than its usual pace. Stretched readings like this often come before a short relief bounce.

An oversold signal does not mark a bottom by itself. In a strong downtrend, RSI can stay low for weeks while price keeps sinking. Buyers need to show up first.

So far they have not. The MACD line remains below its signal line, which means momentum is still pointing down. Trend strength readings show sellers leading a firm trend.

A bounce from these levels may come. The broader pressure still favors the downside.

The First Wall Sits Above an Empty Floor

No support level shows up on the daily chart right now. SHIB keeps printing fresh lows, so there is no recent floor where buyers stepped in before. Price has open air beneath it.

Overhead, the picture is clearer. The first resistance sits near $0.0000043. A reclaim of that level would be the first sign of relief for holders.

The next barrier waits around $0.0000048. A move above it would put SHIB back over the 50-day line and break the ceiling that has capped every rally this fall.

Even that would leave the bigger test untouched. Daodu named a monthly close above $0.0000093 as the first real sign of a trend change. That level also marks the one-year high, set on Jan 5. SHIB would have to more than double just to reach it.

What Decides the Next Three Days

Two outcomes look most likely over the next three days, and Bitcoin will probably pick between them.

  • Bullish: The oversold reading sparks a relief bounce that reclaims the first resistance and runs toward the second barrier near the 50-day line. A slide back under the current low would cancel this path.
  • Bearish: Bitcoin keeps weakening, SHIB stays capped below the first wall, and fresh lows follow in open air. A daily close above the second barrier would end this setup and hand buyers their first real win.

The Burn Story Cannot Outrun the Chart

Daodu's math holds up, and the chart makes the target look harder. Burns are too small to lift price, so the goal remains a long shot.

The main risk sits below. If Bitcoin keeps falling, the meme coin could set new lows quickly, with little to slow the drop.

title: Banks Are Adopting Stablecoins: Here Is Why Crypto-Native Dollars Still Win on User Freedom
description: As traditional giants rush into digital dollars, USDD’s Yvonne Chia explains why 24/7 access, self-custody, and transparent yield give decentralized stablecoins an edge banks can’t replicate. 20 November – Road Town, Totorla, British Virgin Islands – Decentralized stablecoin protocol USDD is accelerating its multichain utility across TRON, Ethereum, and BNB Chain—combining automated sUSDD yield via its Smart Allocator with GasFree zero-TRX transfers—as traditional financial giants race to build competing stablecoin rails.  In a recent industry interview with instant exchange partner ChangeNOW, USDD Head of Communications Yvonne Chia outlined why self-custody, 24/7 settlement, and transparent onchain reserves give decentralized digital dollars a structural advantage over bank-issued alternatives. 1. Permissionless Access vs. Gatekept Accounts For billions of people globally, opening and maintaining a traditional bank account still involves paperwork, minimum balance requirements, geographic restrictions, and approval delays. Even when banks integrate stablecoin rails behind the scenes, those services remain gated behind legacy compliance walls and intermediary control. Crypto-native stablecoins flip that model on its head. As Yvonne Chia highlighted during the interview: “Compare this to a stablecoin like USDD, where all you need is a phone, a working internet connection, you can immediately start a wallet and you have access to your funds right away.” With USDD, users can access and manage their digital dollars directly through their own wallets, without depending on traditional financial intermediaries.  This represents a fundamental shift in financial access: users are no longer limited to the services, operating hours, or account structures of a single institution. Instead, they have the freedom to hold, manage, and transfer their assets on their own terms. Self-custody also gives users greater autonomy over their financial decisions. They can choose which wallets to use, where to transfer their assets, and which supported decentralized applications to interact with, without needing to route every transaction through a centralized financial institution.  With USDD, users’ digital dollars can move with them across an open blockchain ecosystem, rather than remaining tied to a particular bank or service provider. 2. 24/7 Global Settlement vs. “Banking Hours” Legacy payment networks still operate on decades-old schedules: weekend cutoffs, bank holidays, and multi-day cross-border settlement delays accompanied by hefty wire fees. Blockchain networks never close. Whether it is a Sunday night or a public holiday, USDD moves globally without depending on traditional banking operating hours or settlement windows. “We are able to have transfers 24/7 and we’re not limited to any traditional banking hours. So I think that in some ways, stablecoins are not just becoming banks, but exceeding what traditional banks can offer to users.” To make everyday transfers even smoother than fintech apps, USDD introduced GasFree integration on TRON, allowing users on supported wallets to pay network fees directly in USDD without needing to hold TRX. This removes another practical barrier to stablecoin adoption: having to acquire and maintain a separate gas token just to transfer digital dollars. With GasFree, eligible users can pay approximately 0.5 USDD per transaction, compared with around 1.5 USDT for a standard USDT transfer under the referenced fee conditions. These improvements matter because the usefulness of a stablecoin is not determined by its peg alone. Low-cost transfers, straightforward wallet experiences, and around-the-clock availability are what make digital dollars practical for everyday payments and global value transfers. 3. Passing Yield Back to Users vs. Bank Spreads Perhaps the sharpest contrast between banks and decentralized stablecoins lies in how yield is distributed.  In traditional banking, institutions take customer deposits, deploy them into yield-generating markets, and retain a significant portion of the returns. Everyday depositors may receive relatively low interest rates, while higher-yielding products often come with eligibility requirements, minimum deposits, or fixed maturity periods. Stablecoins introduce another way to participate in digital-dollar opportunities. Rather than keeping capital entirely within a traditional deposit account, users can access onchain yield opportunities through decentralized protocols and transparent investment mechanisms. USDD was built to return that value directly to holders. Through USDD Earn, users can deposit USDD to receive sUSDD, earning automated, competitive yield powered by our Smart Allocator system, with no fixed lock-up periods restricting access to their capital. For users, the distinction is important: USDD Earn provides access to a productive stablecoin while maintaining flexibility, rather than requiring users to commit their capital to a conventional fixed-term product. 4. Onchain Verification vs. Institutional Trust Traditional banks ask customers to trust closed-door balance sheets and periodic regulatory filings—until a crisis proves otherwise.  USDD takes a different approach through its “Don’t trust, verify” ethos, emphasizing publicly accessible onchain information and independent verification. Onchain Transparency: Smart contract addresses, collateral reserves, and Smart Allocator deployments are publicly viewable, allowing users to examine relevant information directly on the blockchain. Structured Disclosures: Quarterly Treasury Reports provide additional information about reserve positions, financial performance, and operational developments. Independent Security Reviews: USDD undergoes third-party security audits to assess its smart contracts and identify potential vulnerabilities. Transparency does not eliminate financial or technical risks, but it changes how users can evaluate them. Instead of relying exclusively on an institution’s assurances, users have access to information that can be independently examined and verified. 5. Beyond a Single Network: An Open, Multichain Financial Ecosystem Financial freedom is not just about holding digital dollars. It is also about being able to use them wherever opportunities and applications exist. A stablecoin confined to a single network or limited use case cannot fully realize the potential of open blockchain finance. Following its January 2025 protocol upgrade, USDD expanded natively from TRON onto Ethereum and BNB Chain, extending its reach across multiple blockchain ecosystems. This multichain presence allows USDD to connect with different communities, liquidity environments, and decentralized applications. Its sUSDD product has also expanded into DeFi integrations, including Pendle and Morpho, giving users additional ways to access yield strategies across supported ecosystems. The bigger picture is an interconnected financial ecosystem in which users can move between holding, transferring, exchanging, and deploying their stablecoins according to their own needs. These are not isolated functions. Together, they make stablecoins more useful as everyday financial infrastructure. The Future: Interconnected, Open, and Multichain Banks will undoubtedly continue using stablecoin rails to modernize their back-end settlement. However, true financial freedom comes from open networks where assets flow freely across protocols without intermediaries. For USDD, the opportunity goes beyond offering a dollar-pegged asset. It is about making digital dollars accessible, transferable, and productive across an interconnected financial ecosystem. From self-custody and 24/7 transfers to flexible yield opportunities and multichain DeFi access, these capabilities give users more ways to put their money to work. Banks may be bringing stablecoins into traditional finance. Crypto-native protocols are showing what stablecoins can make possible beyond it. Stablecoins introduce another way to participate in digital-dollar opportunities. Rather than keeping capital entirely within a traditional deposit account, users can access onchain yield opportunities through decentralized protocols and transparent investment mechanisms.

USDD was built to return that value directly to holders. Through USDD Earn, users can deposit USDD to receive sUSDD, earning automated, competitive yield powered by our Smart Allocator system, with no fixed lock-up periods restricting access to their capital.

For users, the distinction is important: USDD Earn provides access to a productive stablecoin while maintaining flexibility, rather than requiring users to commit their capital to a conventional fixed-term product.

4. Onchain Verification vs. Institutional Trust

Traditional banks ask customers to trust closed-door balance sheets and periodic regulatory filings—until a crisis proves otherwise. 

USDD takes a different approach through its “Don’t trust, verify” ethos, emphasizing publicly accessible onchain information and independent verification.

  • Onchain Transparency: Smart contract addresses, collateral reserves, and Smart Allocator deployments are publicly viewable, allowing users to examine relevant information directly on the blockchain.
  • Structured Disclosures: Quarterly Treasury Reports provide additional information about reserve positions, financial performance, and operational developments.
  • Independent Security Reviews: USDD undergoes third-party security audits to assess its smart contracts and identify potential vulnerabilities.

Transparency does not eliminate financial or technical risks, but it changes how users can evaluate them. Instead of relying exclusively on an institution’s assurances, users have access to information that can be independently examined and verified.

5. Beyond a Single Network: An Open, Multichain Financial Ecosystem Financial freedom is not just about holding digital dollars. It is also about being able to use them wherever opportunities and applications exist. A stablecoin confined to a single network or limited use case cannot fully realize the potential of open blockchain finance. Following its January 2025 protocol upgrade, USDD expanded natively from TRON onto Ethereum and BNB Chain, extending its reach across multiple blockchain ecosystems. This multichain presence allows USDD to connect with different communities, liquidity environments, and decentralized applications. Its sUSDD product has also expanded into DeFi integrations, including Pendle and Morpho, giving users additional ways to access yield strategies across supported ecosystems.

The bigger picture is an interconnected financial ecosystem in which users can move between holding, transferring, exchanging, and deploying their stablecoins according to their own needs. These are not isolated functions. Together, they make stablecoins more useful as everyday financial infrastructure.

The Future: Interconnected, Open, and Multichain

Banks will undoubtedly continue using stablecoin rails to modernize their back-end settlement. However, true financial freedom comes from open networks where assets flow freely across protocols without intermediaries.

For USDD, the opportunity goes beyond offering a dollar-pegged asset. It is about making digital dollars accessible, transferable, and productive across an interconnected financial ecosystem. From self-custody and 24/7 transfers to flexible yield opportunities and multichain DeFi access, these capabilities give users more ways to put their money to work.

Banks may be bringing stablecoins into traditional finance. Crypto-native protocols are showing what stablecoins can make possible beyond it.
