title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged the Fed not to embrace a bigger rate hike as Citi and traders still see a quarter-point move in December and bitcoin fell below $60,000.
This post U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a bigger Federal Reserve rate hike, even as bitcoin broke below $60,000 for the first time since July and stocks sank on bets that the Fed will keep tightening into a selloff.

Bessent told CNBC he would encourage the Fed not to embrace a half-point increase at its Dec. 8-9 meeting. He cited the energy supply shock and a drop in crude prices as reasons for the central bank to hold back.

Bessent says the Fed should look forward

He argued that one governor now backing a 50 basis point hike had wanted a similar cut within the last year. Bessent said it “seems somewhat peripatetic” to want the bigger increase only 11 or 12 months later. He did not name the governor.

“I would encourage the Fed to look forward, not backwards,” Bessent said.

The comments came two days after Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC a half-point hike is probably necessary in December and that the central bank may need to “shock people.” Waller said inflation is “headed in the wrong direction, and it’s spreading out.”

Fed officials split on how far to go

Waller is not alone. Minutes of the October meeting showed nearly all officials expect a quarter-point hike in December, and two floated a larger one. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee also declined to rule out a bigger move on Thursday.

“We’ve now had multiple months in a row of borderline disturbingly high inflation rates with little progress in the sectors where we would expect to be seeing some progress,” Goolsbee told reporters. “So everything’s always on the table.”

Not everyone wants to go bigger. New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that “I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action.” St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem has suggested as many as four hikes by the spring of 2027.

The Fed raised rates in September for the first time in more than three years and held them steady in October. Inflation has stayed hot since the Iran strikes pushed up energy prices earlier this year.

Citi and traders still see a quarter-point hike

Citi still expects a quarter-point increase in December. Global chief economist Nathan Sheets said Thursday he does not see a need for 50 basis points despite persistent inflation. In a note Friday, the bank wrote that “Fed officials will consequently have little appetite to hike into an equity sell-off.”

Citi expects the Fed to hold after December and begin cutting later in 2027. Traders agree on the next step: the CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point hike, and the 10-year Treasury yield fell more than 10 basis points to 4.95% as investors bought bonds.

Stocks fell for another day. The Nasdaq Composite dropped more than 2% in morning trading, and the VIX volatility index topped 30, its highest level since March.

What it means for bitcoin

Bitcoin traded near $59,700 shortly before 11 a.m. ET, down more than 5% on the day, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro. It broke below $60,000 for the first time since early July and is on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, the longest streak since 2022.

Higher rates are a headwind for assets that pay no yield, and the selloff has reached companies that hold bitcoin. Strategy’s stock fell for a sixth straight session on Thursday, and the bitcoin price has dropped roughly 25% in a month, a slide Bitcoin Magazine tracked earlier this week.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill tied the outlook to inflation in a note dated Nov. 18. “Our base case remains range trading around USD 60k to 90k through much of 2027, until falling inflation gives monetary policy room to ease,” he said.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $59,300.

This post U.S. Treasury Secretary Pushes Back on Bigger Fed Hike first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Bitcoin Plummets to 4.5-Month Low, Anthropic IPO Shatters Records, Wall Street Bleeds: Weekly Recap
description: BTC dipped below $60,000 for the first time since early July on Friday.
fullContent:
It was another historic week for financial markets, but not everything went smoothly or as expected. For crypto, it was mostly pain.

But let’s begin as usual, with a small recap from the end of the previous week. At the time, BTC had tanked below $70,000, which was already a massive collapse. It came on the heels of Nvidia’s scandal and subsequent CEO resignation, while inflation fears had rocketed.

The weekend came. In general, it was expected to be a quiet one, as most weekends are. The reality was very different. The bears took control of the market once again and kept pressing the price south. The culmination took place in the evening, when BTC had tanked to $62,000 for the first time in months. This meant that it had dumped by $19,000 in 10 days or so.

The relief rally was next, and it took place on Sunday and Monday with a brief pump to $66,000. The predominantly bearish market sentiment and the expectations for the upcoming Anthropic IPO, which many experts linked to the crypto calamity, as investors were allegedly pulling capital out of other risk-on assets to take advantage of what became the largest public listing.

BTC continued to bounce between $62,000 and $65,000, but the upper boundary was too strong. The lower, on the other hand, couldn’t provide the necessary support on Friday morning when BTC dipped below it. Although it managed to hold there for almost an entire day, the market unraveled once again minutes ago.

As reported earlier, bitcoin crashed below $60,000 for the first time in almost five months, and has since continued its journey south to just under $59,000 as of now. This means that it has now tumbled by $22,000 in two and a half weeks. The decline on a weekly scale is quite staggering, with bitcoin dumping by 13%. ETH has slumped by a similar percentage, while HYPE, ZEC, DOGE, and XMR are down by over 15%.

Market Data

Market Cap: $2.2T | 24H Vol: $91B | BTC Dominance: 54.5%

BTC: $58,750 (-13%) | ETH: $1,630 (-14%) | XRP: $0.90 (-10.6%)

This Week’s Crypto Headlines You Can’t Miss

Global Markets Turn Red: Bitcoin Crashes as Wall Street Loses Over 1,100 Dow Points. As the title of this Market Update suggests, Wall Street has been hit hard as well. Recent data showed that the S&P 500 lost over $6 trillion in market cap since early October, and the losses have only worsened over the past week.

Ripple CEO Sees Crypto Comeback After Anthropic IPO: Is History About to Repeat? Meanwhile, market experts are still hopeful that the overall bearish trend will reverse now that the Anthropic IPO is behind us. The latest to outline such an opinion was Ripple’s CEO, who predicted a crypto comeback.

Jensen Huang Breaks Silence on Nvidia Scandal, Says He Is Ready to Return as CEO. The saga around Nvidia’s former CEO unfolded very quickly, and he finally broke his silence at the start of the current week. He admitted to personal misconduct, expressed gratitude for the support he had received, and suggested that he is open to returning to leadership despite ongoing investigations.

These 4 Tokens Will Pump Before the AI Bubble Ends: Arthur Hayes. The uncertainty within all markets hasn’t deterred Arthur Hayes from making some bold claims about certain tokens that could still post major gains before the AI bubble shatters. The ones he believes in are ETH, ZEC, NEAR, and VVV.

Former SEC Chair Warns When the AI Boom Will Cause a Recession. Speaking of the potential end of the AI bubble, former SEC Chair Gary Gensler warned that such a development may lead to a worldwide recession before 2028, as he linked it to past economic downturns.

Solana Is Planning Its Next Major Upgrades: Here’s What Changes. Solana plans significant network upgrades for next year as it aims to double compute capacity and reduce token account compute units by 80% to enhance performance. Anza CEO Brennan Watt unveiled a roadmap that includes faster block distribution, improved transaction ordering, and cheaper on-chain computation for complex financial apps.

title: ETH May Slide to $1,000 if $1,500 Breaks on a Higher Timeframe Close, CryptoPatel Warns
description: Ethereum sits deeply oversold as ETF outflows and exchange inflows build. Analyst CryptoPatel says a close below $1,500 could open a slide toward $1,000.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Fresh coins are flowing onto exchanges while spot Ethereum ETFs log a seventh straight week of outflows.
  • Ether looks deeply oversold on the daily chart, yet sellers still control the trend.
  • Analyst CryptoPatel says a higher-timeframe close below $1,500 could open a much deeper slide.

Ethereum faces a test of nerve as on-chain data show coins moving back to exchanges and fund investors keep pulling money out. Analyst CryptoPatel warned that a break of one key level could send ETH sharply lower.

The warning lands after a bruising month for the second-largest crypto asset. Oversold readings hint at a possible bounce, yet buyers have stayed quiet.

Exchange Inflows and ETF Exits Put $1,500 in Focus

Ethereum is drawing fresh coins onto exchanges as its price slides. CryptoQuant data show exchange reserves fell to about 14.43 million ETH on Nov 16. They jumped by roughly 140,000 ETH the next day and have held near 14.57 million since.

Binance logged a net inflow of 17,485 ETH during the decline. Coins moving to an exchange often signal plans to sell, though an inflow alone does not prove a sale.

Fund flows point the same way. Spot Ethereum ETFs lost about $398.9 million in the week ending Nov 13, their seventh straight week of outflows. Santiment offered the lone counter signal, tracking a one-day net outflow of 4,186 stETH from exchanges. That was the largest since May 30.

Analyst CryptoPatel places ETH near the top of a $1,646 to $1,744 zone. He calls $1,500 the key test and warns that a higher-timeframe close below it could expose $1,000. A move above $2,807 would be the first sign of a broader bullish shift, he said. Merlijn The Trader sees $1,575 as the next potential stop.

ETH Trades Far Beneath Both Averages After a 29% Month

Ethereum (ETH) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Ether traded near $1,740 on the latest data, unchanged over the past day. The calm session follows a rough stretch. ETH lost about 14% over the week and roughly 29% over the past month.

That monthly drop leaves the token near the bottom of its 30-day range. Buyers who stepped in during the past few weeks are now holding losses. That can add supply on any rebound, as traders look to exit near their entry price.

Moving averages show the depth of the damage. A moving average smooths out daily swings to show the underlying trend. The 50-day average sits near $2,190. The 200-day average is higher, around $2,260. ETH trades well beneath both, so each line now acts as a ceiling overhead.

The 50-day line has slipped below the 200-day line. That means the recent trend is weaker than the longer one, a pattern traders read as a sign of lasting pressure. The wide gap between price and both lines shows how quickly the selling has run.

A session without new losses suggests sellers paused after a heavy week. A single quiet day does not make a reversal, though. ETH would need to string together higher closes before the chart shows real repair.

Oversold Readings Have Not Stopped the Sellers

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 22 on the daily chart. Any reading below 30 counts as oversold. It means sellers have pushed the price down faster than usual, and markets in that state often stage short relief bounces.

An oversold reading alone gives no buy signal. Momentum still points down on the MACD. Sellers have not yet lost their grip on the daily trend.

Trend strength readings back that up. They show a real trend in place, and sellers are the ones driving it. In strong downtrends, RSI can stay pinned in oversold territory for days or even weeks.

A bounce would carry more weight if momentum turned higher while the price stopped setting fresh lows.

Why $2,170 Matters More Than Any Bounce

Nearest resistance sits near $2,170, just under the 50-day line. A daily close above it would be the first real repair on the chart. It would put ETH back above a ceiling sellers have defended through the slide. The next barrier waits near $2,280, close to the 200-day average.

The downside map looks thinner. Chart support does not appear until about $1,200, and no level is marked in between. That gap makes CryptoPatel's key test the practical floor for now. Analysts flag a broad $1,500 to $1,800 band as possible support. Convincing buyers have not shown up there yet.

Traders would first want to see ETH recover around $1,900. That recovery would show demand returning before price tests the heavier resistance overhead.

Two Roads From the Bottom of the Range

ETH now sits between a crowded ceiling and a thin floor, and the next decisive move sets the path.

  • Bullish: An oversold relief rally that clears the reassuring level analysts flagged would open a run at nearest resistance, just under the 50-day line. A slide back under Merlijn The Trader's next stop would cancel that setup.
  • Bearish: Losing Merlijn's stop would bring CryptoPatel's floor into play, with the chart's lone support level waiting below. A daily close back above the reassuring level would invalidate this case.

Oversold but Not Yet Bought

ETH looks stretched enough for a bounce. The trend still belongs to sellers until the price reclaims resistance under the 50-day line.

The bigger risk sits in the flows. If ETF exits and exchange inflows keep building, a break of that floor could turn into the deeper slide CryptoPatel warned about.

title: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since early July on Friday as a tech stock rout, rate hike bets and record ETF outflows hit risk assets.
This post Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens

The bitcoin price crashed below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since early July, falling about $1,800 in roughly an hour as a deepening U.S. tech stock selloff dragged risk assets lower.

Bitcoin traded near $61,400 at 9:40 a.m. ET and slid to about $59,600 by 10:45 a.m., a drop of nearly 3%, according to Look Into Bitcoin data. The bitcoin price is down about $3,400, or more than 5%, from the same time Thursday, when it traded near $63,000.

The break of $60,000 is a key psychological level, and it came with little warning. Bitcoin price had held above $61,000 for most of the morning, even after a third straight daily loss.

Stocks and rate hike bets drive the selloff

Wall Street opened sharply lower. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% in morning trading as shares of Anthropic extended losses in its second day since a record Nasdaq debut. Nvidia and AMD also traded lower.

Bitcoin has been moving with tech stocks. The market has questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off, and Friday’s open did nothing to ease that worry.

Rate expectations are adding pressure. Traders see a roughly 94% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed. Higher rates tend to hurt bitcoin and other assets that pay no yield.

Earlier Friday, South Korea’s Kospi index fell more than 5% and chipmakers sank across Asia. That selling carried into U.S. trading and then into bitcoin.

Some analysts had flagged $60,000 as a floor. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of bitcoin’s trading range sits “just below 60,000,” and that it “appears to be trying to find a footing.” Friday’s drop tests that view.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said this week the drop is a “continuation of the existing bear market.” His base case is range trading around $60,000 to $90,000 through much of 2027.

ETF outflows and liquidations

Funds have been sellers. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost $541.1 million on Thursday, its biggest one-day outflow on record. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total, extending a streak of heavy withdrawals this week.

Leveraged traders were hit as well. More than $700 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the 24 hours before the latest drop, and about 86% were bets on higher prices. The slide below $60,000 likely forced out more of them.

The move extends a month-long slump. Bitcoin has dropped roughly $20,000 in the past month, a slide tracked as the price fell under $62,000 on Thursday.

Crypto stocks fall harder than bitcoin price

Crypto stocks fell even faster. Strategy (MSTR) was down about 7% near $79.85, a day after it tumbled for a sixth straight session. Coinbase (COIN) fell about 3% to $105.36. Shares of Strive (ASST) fell to $15.31 Friday morning, down 21.47%, or $4.19, over the past five days. The stock has slid steadily from near $19.50 as bitcoin price’s sell-off deepened, with its sharpest drop in Friday’s trading.

Bitcoin miners took the worst of it. MARA Holdings (MARA) dropped about 11% to $5.55. Riot Platforms (RIOT) lost about 11% to $15.85, and CleanSpark (CLSK) fell about 12% to $5.13.

Data center operators that also mine bitcoin were hit hard. IREN fell about 12% to $12.62, and Cipher Digital (CIFR) dropped 14% to $5.58. Both have traded with AI stocks, which are also under pressure.

The bitcoin price is now at its lowest since the first days of July. Bitcoin set its record above $126,000 in October 2025, so it has lost more than half its value from that peak.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $59,600.

Stocks and rate hike bets drive the selloff

Wall Street opened sharply lower. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% in morning trading as shares of Anthropic extended losses in its second day since a record Nasdaq debut. Nvidia and AMD also traded lower.

Bitcoin has been moving with tech stocks. The market has questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off, and Friday’s open did nothing to ease that worry.

Rate expectations are adding pressure. Traders see a roughly 94% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed. Higher rates tend to hurt bitcoin and other assets that pay no yield.

Earlier Friday, South Korea’s Kospi index fell more than 5% and chipmakers sank across Asia. That selling carried into U.S. trading and then into bitcoin.

Some analysts had flagged $60,000 as a floor. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of bitcoin’s trading range sits “just below 60,000,” and that it “appears to be trying to find a footing.” Friday’s drop tests that view.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said this week the drop is a “continuation of the existing bear market.” His base case is range trading around $60,000 to $90,000 through much of 2027.

ETF outflows and liquidations

Funds have been sellers. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost $541.1 million on Thursday, its biggest one-day outflow on record. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total, extending a streak of heavy withdrawals this week.

Leveraged traders were hit as well. More than $700 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the 24 hours before the latest drop, and about 86% were bets on higher prices. The slide below $60,000 likely forced out more of them.

The move extends a month-long slump. Bitcoin has dropped roughly $20,000 in the past month, a slide tracked as the price fell under $62,000 on Thursday.

Crypto stocks fall harder than bitcoin price

Crypto stocks fell even faster. Strategy (MSTR) was down about 7% near $79.85, a day after it tumbled for a sixth straight session. Coinbase (COIN) fell about 3% to $105.36. Shares of Strive (ASST) fell to $15.31 Friday morning, down 21.47%, or $4.19, over the past five days. The stock has slid steadily from near $19.50 as bitcoin price’s sell-off deepened, with its sharpest drop in Friday’s trading.

Bitcoin miners took the worst of it. MARA Holdings (MARA) dropped about 11% to $5.55. Riot Platforms (RIOT) lost about 11% to $15.85, and CleanSpark (CLSK) fell about 12% to $5.13.

Data center operators that also mine bitcoin were hit hard. IREN fell about 12% to $12.62, and Cipher Digital (CIFR) dropped 14% to $5.58. Both have traded with AI stocks, which are also under pressure.

The bitcoin price is now at its lowest since the first days of July. Bitcoin set its record above $126,000 in October 2025, so it has lost more than half its value from that peak.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $59,600.

This post Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Why the Agent Era Needs a New Operating System | DHH
description:
David Heinemeier Hansson thinks the agent era is reopening a window in computing that has been closed for decades: the chance to build a new operating system people actually want to use.
DHH joins a16z General Partners Martin Casado and Anish Acharya to explain why he’s building Omarchy, an agent-first Linux distribution designed around a computer that users can modify simply by asking. They discuss why the command lines, config files, and detailed error messages that once made Linux intimidating now make it unusually well suited to agents, and why DHH believes software development has become cheap enough to challenge decades-old platform lock-in.
But if code is becoming abundant, what still matters? DHH argues that taste, craft, and the willingness to obsess over the final 2% become more important, not less. The conversation moves from tiny teams wielding the productive capacity of thousands of people to open models, competition at the frontier, and the return of hacker, demo, and pseudonymous internet culture.

title: Bitcoin Drops Below $60,000 for First Time Since July
description:
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since July, even as US inflation expectations dropped to 3.7%. Here's why.
The post Bitcoin Drops Below $60,000 for First Time Since July appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July. It touched $59,850 on Binance less than an hour after Americans said they expect inflation to cool.

That should have been good news for risky assets. It was not. Traders still see a 97.9% chance the Federal Reserve (Fed) raises rates on December 9, CME FedWatch data shows.

What Did Americans Just Say About Inflation?

Americans now expect 3.7% inflation over the next year, down from 4.7% in October, a University of Michigan survey showed. Cheaper gas helped.

The news killed one bet. A week ago, traders gave a half-point “jumbo” hike 11.5% odds. By Friday morning, those odds hit zero.

But a smaller hike is still a hike. It would extend a run that began with the Fed’s first hike in three years in September.

Why Is Bitcoin Still Falling?

Higher rates hurt assets that pay nothing. They make gold costlier to hold. Bitcoin pays no interest either.

Big investors are also heading for the exits. US Bitcoin funds have lost about $3.47 billion this month, including BlackRock’s record $541 million outflow.

Bitcoin had already slipped to its estimated $62,000 mining cost on Thursday. Friday’s drop pushed it lower still.

Gold slid after the survey too, before paring losses.

Is the Fed Listening to Cheaper Gas?

Not yet. Most Fed officials feared inflation could stick even if gas prices kept falling, October meeting minutes showed.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller still wants a half-point hike.

“If you really want to get it down, you’ve got to start taking more aggressive actions,” AP reported.

Even Friday’s survey shows scars. Both inflation gauges remain above levels seen before the Iran war began in February.

The Fed’s preferred inflation gauge lands November 25. On December 9, Bitcoin holders learn whether the Fed shares Americans’ optimism.

title: Over $1 Billion in Longs Wrecked as Bitcoin (BTC) Slides Below $60K
description: The cryptocurrency is down by over $21,000 in just over two weeks.
fullContent:
It’s been a new low every day over the past few weeks, with bitcoin sliding to just inches below $60,000 minutes ago for the first time since early July, which was considered the bear market bottom. It’s not so certain now, though.

As usual, the altcoins have followed suit. Ethereum has tanked by almost 6%, while SOL has plunged by over 7%. ZEC continues to dig new lows, plummeting by a mind-blowing 16.5% in the past 24 hours alone.

Recall that the leading cryptocurrency tapped $81,000 just a day after the midterm elections in the US concluded at the start of the month. Who could have envisioned what happened in the next several weeks?

The calamity pushed BTC south to under $76,000 first, before the asset continued losing key support levels. The drop below $70,000 was particularly painful as it opened the wormhole for additional losses that continue to unravel almost on a daily basis. The latest came minutes ago with a dip to $59,950 on Bitstamp, even though the asset is barely hanging at $60,000 as of press time.

The reasons for this massive nosedive vary. Although many people blame it on the Anthropic IPO and how it drains liquidity similar to the SpaceX listing earlier this year, it’s not as simple.

Other macro factors are in play, including expectations for the Fed to continue hiking rates next month, as well as new reports claiming the US and Israel are preparing to restart attacking Iran. Oh, Russia and Ukraine are nowhere close to a deal, while oil prices remain elevated, and so is inflation.

The reality is that BTC has taken a massive hit, but it’s not alone. Yes, the altcoins are crashing hard, but so are Wall Street, as well as gold and silver.

However, let’s get back to the current market environment and check out the liquidations. CoinGlass data shows over $340 million in longs wrecked in the past hour alone, and the figure is up to $1.01 billion on a daily scale. More than 225,000 traders have been wrecked in the past day.

title: Cathie Wood Says BTC Has Found Its Low and Keeps ARK's $1.5M Target for 2030
description: Cathie Wood says bitcoin has bottomed and keeps ARK's $1.5 million 2030 target. The chart shows oversold momentum, with $75,000 as the ceiling to clear.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • ARK Invest's Cathie Wood said bitcoin has found its low and kept the firm's long-range bull target intact.
  • The daily chart shows deeply oversold momentum, yet sellers still control the trend.
  • Bitcoin's converged moving averages near $75,000 now form the ceiling any recovery must clear.

Cathie Wood says the bitcoin sell-off is over. The ARK Invest chief said the firm believes the coin has bottomed, and she stood by ARK's bull case for 2030.

Her call lands as the regulation story that powered this cycle has stalled in Washington. Crypto executives now pin their hopes on tokenization and Wall Street adoption. Traders face a sharper near-term test: whether exhausted sellers give way to real buying.

ARK Holds Its $1.5 Million Call as the Regulation Trade Fades

Wood, ARK's chief investment officer, kept the firm's $1.5 million bull-case target for 2030. She added that a new all-time high before the end of 2027 would not surprise her.

Bitcoin now trades more than 50% below its record above $126,000, set in October 2025. Regulation was supposed to carry this cycle. That driver fizzled after the Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act, a crypto market-structure bill, on Sept. 15.

Industry leaders now point to tokenization. "Every single traditional firm is now looking at digital assets," BitGo CEO Mike Belshe said, citing BlackRock. eToro CEO Yoni Assia said "hundreds of trillions of dollars" will move onchain. He pointed to the CFTC clearing stock-linked perpetual futures and an SEC order on tokenized stocks. Strategy's Michael Saylor said last month that the next bull market is already underway.

Wood flagged cybersecurity as a top risk after the $6.3 billion Binance hack. She also said AI is pulling attention away from bitcoin. Inflation and the Iran war remain on investors' lists too.

Bitcoin Trades Far Beneath a Converged $75K Average

Bitcoin (BTC) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Bitcoin traded near $60,000 on Friday, down about 3% in the past day. The coin fell about 15% this week and roughly 27% over the past month.

That monthly slide leaves bitcoin pinned near the bottom of its 30-day range. Buyers have not yet stepped in with enough force to lift it off those lows. On the daily chart, the price sits in open space with no marked floor beneath it.

A moving average smooths out daily swings to show the underlying direction of price. Bitcoin trades well below its 50-day average, which sits near $75,000. The longer 200-day average has slid to the same level.

When the two averages meet, the short-term and long-term trends line up. Together they form one ceiling about $15,000 above the price. Any rally would have to climb that full distance before the trend could flip.

Trend-strength readings confirm that sellers are driving an orderly decline.

That picture sits awkwardly next to Wood's view that the low is already in. A durable bottom usually shows up as sellers losing their grip. So far, the chart shows them still firmly in charge.

Oversold Readings Hint at Exhaustion but Not Yet a Turn

The relative strength index, or RSI, is a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum. Readings below 30 signal that selling has gone too far, too fast. Bitcoin's daily RSI now sits near 18, deep in oversold territory.

Levels that stretched often come before relief bounces. Sellers tend to run out of fuel, and short-term traders step in to buy the dip. That is the one sign on the chart that lines up with Wood's view.

Exhaustion still differs from a reversal. The MACD, a tool that tracks shifts in momentum, remains below its signal line. In plain terms, downside momentum has not flipped yet.

A cross back above that line would be the first technical hint that buyers are taking over. Until it happens, oversold readings can stay oversold for weeks. Wood's bottom call needs that confirmation to hold.

With No Floor Below, Every Bounce Runs Into $75K

The data shows no marked support level beneath bitcoin right now. If selling resumes, traders have no obvious price where buyers have defended the coin before.

Overhead, the picture is clearer. First resistance sits right at the converged moving averages, the same ceiling the trend has pressed down from. Any relief bounce from oversold levels will likely meet sellers there first.

Reclaiming that zone would matter. A daily close above it would put bitcoin back over both averages and start to repair the broken trend. That would be the strongest chart evidence yet for Wood's bottom call.

Above that, the next ceiling stands near $81,000. Clearing it would open a path toward winning back a large share of last month's losses.

What Could Happen in the Next 72 Hours

Bitcoin's next three days hinge on whether oversold exhaustion turns into buying.

  • Bullish: A relief bounce carries price back to the merged averages. A daily close above that ceiling would set up a run at the next resistance. A drop back under the current price zone would cancel this setup.
  • Bearish: Sellers push price below its current level and extend the slide into territory with no mapped support. A reclaim of the moving averages would invalidate the bearish case.

The Bottom Call Still Needs the Chart's Agreement

ARK's 2030 case rests on tokenization and Wall Street adoption. The near-term trend points the other way. Sellers keep control until bitcoin closes back above that ceiling.

The risk runs to the downside first. With no mapped support beneath the price, another exchange hack or an inflation scare could drag bitcoin lower fast.

title: Bitcoin Dips Under $60,000 as Crypto Market Sinks at US Open
description:
Update, 16:08 UTC: Bitcoin extended its slide below $60,000 and dipped to about $59,000, according to CoinMarketCap data. SUMMARY ▸Bitcoin […]
The post Bitcoin Dips Under $60,000 as Crypto Market Sinks at US Open appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Update, 16:08 UTC: Bitcoin extended its slide below $60,000 and dipped to about $59,000, according to CoinMarketCap data.

SUMMARY
▸Bitcoin lost 3% in a single hour
▸Ether fell harder, sliding under $1,700
▸BlackRock’s IBIT logged a record daily outflow
▸Overnight losses hit HYPE and Zcash first

The drop came as chip stocks extended their slide after the US open, adding to a selloff that had already taken bitcoin to nearly $61,200 overnight, CoinDesk reported.

The Hour That Did Most of the Damage

As of 15:24 UTC, CoinMarketCap data showed Bitcoin at $60,079 and Ethereum at $1,672. Less than an hour earlier, CoinDesk’s live coverage still had bitcoin near $61,700, down under 1% on the day. The gap between those two readings accounts for most of Friday’s decline in the two largest cryptocurrencies.

How much of the 24-hour loss came in the last hour

CoinMarketCap data, 15:24 UTC, November 20. Shares are approximate: the last-hour change divided by the 24-hour change.

No crypto-specific headline came with the final leg down. It matched the timing of the stock market. Nvidia fell another 5% after the open to $139, leaving it about 42% below its October peak, according to CoinDesk. Anthropic, which priced its IPO at $83 and closed its first trading day at $97, had already slid about 13% to $88 in premarket trading. With the tech trade unwinding, bitcoin traded alongside chip stocks, not as a hedge against them.

Two Selloffs, Not One

The split bars show that Friday’s decline came in two separate waves. The overnight wave hit trading tokens hardest. By 10:25 a.m. ET, the CoinDesk 20 index was down 1.9% with none of its 20 members higher. Zcash had fallen 11%, NEAR 9.3%, Hyperliquid’s HYPE 7%, and Lighter and Derive 11% and 10%, according to the same CoinDesk coverage, which identified tokens tied to decentralized exchanges and derivatives platforms as among the hardest hit. Most of HYPE’s and Zcash’s daily losses were already in place before the US open.

The same morning, CoinDesk reported that the CFTC had said Hyperliquid and other onchain venues would get no special exemptions. Nothing in the reporting links that statement to the drop in derivatives tokens, but it landed on a day when that sector was already under the most pressure.

The second wave, after the open, hit the large caps. Ether lost the biggest share of its day in that hour, which is what took it below $1,700.

The Buyer That Stepped Back

Earlier dips this year met steady buying from spot ETFs. That support is now going the other way. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust recorded $541.1 million in net outflows on Thursday, its largest single-day withdrawal since launch, according to Farside Investors data cited by CoinDesk. Across all US spot bitcoin ETFs, Thursday’s net outflows topped $580 million, taking November’s total to about $3.47 billion, according to SoSoValue figures in CoinDesk’s Friday market briefing.

That briefing also noted that an argument popular earlier in the week has not played out: that money would rotate back into bitcoin once Anthropic’s record IPO was done. Instead, bitcoin is down about 28% for the quarter.

A Broad Retreat From Risk

Crypto wasn’t the only market falling. Nasdaq futures dropped more than 1% before Friday’s open as Anthropic shares retreated and hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials weighed on sentiment, Reuters reported. On Wednesday, Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC that a half-point rate hike is probably necessary at the December 8–9 meeting, saying “you might need to, like, shock people.” Waller and Governor Lisa Cook were both scheduled to speak on Friday.

Gold, often compared with bitcoin as a store of value, fell nearly 3% to about $3,514, its lowest since early September. Treasury yields fell as money moved into government bonds instead. Implied volatility rose across asset classes: the VIX reached 29.5, its highest since March, and Volmex’s bitcoin volatility index climbed to 52.2, according to CoinDesk. Reuters, cited in the same briefing, reported that Asian shares were heading for their worst week since 2020.

Who Held Up Over the Week

On a weekly view, the order looks different from Friday’s. TRON lost a small fraction of what the rest of the top ten did. XRP, despite a steeper Friday than bitcoin, is still down less than bitcoin over seven days. Speculative assets took the heaviest weekly losses: Dogecoin, Zcash, Monero and HYPE.

What Traders Are Watching Into the Weekend

The near-term schedule is short. Friday’s remarks from Waller and Cook are the last Fed comments before the weekend, and the December 8-9 meeting is now the main reference point for rate expectations. CoinDesk’s briefing noted that weekend trading may leave crypto to absorb market stress on its own, with stock markets closed and spot ETFs not trading until Monday. Sunday’s weekly close will be the first full candle to include this week’s ETF exits and Friday’s post-open drop.

The post XRP News: CME Futures Hit $81.2 Billion in 18 Months – So Why Is XRP Down 61%? appeared first on 99Bitcoins.
fullContent:
Based on the latest XRP news, CME Group said its XRP and Micro XRP futures have traded $81.2 billion in notional volume in their first 18 months. It is a sign that large US traders kept using the contracts even as the coin slumped. Notional volume is the full dollar value of the XRP behind each contract traded.

CME Group’s XRP and Micro XRP futures hit $81.2 billion in notional trading volume in their first 18 months, with 1.9 million contracts traded.@XRP @Ripple pic.twitter.com/5eUtFa2LbE

— MSB Intel (@MSBIntel) November 20, 2026

One thing stood out: the timing is awkward. XRP trades at $0.949, about 61% below the $2.43 it fetched when the futures launched in May 2025.

Traders swapped 1.9 million contracts through November 16, an average of $216 million a day, CME said. That equals about 42.8 billion XRP, roughly two-thirds of all the XRP in circulation.

We measured that total against Binance’s XRP/USDT spot pair, where traders buy and sell the coin itself, over the same 547 days. The futures traded 58% as much, and their share has grown as spot trading faded.

So who is still trading XRP, and does a busy futures market help the price?

XRP News: CME Says Its XRP Futures Lead on Open Interest

CME listed two sizes in May 2025: a standard contract for 50,000 XRP and a Micro contract for 2,500 XRP. Both settle in cash against the CME CF XRP-Dollar Reference Rate, so no coins change hands.

The first trade was a block deal cleared by Hidden Road, a prime broker Ripple has since bought, and day one brought more than $19 million in notional volume. The busiest day so far came on October 27, 2025, with 9,900 contracts.

The product line has kept growing. Options on XRP futures started trading in October 2025, and futures quoted in spot-style prices followed in December.

CME also pointed to open interest, the value of contracts still open at a given moment. Citing CoinGlass data from November 19, it said its XRP futures held about 18.5% of open interest across the exchanges tracked, the largest share of any venue.

DISCOVER: 20+ Next Crypto to Explode in 2026

Binance Spot Matched CME’s Total in Six Months, Then Slowed

To put $81.2 billion in context, we added up the daily dollar volume of Binance’s XRP/USDT pair since May 19, 2025, the day CME’s futures opened.

Binance’s pair traded $139 billion over those 18 months. CME’s futures reached 58% of that. Counted in coins, the gap is about the same: 42.8 billion XRP on CME against 70.2 billion on the Binance pair.

The real story is in the timing. Binance spot trading passed CME’s 18-month total by November 27, 2025, about six months in. It then added only $58 billion in the next 12 months.

Spot trading has dried up. The pair traded $23.3 billion in July 2025, when XRP hit its record high, and just $3.9 billion in October 2026, a drop of 83%.

CME has held up better. Its quarterly crypto report shows $10.1 billion in XRP futures and options trading in the third quarter of 2026. Binance’s pair did $14.8 billion in the same months, so CME’s suite ran at 68% of it, up from 58% across the full 18 months.

This is a comparison with one pair on one exchange, and XRP also trades against other coins and on many other platforms. Still, the trend in this XRP news points one way. More of the XRP market now runs through regulated futures, where funds can hedge or bet against the coin as easily as on it.

That is why the futures boom has not lifted the price. Every futures contract has a buyer and a seller, so heavy volume shows demand for exposure, not demand for XRP itself.

XRP Price Analysis: $1.045 Is the First Test

Other XRP news this month has been grim: the coin hit a two-year low on November 14. XRP trades at $0.949, down 4.6% in 24 hours and 30% in a month. It sits below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1.19, and its 200-day EMA at $1.31.

  • Resistance: $1.045, the June to August floor that now acts as a ceiling. Above that, $1.185, where XRP turned lower in June and July.
  • Support: $0.893, the November 14 low and XRP’s lowest price in two years.

XRPUSDT 1D chart. Source: TradingView

Path What has to happen Next stop
Push higher A daily close above $1.045 $1.185, the June and July turning point
Stall Price stays between $0.893 and $1.045 A base near the November low
Slip A daily close below $0.893 $0.60 to $0.70, where XRP traded before its November 2024 breakout

The CME milestone is good XRP news for the market’s plumbing. The chart is another matter. For traders, the next clue is whether $0.893 holds while the futures crowd keeps trading both sides.

title: Binance Hackers Move Nearly $600M in Ethereum Through THORChain
description: Wallets linked to the $6.3 billion Binance hack saw the Binance hackers move approximately $594 million worth of Ethereum over two days, routing portions of the stolen assets through cross-chain protocols THORChain and Chainflip. The latest activity highlights how attackers continue to move funds across blockchain networks, complicating efforts to trace and potentially recover the […]
fullContent:
Wallets linked to the $6.3 billion Binance hack saw the Binance hackers move approximately $594 million worth of Ethereum over two days, routing portions of the stolen assets through cross-chain protocols THORChain and Chainflip. The latest activity highlights how attackers continue to move funds across blockchain networks, complicating efforts to trace and potentially recover the stolen cryptocurrency.

According to blockchain data provider Onchain Lens, the attackers transferred approximately $248 million in ETH on Thursday, followed by another 197,460 ETH worth around $346 million on Friday. The funds were sent to newly created wallets, with some subsequently moving through cross-chain swapping services.

Blockchain analyst SomaXBT estimated that approximately $5 million passed through Chainflip, while THORChain handled most of the cross-chain activity identified in the transfers. The movements come as investigators continue monitoring wallets associated with the Binance exploit.

THORChain Handles Most of the Tracked Cross-Chain Activity

The latest transfers involved two cross-chain protocols, but the reported amounts suggest that their roles were considerably different.

SomaXBT estimated that only around $5 million of the funds moved through Chainflip, with THORChain accounting for the majority of the cross-chain activity he tracked. Onchain analyst Specter similarly described the amount passing through Chainflip as a relatively small portion of the overall transfers.

THORChain has faced similar scrutiny because of its previous use in laundering funds associated with significant crypto exploits. Its decentralized cross-chain infrastructure allows users to swap assets across different networks, making it a relevant route for attackers seeking to move cryptocurrency between blockchains.

Binance Hackers Still Hold Nearly $400M in Tracked ETH

Despite moving approximately $594 million over two days, the attackers appear to retain a substantial Ethereum balance.

Data from blockchain analytics platform Arkham showed that publicly tracked addresses associated with the Binance hackers held approximately 224,722 ETH following the latest transfers. At the reported valuation, the remaining balance was worth around $394 million.

The figure represents the ETH held in the identified addresses and should not be interpreted as the total value of all assets connected to the attack. Funds previously moved into other cryptocurrencies or through additional wallets may not be reflected in that balance.

The Binance incident has also been linked to North Korean cybercriminal activity. Blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have associated the $6.3 billion hack with TraderTraitor, a hacking group linked to North Korea.

The group has previously been connected to major cryptocurrency thefts, making the ongoing movement of funds particularly relevant to blockchain investigators and security firms monitoring illicit transactions.

THORChain Activity Surges as Hack-Linked Transfers Continue

The movement of stolen funds has also coincided with a sharp increase in THORChain’s transaction activity.

According to the protocol’s dashboard, its 24-hour swap volume reached approximately $239 million on Friday. Protocol earnings climbed to around $243,000 during the same period. The increase comes as THORChain continues to attract attention over its role in cross-chain transactions involving assets linked to major cryptocurrency exploits.

The protocol has previously been used to move funds connected to other high-profile attacks. These include the $1.4 billion Bybit hack in February 2025 and the $388 million Bitget exploit in September 2026, both of which have been associated with North Korean hackers.

The latest Binance-related activity adds another example of how cross-chain infrastructure can become part of the movement of stolen digital assets. While such protocols serve legitimate purposes by enabling transfers between blockchain networks, their permissionless features can also create challenges for tracking suspicious transactions.

For now, analysts continue monitoring the remaining ETH balances and the movement of funds through cross-chain services. Whether additional transfers will follow, and how much of the stolen cryptocurrency can ultimately be traced or recovered, remains uncertain.

Do you think decentralized cross-chain protocols should introduce stronger safeguards against transactions involving stolen cryptocurrency? Could the latest Binance-related transfers lead to greater scrutiny of THORChain and other cross-chain services?

title: XRP Price Is 4% From a Line That Has Held Since 2020
description:

The post XRP Price Is 4% From a Line That Has Held Since 2020 appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

1Bounce to $1 faded, price near $0.94
2Channel floor sits between $0.85 and $0.90
3A bounce faces $1, then $1.15-$1.50
4Weekly close under the rail opens $0.75

Coindoo’s November 11 XRP analysis laid out a path from $0.99 down to a weekly support band. The first step of that path is done, and the weekly chart now shows what the second step would test.

Nine Days, One Lost Floor

MarkerNov 11Nov 20
XRP priceAbout $1.05About $0.94
$0.99 daily floorBeing defendedLost
Weekly candle low$1.03$0.93
$0.84–$0.90 bandNot in reachNot yet reached

The daily level failed first. Once $0.99 went, the next reference was the weekly band the earlier piece had already marked, and nothing in between has slowed the decline.

This week’s candle shows how the old floor now behaves. XRP opened the week near $0.97, reached $1.0066 and then fell back. With two and a half days left in the candle when the chart was captured, it was trading at $0.9382, down 3.65% on the week and close to its low of $0.9323. Buyers did not hold $1 even once on the way back up. That makes $1 the first ceiling any rebound would have to clear, where it used to be a floor.

Bitcoin Set the Pace

XRP’s slide has tracked Bitcoin’s. On November 19, Bitcoin fell to $61,800, its lowest price since early July, as a stock selloff deepened into the close and the Nasdaq and Dow each lost 2.1%, CoinDesk reported. That put Bitcoin on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, and XRP stayed under $1 through the session. Bitcoin has since retested $61,500, the zone it lost in June. With the market leader still making new lows, XRP’s supports are being tested by market-wide selling, not by anything specific to XRP.

Zooming Out to the Six-Year Channel

The November 11 piece counted the rising trendline from the 2020 lows as one of four supports. On the weekly chart, that trendline is the lower rail of a full channel, and the rest of the channel adds context.

The lower rail caught XRP’s lows in 2020, 2022, 2023 and 2024, and the November 2024 breakout started from it. The upper rail touched the late-2021 highs and capped the 2025 run at the $3.66 peak. XRP spent most of 2025 in the upper half of that range. Since the peak, it has fallen inside a smaller descending channel. It lost the dashed midline of the larger channel, and the August–October rebound briefly lifted it back above that midline. The rebound stalled at the descending channel’s upper rail and the falling 50-week average, above $1.50, and price has dropped from there into this week.

The descending channel’s lower rail meets the six-year channel’s lower rail close to the same $0.85-$0.90 zone. If XRP gets there, both structures will be tested at once.

The lines on the chart, and where each stands

AVERAGES AND ZONES

 What Still Works Against a Rebound

All three weekly averages sit above price. The 50-week, near $1.41 at the November 11 reading, is clearly sloping down. The 200-week, near $1.28, has flattened. The 100-week, near $1.96, has started to turn lower. A rebound from the channel floor would run into all three on the way up.

Momentum hasn’t turned either. Weekly RSI is in the lower part of its range and below its own moving average. The August bounce lifted it above that average, but the reading has fallen back since then and shows no upturn yet. The shaded bands on the chart are the Fibonacci levels from the earlier article, and the lowest of them, near $0.87, sits inside the channel-floor zone.

Distance from $0.94

$1.50 rebound top+60%
$1.28 200-week+36%
$1.15 rebound start+23%
$1.00 rejected high+7%
$0.90 band top−4%
$0.85 band base−9%
$0.84 last average−10%
$0.75 lower band−20%

Two Ways the Weekly Closes Can Read

If the floor answers

Trigger: weekly candles hold the rising lower rail around $0.85–$0.90 and turn higher.

First test: $1, this week’s rejected high.

Room above: a counter-trend move toward $1.15–$1.50 while the six-year channel stays intact.

If the floor gives way

Trigger: a decisive weekly close below the rising lower rail.

Last line: under $0.84, no average or trendline from the November 11 map remains below price.

Room below: the lower horizontal bands open, $0.75 and below, outside a channel XRP has traded in since 2020.

The upside range is wider than it looks. The 200-week average near $1.28 sits inside it, and the November 11 analysis treated any rebound that stalls below that line as a recovery within a downtrend. The top of the range, around $1.50, is roughly where the August–October bounce gave out, and the 0.618 retracement sits near $1.47. Reaching $1.15 would be a rebound. Holding above $1.28 would be the first change in the weekly structure.

The setup is awkward for both sides. Sellers have already taken XRP from above $1.50 to $0.94, and opening new shorts just above a six-year trendline means betting against a level that has stopped every major decline since 2020. Buying before a weekly candle confirms a hold means risking that this is the time the trendline breaks, with Bitcoin still printing new lows.

The Two Closes on the Calendar

Sunday, November 22 · weekly close
Monday, November 30 · monthly close

Sunday’s candle will show whether this week ends at its lows or with a rejection wick off them. The monthly close will show where November finishes relative to a band that sat 15% below price when the month’s analysis began. Until a weekly candle closes inside or below the $0.85–$0.90 zone, the six-year channel has not been tested, only approached.

title: Unrig: A Prediction Market Protocol That Needs No Liquidity and Can't Be Rigged
description:
Introduction
Unrig is a prediction market protocol built on Ethereum. It enables counterparties to emerge naturally without any liquidity provision, and eliminates any room for profitable manipulation within its trading mechanism. The first removes the fundamental constraint that prediction markets have lived with since their inception, turning them from a product bounded by liquidity into general-purpose infrastructure for all of humanity’s judgments about the future. The second proves, for the first time in financial history, that a continuously traded market can make manipulation unprofitable through its mathematical properties alone, without relying on any sustained effort from external regulators.
Consider the simplest possible prediction market: those who predicted correctly take the funds of those who predicted incorrectly, in proportion to what they staked. In practice, such a model cannot work at all. Bets placed at different times face very different levels of risk, and if everyone receives the same return no matter when they enter, everyone will wait until the outcome is certain before betting. No counterparties form, and no market can exist. Existing designs solve this with arbitrage driven by price movements, but that requires a market to keep generating enough capital inflow and trading activity — and so the limits of liquidity become the limits of where prediction markets can exist. Unrig does not take that route. It directly measures the real risk each participant bears and makes returns precisely commensurate with risk. Even if a market has only a handful of participants from start to finish and its price barely moves, it still works normally. As a result, on any topic and at any time, a prediction market exists as soon as someone is willing to act.
Manipulation has existed for as long as financial markets have, because every form of it shares the same driver: the manipulator can profit from it. Existing anti-manipulation efforts focus on detecting and blocking specific techniques, but they run into a fundamental dilemma: from the outside, manipulation and normal trading look the same. A large buy followed immediately by a sale could be a pump-and-dump, or simply a change of mind. The outward behavior is identical; only the motive differs, and no system can observe motive. As long as manipulation can be profitable, it will continue, however advanced anti-manipulation tools become. Unrig does not try to block specific techniques. Instead, its mathematical structure removes the possibility of profit itself: each participant’s return is calculated strictly by formula from the real risk they bear, manipulators cannot create any return for themselves beyond what the formula gives them, and the cost of carrying out manipulation is strictly positive. A manipulator can still take any action, but no action will make them a profit. This is not because manipulation is blocked, but because no one has any reason to do it.
After a market expires, who won and who lost must be determined accurately. This is the premise everything rests on: if it fails, everything collapses. Once the liquidity constraint is removed and the number of markets is no longer capped, outcome determination has to keep up with that scale. Unrig has redesigned outcome determination from the ground up as well — built for an unlimited number of markets, and more reliable than any existing approach.
This paper sets out in full the mathematical structure and logic of risk pricing, proves rigorously that manipulators cannot profit, and describes in detail the settlement process, the market creation rules, the outcome determination system, the Community Sovereign Voting mechanism, the economics of the $UNRIG token, the referral distribution network, the ethical boundaries of markets, and contract security and permissions.
Chapter 1: Counterparty Formation
For counterparties to form, someone has to be willing to bet first.
People will act first if the risk of acting first earns a commensurate return. But for that return to reach those who acted first, two further conditions must hold: late capital cannot touch the returns of those who acted first, and losers cannot take winners’ money.
Unrig has designed two mechanisms for this: the risk duration integral (T_acc), and continuous integral pricing for early exits. Both rely on the same number: the option’s market probability p, the share of all capital in the market that is staked on that option. The share staked on the other side, 1 − p, is the probability that you lose your principal at this moment — the risk you bear. T_acc adds up that risk second by second, and returns are distributed according to the total: every second of risk borne by those who acted first is already recorded, and even if the outcome is already determined before the market expires, late capital cannot touch it. Exits settle at p: for each unit of principal you exit, you take back only p, and the lower the probability, the heavier the penalty. Losers cannot take winners’ money.
The rest of this chapter sets out the two mechanisms and shows why manipulators cannot profit within this structure.
1.1 Risk Duration Integral (T_acc)
Each option maintains a variable, T_acc, which grows at the following rate:
T_acc increment per second = (1 − p) ÷ W

W is the total principal of all current positions on the option, M is the total current principal across all options in the market, and p = W ÷ M is the option’s market probability. 1 − p is the share of capital staked on the other side, where the other side means every other option.
Every second, a position accumulates allocation weight equal to the risk it bears. The numerator, 1 − p, is the risk, and it is also the weight its side issues each second. The denominator, W, determines how that weight is divided: the weight issued in a given second is shared among all positions on that side in proportion to principal, so the more principal there is to share it, the less each unit of principal receives.
When you enter, the current value of T_acc is recorded as your entry snapshot. When the market expires, the system locks the final value of T_acc for each option. The final value minus your entry snapshot is the risk duration integral you have accumulated. Your allocation weight is:
Allocation Weight = Principal × Risk Duration Integral

Consider the case where the outcome is already determined before the market expires but betting is still open. Capital that rushes into the winning option at this point is betting on a known outcome. Even so, it cannot touch the weight that those who acted first have already accumulated. The weight for every past second is already recorded; new capital can only accumulate from the moment it arrives, and no amount of money can buy seconds that have already passed. Beyond that, the inflow itself pushes the weight issued in each second after its arrival toward zero: it drives its own side’s p toward 1, so 1 − p approaches zero, and it adds to W, so more principal now shares that weight. However large the inflow, the share it can obtain as a whole is capped, and that share shrinks toward zero as the inflow keeps growing.
Allocation weight can only be determined when the market expires. Your entry snapshot is locked when you bet, but how fast T_acc grows while you hold depends on every participant entering and exiting, on your side and on the other side.
1.2 Early Exit and Penalty Pricing
Before the market expires, any position can be exited early at any time. For each unit of principal exited, you take back p and leave 1 − p behind. By the market’s judgment at that moment, the unit stays with you with probability p and goes to the other side with probability 1 − p; an exit settles only the part that is yours. The 1 − p left behind is the penalty, and it goes to all winners.
Unrig applies continuous integral pricing to exit penalties: the exit amount is treated as infinitely many infinitesimal elements, each priced at its own instantaneous probability. Every portion exited lowers the option’s probability, so exiting the rest costs more.
Let the exit amount be h; before the exit, let the option’s principal be W, the market’s total principal be M, and the other side’s principal B = M − W. The instantaneous probability after s has been exited is:
p(s) = (W − s) ÷ (M − s)

The net proceeds from each infinitesimal element ds are p(s) · ds. Integrating from 0 to h:
Net Proceeds = h − B · ln(M ÷ (M − h))
Total Penalty = B · ln(M ÷ (M − h))

Path independence. The total penalty does not depend on how an exit is split. Split h into two exits, one after the other: when the second begins, W and M have each been reduced by the amount of the first while B is unchanged, so its integration interval picks up exactly where the first left off, and the two together equal a single integral from 0 to h. Exit all at once, in ten installments, or from ten different addresses — the total penalty is the same.
Loser lock-in. As an option’s probability approaches zero, the penalty rate approaches 100%.
1.3 Why Manipulators Cannot Profit
The risk pricing mechanism and the exit penalty mechanism together ensure that the return on every unit of capital is determined strictly by the risk it bears, and the cost of every exit is determined strictly by the state of the market. Both take only objective variables as inputs; neither identifies participants nor judges intent.
In this system, every position held by every participant has only two possible endings: early exit, or holding to settlement. An early exit means paying a penalty, so the net proceeds are strictly less than what was put in — a certain loss. Holding to settlement means the return is determined entirely by whether the prediction was correct and how much risk was borne — that is honest participation. There is no third path. Take the most typical manipulation from traditional markets, as it would play out here: buying heavily while the probability is low, then pushing the probability up to draw in followers. The manipulator, too, must eventually leave through one of these two exits, and neither offers an excess return.
These rules do not depend on detecting manipulation, because manipulation and normal behavior cannot be told apart from the outside. Nor do they depend on oversight or enforcement by any central authority: every rule is written into immutable code on the blockchain and enforced automatically, equally and without exception for all participants, and no one can open a back door for anyone. Within this structure, manipulation is unprofitable. This is not because it is blocked, but because no one has any reason to do it.
Chapter 2: Settlement
When the market expires and the outcome is known, settlement begins. Allocation weights accumulate in real time while the market is open and are locked the moment it expires; once the outcome is known, how much each person receives is fully determined.
Settlement follows a strict flow of funds: total up the fund pool, return all of the winning side’s principal first, treat the remainder as the profit pool, take a 15% protocol fee from the profit pool, and finally distribute the remaining profit to the winning side by allocation weight. The stages run in a fixed order that cannot be reversed, and funds are never mixed between stages. The winning side’s principal is fully set aside before any fee is taken — anyone who predicted correctly and held to settlement cannot lose money by participating.
The full amount of every bet goes into the option’s pool; no fee is deducted on entry. When the market expires, the principal still remaining in each option, plus the total penalties paid by all early exiters while the market was open, constitutes the total fund pool — all of the funds available for distribution.
Total Fund Pool = sum of all options' current remaining principal + Penalty Pool

The first step of settlement is to return the winning side’s principal. Each winner gets back the full current principal of their position in the winning option. Principal in the losing options is not returned; together with the penalty pool, it makes up the profit pool.
Profit Pool = Total Fund Pool − all winning-side principal
Protocol Fee = Profit Pool × 15%

The protocol fee is split among four parties in fixed proportions: creator 30%, staking pool 40%, Protocol Treasury 25%, Founding Team 5%. Where a market has promoters, the promoter receives 15% of the protocol fee and 5% of the $UNRIG minted, in proportion to the promoter weight ratio defined in Chapter 7, and the creator’s corresponding shares are reduced accordingly.
After the protocol fee is taken, the remaining profit is distributed among all holders of the winning option by allocation weight.
Distributable Profit = Profit Pool − Protocol Fee
Individual Profit Distribution = individual allocation weight ÷ total allocation weight of all winners × Distributable Profit

Allocation weight was fully defined in Chapter 1 as the product of principal and the risk duration integral. At settlement, this weight is used directly to distribute profit. Each winner’s net payout is their principal repayment plus their profit distribution.
Individual Net Payout = Principal Repayment + Profit Distribution

Each user can claim only once per market. Everything owed remains claimable indefinitely.
