The first removes the fundamental constraint that prediction markets have lived with since their inception, turning them from a product bounded by liquidity into general-purpose infrastructure for all of humanity’s judgments about the future. The second proves, for the first time in financial history, that a continuously traded market can make manipulation unprofitable through its mathematical properties alone, without relying on any sustained effort from external regulators.

Consider the simplest possible prediction market: those who predicted correctly take the funds of those who predicted incorrectly, in proportion to what they staked. In practice, such a model cannot work at all. Bets placed at different times face very different levels of risk, and if everyone receives the same return no matter when they enter, everyone will wait until the outcome is certain before betting. No counterparties form, and no market can exist. Existing designs solve this with arbitrage driven by price movements, but that requires a market to keep generating enough capital inflow and trading activity — and so the limits of liquidity become the limits of where prediction markets can exist. Unrig does not take that route. It directly measures the real risk each participant bears and makes returns precisely commensurate with risk. Even if a market has only a handful of participants from start to finish and its price barely moves, it still works normally. As a result, on any topic and at any time, a prediction market exists as soon as someone is willing to act.

Manipulation has existed for as long as financial markets have, because every form of it shares the same driver: the manipulator can profit from it. Existing anti-manipulation efforts focus on detecting and blocking specific techniques, but they run into a fundamental dilemma: from the outside, manipulation and normal trading look the same. A large buy followed immediately by a sale could be a pump-and-dump, or simply a change of mind. The outward behavior is identical; only the motive differs, and no system can observe motive. As long as manipulation can be profitable, it will continue, however advanced anti-manipulation tools become. Unrig does not try to block specific techniques. Instead, its mathematical structure removes the possibility of profit itself: each participant’s return is calculated strictly by formula from the real risk they bear, manipulators cannot create any return for themselves beyond what the formula gives them, and the cost of carrying out manipulation is strictly positive. A manipulator can still take any action, but no action will make them a profit. This is not because manipulation is blocked, but because no one has any reason to do it.

After a market expires, who won and who lost must be determined accurately. This is the premise everything rests on: if it fails, everything collapses. Once the liquidity constraint is removed and the number of markets is no longer capped, outcome determination has to keep up with that scale. Unrig has redesigned outcome determination from the ground up as well — built for an unlimited number of markets, and more reliable than any existing approach.

This paper sets out in full the mathematical structure and logic of risk pricing, proves rigorously that manipulators cannot profit, and describes in detail the settlement process, the market creation rules, the outcome determination system, the Community Sovereign Voting mechanism, the economics of the $UNRIG token, the referral distribution network, the ethical boundaries of markets, and contract security and permissions.

Chapter 1: Counterparty Formation

For counterparties to form, someone has to be willing to bet first.

People will act first if the risk of acting first earns a commensurate return. But for that return to reach those who acted first, two further conditions must hold: late capital cannot touch the returns of those who acted first, and losers cannot take winners’ money.

Unrig has designed two mechanisms for this: the risk duration integral (T_acc), and continuous integral pricing for early exits. Both rely on the same number: the option’s market probability p, the share of all capital in the market that is staked on that option. The share staked on the other side, 1 − p, is the probability that you lose your principal at this moment — the risk you bear. T_acc adds up that risk second by second, and returns are distributed according to the total: every second of risk borne by those who acted first is already recorded, and even if the outcome is already determined before the market expires, late capital cannot touch it. Exits settle at p: for each unit of principal you exit, you take back only p, and the lower the probability, the heavier the penalty. Losers cannot take winners’ money.

The rest of this chapter sets out the two mechanisms and shows why manipulators cannot profit within this structure.

1.1 Risk Duration Integral (T_acc)

Each option maintains a variable, T_acc, which grows at the following rate:

T_acc increment per second = (1 − p) ÷ W

W is the total principal of all current positions on the option, M is the total current principal across all options in the market, and p = W ÷ M is the option’s market probability. 1 − p is the share of capital staked on the other side, where the other side means every other option.

Every second, a position accumulates allocation weight equal to the risk it bears. The numerator, 1 − p, is the risk, and it is also the weight its side issues each second. The denominator, W, determines how that weight is divided: the weight issued in a given second is shared among all positions on that side in proportion to principal, so the more principal there is to share it, the less each unit of principal receives.

When you enter, the current value of T_acc is recorded as your entry snapshot. When the market expires, the system locks the final value of T_acc for each option. The final value minus your entry snapshot is the risk duration integral you have accumulated. Your allocation weight is:

Allocation Weight = Principal × Risk Duration Integral

Consider the case where the outcome is already determined before the market expires but betting is still open. Capital that rushes into the winning option at this point is betting on a known outcome. Even so, it cannot touch the weight that those who acted first have already accumulated. The weight for every past second is already recorded; new capital can only accumulate from the moment it arrives, and no amount of money can buy seconds that have already passed. Beyond that, the inflow itself pushes the weight issued in each second after its arrival toward zero: it drives its own side’s p toward 1, so 1 − p approaches zero, and it adds to W, so more principal now shares that weight. However large the inflow, the share it can obtain as a whole is capped, and that share shrinks toward zero as the inflow keeps growing.

Allocation weight can only be determined when the market expires. Your entry snapshot is locked when you bet, but how fast T_acc grows while you hold depends on every participant entering and exiting, on your side and on the other side.

1.2 Early Exit and Penalty Pricing

Before the market expires, any position can be exited early at any time. For each unit of principal exited, you take back p and leave 1 − p behind. By the market’s judgment at that moment, the unit stays with you with probability p and goes to the other side with probability 1 − p; an exit settles only the part that is yours. The 1 − p left behind is the penalty, and it goes to all winners.

Unrig applies continuous integral pricing to exit penalties: the exit amount is treated as infinitely many infinitesimal elements, each priced at its own instantaneous probability. Every portion exited lowers the option’s probability, so exiting the rest costs more.

Let the exit amount be h; before the exit, let the option’s principal be W, the market’s total principal be M, and the other side’s principal B = M − W. The instantaneous probability after s has been exited is:

p(s) = (W − s) ÷ (M − s)

The net proceeds from each infinitesimal element ds are p(s) · ds. Integrating from 0 to h:

Net Proceeds = h − B · ln(M ÷ (M − h))
Total Penalty = B · ln(M ÷ (M − h))

Path independence. The total penalty does not depend on how an exit is split. Split h into two exits, one after the other: when the second begins, W and M have each been reduced by the amount of the first while B is unchanged, so its integration interval picks up exactly where the first left off, and the two together equal a single integral from 0 to h. Exit all at once, in ten installments, or from ten different addresses — the total penalty is the same.

Loser lock-in. As an option’s probability approaches zero, the penalty rate approaches 100%.

1.3 Why Manipulators Cannot Profit

The risk pricing mechanism and the exit penalty mechanism together ensure that the return on every unit of capital is determined strictly by the risk it bears, and the cost of every exit is determined strictly by the state of the market. Both take only objective variables as inputs; neither identifies participants nor judges intent.

In this system, every position held by every participant has only two possible endings: early exit, or holding to settlement. An early exit means paying a penalty, so the net proceeds are strictly less than what was put in — a certain loss. Holding to settlement means the return is determined entirely by whether the prediction was correct and how much risk was borne — that is honest participation. There is no third path. Take the most typical manipulation from traditional markets, as it would play out here: buying heavily while the probability is low, then pushing the probability up to draw in followers. The manipulator, too, must eventually leave through one of these two exits, and neither offers an excess return.

These rules do not depend on detecting manipulation, because manipulation and normal behavior cannot be told apart from the outside. Nor do they depend on oversight or enforcement by any central authority: every rule is written into immutable code on the blockchain and enforced automatically, equally and without exception for all participants, and no one can open a back door for anyone. Within this structure, manipulation is unprofitable. This is not because it is blocked, but because no one has any reason to do it.

Chapter 2: Settlement

When the market expires and the outcome is known, settlement begins. Allocation weights accumulate in real time while the market is open and are locked the moment it expires; once the outcome is known, how much each person receives is fully determined.

Settlement follows a strict flow of funds: total up the fund pool, return all of the winning side’s principal first, treat the remainder as the profit pool, take a 15% protocol fee from the profit pool, and finally distribute the remaining profit to the winning side by allocation weight. The stages run in a fixed order that cannot be reversed, and funds are never mixed between stages. The winning side’s principal is fully set aside before any fee is taken — anyone who predicted correctly and held to settlement cannot lose money by participating.

The full amount of every bet goes into the option’s pool; no fee is deducted on entry. When the market expires, the principal still remaining in each option, plus the total penalties paid by all early exiters while the market was open, constitutes the total fund pool — all of the funds available for distribution.

Total Fund Pool = sum of all options' current remaining principal + Penalty Pool

The first step of settlement is to return the winning side’s principal. Each winner gets back the full current principal of their position in the winning option. Principal in the losing options is not returned; together with the penalty pool, it makes up the profit pool.

Profit Pool = Total Fund Pool − all winning-side principal
Protocol Fee = Profit Pool × 15%

The protocol fee is split among four parties in fixed proportions: creator 30%, staking pool 40%, Protocol Treasury 25%, Founding Team 5%. Where a market has promoters, the promoter receives 15% of the protocol fee and 5% of the $UNRIG minted, in proportion to the promoter weight ratio defined in Chapter 7, and the creator’s corresponding shares are reduced accordingly.

After the protocol fee is taken, the remaining profit is distributed among all holders of the winning option by allocation weight.

Distributable Profit = Profit Pool − Protocol Fee
Individual Profit Distribution = individual allocation weight ÷ total allocation weight of all winners × Distributable Profit

Allocation weight was fully defined in Chapter 1 as the product of principal and the risk duration integral. At settlement, this weight is used directly to distribute profit. Each winner’s net payout is their principal repayment plus their profit distribution.

Individual Net Payout = Principal Repayment + Profit Distribution

Each user can claim only once per market. Everything owed remains claimable indefinitely.

title: Ethereum’s New DeFi Security Tool Sparks Debate Over Censorship Risks
description: Ethereum’s new Defi security tool system is designed to prevent decentralized finance (DeFi) exploits before they settle but is raising questions about how far transaction filtering should go on Ethereum. Developed by Phylax and integrated with block builder Titan Builder, the technology allows applications to block transactions that could cause harmful outcomes. The system could […]
fullContent:
Ethereum’s new Defi security tool system is designed to prevent decentralized finance (DeFi) exploits before they settle but is raising questions about how far transaction filtering should go on Ethereum.

Developed by Phylax and integrated with block builder Titan Builder, the technology allows applications to block transactions that could cause harmful outcomes. The system could help protocols defend against hackers and prevent significant financial losses. However, it also introduces a potential mechanism for freezing smart contract functions, prompting concerns about whether a security measure could eventually become a tool for censorship or centralized control.

The debate comes as Ethereum continues to address vulnerabilities across its DeFi ecosystem while facing questions about the concentration of power among a relatively small number of block builders.

Phylax Introduces Circuit Breakers to Stop DeFi Exploits

Announced on November 10, Phylax’s integration with Titan Builder allows Ethereum applications to establish rules that filter out potentially harmful transactions during block construction.

Titan checks transactions against these rules before deciding whether to include them in its blocks. Phylax says Titan produces approximately one in every two Ethereum blocks, giving the integration significant reach across the network. The objective is to prevent exploits from being finalized rather than relying on monitoring tools or emergency responses after an attack has already begun.

Phylax illustrated the system’s potential using a vulnerable DeFi vault that could mistakenly release $1 million to a user whose shares were worth only $1,000. A circuit breaker could impose a limit on the amount leaving the vault in a single transaction, preventing the funds from being drained.

Similar protections could potentially reduce losses in major incidents, including the reported $6.3 billion Binance hack and the $380 million Bitget exploit. In both cases, attackers were able to drain substantial amounts of cryptocurrency and move funds through decentralized protocols.

Fail-Open Settings Could Reduce the Risk of Frozen Contracts

Phylax founder and CEO Odysseas Lamtzidis says protocols can limit the possibility of a freeze by allowing transactions to proceed even when the security system is unavailable.

The company recommends a configuration known as fail-open behavior. Under this approach, a protocol does not automatically block transactions simply because the security checks cannot be completed.

Shapiro argued that fail-open protections should be mandatory rather than left to individual protocol decisions. He also suggested introducing time delays before security settings can be changed, preventing safeguards from being removed immediately.

The disagreement highlights a central challenge for DeFi developers: a system that blocks suspicious transactions may protect users from exploits, but the same mechanism could interrupt legitimate activity if its safeguards are unavailable or configured too restrictively.

Ethereum’s Concentrated Builder Market Raises Further Concerns

Beyond the possibility of frozen applications, researchers have questioned whether Phylax’s integration could reinforce the concentration of power within Ethereum’s block-building market.

Ethereum researcher Fan Zhang said the technology has become practical partly because the builder market is already concentrated. While he acknowledged its potential security advantages, particularly as AI-powered tools become more capable of identifying software vulnerabilities, he warned that the approach could introduce additional risks.

Ethereum researcher Sen Yang similarly warned that if major protocols rely on a small number of builders to enforce security rules, those builders could gain a competitive advantage and further strengthen their market position.

Ethereum’s proposed enshrined proposer-builder separation (ePBS), which is slated for the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade, could reduce reliance on third-party relays. However, Yang noted that the proposal does not directly address the concentration of block builders.

Where Should Ethereum Draw the Line Between Security and Censorship?

Phylax maintains that its system does not give an outside authority control over Ethereum transactions because the filtering rules are established by the applications choosing to use it.

Lamtzidis described the technology as explicitly opt-in and compared its checks to conditions already embedded in smart contracts. From his perspective, censorship involves arbitrary decisions or coercion, whereas Phylax’s system applies rules selected by individual applications.

Stefanie Boss, co-author of research on censorship resistance and compliance behavior in Ethereum’s consensus mechanism, considers the security trade-off potentially acceptable. She noted that rules based on transaction outcomes may carry less risk than rules targeting specific users or participants.

Phylax’s system offers one possible approach, but its long-term implications will depend on how protocols configure the safeguards, how builders participate, and whether the broader Ethereum ecosystem can prevent security improvements from reinforcing existing centralization risks.

Do you think Phylax’s transaction-filtering system represents a necessary improvement to DeFi security, or could it create new censorship risks for Ethereum users? Should fail-open protections be mandatory for protocols adopting this type of technology?

title: Ripple Price Analysis: Silver Lining Emerges After XRP’s Brutal 32% Monthly Collapse
description: Ripple’s XRP is holding near $0.96 after its rebound from $0.89 failed to sustain a move above $1.00. The consolidation suggests that selling has slowed, but buyers still need to overcome nearby resistance to turn stabilization into a broader recovery. Ripple Price Analysis: The Daily Chart The daily chart shows XRP consolidating after a steep […]
fullContent:
Ripple’s XRP is holding near $0.96 after its rebound from $0.89 failed to sustain a move above $1.00. The consolidation suggests that selling has slowed, but buyers still need to overcome nearby resistance to turn stabilization into a broader recovery.

Ripple Price Analysis: The Daily Chart

The daily chart shows XRP consolidating after a steep decline from the $1.20–$1.34 main supply zone. The initial recovery from approximately $0.89 reached the psychological $1 level, but subsequent candles have struggled to extend higher, leaving price around $0.96.

Smaller candle bodies indicate a pause in the bearish impulse rather than a confirmed reversal. The broader sequence of lower highs and lower lows remains intact, while the daily RSI is hovering around the oversold threshold near 30. Momentum has improved from its extreme low, although the recovery remains weak.

The $0.99–$1.01 region is the first important resistance area. Sustained acceptance above it would improve the prospects of a corrective rally toward the previous breakdown area around $1.03–$1.08. However, the larger $1.20–$1.34 supply zone remains the main structural obstacle farther overhead.

On the downside, the recent consolidation lows around $0.94–$0.95 provide immediate support. Losing this area would increase the likelihood of another test of $0.89–$0.91. A decisive break beneath the recent low would confirm a continuation of the broader downtrend.

XRP/USDT 4-Hour Chart

The four-hour chart shows XRP building a short-term range following its sharp rebound from the lows. Buyers have repeatedly defended approximately $0.94–$0.95, while recovery attempts toward $0.99–$1 have attracted selling.

The latest rejection has returned price toward the lower portion of that range. Meanwhile, the four-hour RSI has slipped below 50 after briefly recovering above it, suggesting that the improvement in bullish momentum has faded.

A sustained breakout above $1 would interrupt the immediate pattern of failed recoveries and bring the marked $1.03–$1.08 supply zone into focus. Reclaiming that zone would provide stronger evidence that buyers are gaining control beyond the current consolidation.

Conversely, a confirmed close beneath $0.94 would weaken the developing base and expose $0.91, followed by the $0.89 low. Until XRP clears the range highs, the sideways action remains vulnerable to becoming another pause before bearish continuation.

title: Bitcoin drops to near 5-month low below $62k as AI rout batters risk appetite
Bitcoin Price Analysis: Is a Drop Below $60K Next After BTC’s Latest Rejection?
description: Bitcoin remains under pressure near $61.8K after losing another daily support zone. Deeply oversold momentum leaves room for a relief rally, but buyers have yet to interrupt the bearish structure as price approaches major demand around $60K. Bitcoin Price Analysis: The Daily Chart The daily chart shows a sustained decline following Bitcoin’s rejection from the […]
fullContent:
Bitcoin remains under pressure near $61.8K after losing another daily support zone. Deeply oversold momentum leaves room for a relief rally, but buyers have yet to interrupt the bearish structure as price approaches major demand around $60K.

Bitcoin Price Analysis: The Daily Chart

The daily chart shows a sustained decline following Bitcoin’s rejection from the $77.5K–$81K supply zone. Selling accelerated through the $67.8K–$70K demand area, and price has now slipped beneath the former support band around $62.2K–$63.7K.

This latest breakdown leaves the $57.8K–$60K demand zone as the next significant support area. The zone contains the June lows and could attract buying interest, although the current sequence of lower highs and lower lows suggests that sellers retain control.

The daily RSI is hovering near 20, reflecting deeply oversold conditions. This creates scope for a corrective bounce, but does not confirm exhaustion. Recent candles have yet to show the sustained bullish follow-through needed to support a reversal.

Reclaiming $62.2K–$63.7K would be the first meaningful improvement and could allow a recovery toward $64K–$65.5K. Conversely, continued rejection beneath former support would keep a test of $60K in focus. A decisive loss of the lower demand zone would signal further deterioration.

BTC/USDT 4-Hour Chart

On the four-hour timeframe, Bitcoin continues to form lower highs, with the latest recovery toward $64K followed by another decline toward $61K–$62K. Smaller candles near the lows indicate a pause in selling, but there is no clear bullish structure shift yet.

The immediate downside reference is the recent low around $61.1K–$61.3K. Losing this area would expose the upper boundary of demand near $60K, followed by the remainder of the $57.8K–$60K support zone.

For buyers to gain traction, Bitcoin first needs to recover the recent lower high around $64K and then overcome the consolidation around $64.5K–$65.5K. Sustained acceptance above those levels would weaken the immediate bearish continuation setup.

The marked $72.7K–$74.7K supply zone remains a distant recovery barrier. Together with lower demand, it defines the broader area highlighted on the chart, although price has yet to establish a sideways trading range between those boundaries.

Sentiment Analysis

The one-week liquidation heatmap highlights a bright concentration of estimated liquidation exposure beneath the current price, around $60.8K–$61.2K, with additional bands extending toward $60K. These levels could become relevant if Bitcoin loses its nearby lows.

The buildup is consistent with leveraged long exposure vulnerable to another downside move. However, the heatmap alone cannot confirm an increase in net long positioning. A sweep through these bands could trigger forced closures and accelerate selling before any meaningful support response develops.

Above the market, nearby concentrations sit around $62.7K–$63K and $64.3K–$64.7K. A larger concentration spans approximately $65.5K–$68K, creating potential for a sharper recovery if buyers reclaim resistance and trigger short liquidations.

For now, nearby downside exposure aligns with the weak technical structure. A sustained recovery above the broken daily support zone would provide stronger evidence of stabilization than oversold momentum or liquidation concentrations alone.

title: Christine Lagarde Warns Europe Could Lose Ground in Tokenized Asset Market
description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde warns that Europe risks losing the opportunity to establish a unified market for tokenized financial assets unless lawmakers introduce common rules before competing blockchain platforms become difficult to connect. Speaking at the Frankfurt European Banking Congress on November 20, Lagarde highlighted the growing role of blockchain technology in traditional […]
fullContent:
European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde warns that Europe risks losing the opportunity to establish a unified market for tokenized financial assets unless lawmakers introduce common rules before competing blockchain platforms become difficult to connect.

Speaking at the Frankfurt European Banking Congress on November 20, Lagarde highlighted the growing role of blockchain technology in traditional finance. Tokenization allows assets such as stocks and bonds to be represented and traded as digital tokens, potentially bringing issuance, trading, and settlement together on a single platform.

However, she cautioned that technological progress alone will not guarantee an integrated European market. Without consistent standards, financial institutions could develop separate blockchain systems that cannot easily process transactions between one another.

The warning comes as the global market for tokenized traditional assets on public blockchains continues to expand. It was valued at approximately €23 billion ($25 billion) in March, representing a fivefold increase compared with the previous year.

Lagarde Calls for Common Rules as Tokenized Markets Expand

Lagarde described tokenization as an opportunity for Europe to build a genuine single market for digital financial assets from the outset. However, she warned that the window to establish common standards is limited.

As banks and other financial institutions increasingly adopt blockchain-based systems, different platforms could begin operating under incompatible rules. This could make cross-platform settlement difficult and create fragmented markets rather than the connected financial ecosystem Europe is seeking to develop.

“With the right framework, tokenization offers a chance to build a genuine single market in digital assets, integrated from the start. For Europe, that is a huge opportunity,” Lagarde said.

She also made clear that the responsibility does not rest with central banks and technology providers alone. European lawmakers will need to establish the legal framework required to ensure that tokenized securities can move across platforms under consistent rules.

Her comments underline a broader challenge for European financial markets: building the infrastructure for blockchain-based finance while ensuring that regulatory differences do not prevent institutions from using it effectively.

ECB’s Pontes Platform Already Supports Digital Bond Settlement

The European Central Bank has already taken steps to provide the infrastructure needed for tokenized financial transactions.

In September, the Eurosystem launched Pontes, a settlement platform that allows banks and other financial institutions to settle tokenized securities transactions using central bank money. This provides an alternative to relying on private stablecoins or commercial bank deposits for settlement. The platform has already been used for a major transaction. Earlier in November, the European Stability Mechanism, the eurozone’s financial rescue fund, settled a €1 billion digitally native bond through Pontes.

The transaction demonstrates how blockchain-based settlement is moving beyond experimental projects and into larger financial operations involving European institutions. The ECB has also started preparing to invest part of its own foreign exchange reserves in tokenized securities, initially focusing on euro-denominated public-sector debt.

These developments suggest that the central bank is seeking to expand the practical use of tokenization while maintaining the role of central bank money within the financial system.

Appia Initiative Aims to Connect Europe’s Tokenized Financial Markets

Alongside Pontes, the Eurosystem is developing its longer-term Appia initiative, which aims to establish common standards and connect Europe’s tokenized financial markets.

The project is intended to bring market participants together around an integrated framework for blockchain-based financial services. The ECB’s broader work under Appia is expected to produce a blueprint in 2028. However, Lagarde stressed that infrastructure and shared settlement systems cannot resolve the problem on their own.

“Infrastructure alone is not enough. Common rules will be needed too, and those lie with legislators,” she said.

Her remarks point to a distinction between having the technology to settle tokenized assets and having a regulatory framework that allows different platforms to operate together. Without legislative coordination, Europe could end up with several technically advanced but disconnected markets.

Lagarde is expected to leave her position as ECB president in February 2027, making the speech one of her final policy messages at the Frankfurt European Banking Congress.

The next stage will depend on whether European lawmakers can establish common rules alongside the infrastructure already being developed by the Eurosystem. As tokenized financial markets continue to grow, the decisions made now could influence how easily European institutions participate in this emerging sector.

Do you think Europe can establish a unified tokenized asset market before competing blockchain platforms become too fragmented? Could common regulatory standards give European financial institutions an advantage in the expanding digital securities market?

title: Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food
Block’s first bitcoin payments report found the median Square payment is about $13, with 72% at food and drink businesses, as it pushes for a de minimis tax exemption.
This post Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food

Most bitcoin payments at Square sellers are small, everyday purchases at coffee shops and restaurants, Block said in a new report that it hopes will inform a debate in Congress over a tax break for small crypto purchases.

The report, “The State of Bitcoin Payments,” covers completed bitcoin payments at U.S. Square sellers from Nov. 1, 2025, to Oct. 15, 2026. The median payment was about $13, and the average was about $29.

Food and drink businesses took 72% of those payments, Block found. That is a bigger share than the category’s 67.5% slice of regular card payments on Square over the same period.

“Most bitcoin payments are small and routine,” the company wrote on X Thursday, calling the report one of the first datasets on how people spend bitcoin in the local economy.

Coffee, quick bites and repeat visits

Coffee shops and fast food businesses accounted for 62.6% of the bitcoin payments in the food and drink category, with a median payment of $9.10. Grocery stores made up a smaller share but had the highest average payment in the group, at $60.73.

Small tickets dominated. About 42% of bitcoin payments on Square were under $10, and 65.1% were under $20. Those sub-$20 payments made up just 19.1% of total payment value, though, with a few larger purchases accounting for much of the dollars spent.

Customers also came back. Among Cash App users who paid with bitcoin at least twice at the same merchant, the median was three purchases per customer-merchant pair. About 44% of bitcoin payments from Cash App were repeat payments, and 86% of those came within 30 days.

The activity was not limited to Block’s own app. External Lightning wallets such as Strike, Wallet of Satoshi, Phoenix and Coinbase handled 56.6% of Square bitcoin payments and about 66% of payment value, while Cash App wallets made up the rest.

Square sellers can choose how much of each sale they keep in bitcoin, and Square converts the rest to dollars automatically. Block said zero-fee processing for bitcoin payments on Square has been extended through Dec. 31, 2027. Local governments are testing similar setups, with Miami-Dade County now taking bitcoin for property taxes and converting it to dollars.

A push for a de minimis bitcoin exemption

Block tied the data to tax policy. Under current U.S. federal rules, paying with bitcoin generally means calculating a capital gain or loss on every purchase, even a $10 coffee, the company said.

A Morning Consult survey that Block commissioned found that 23.6% of businesses that don’t accept bitcoin cite tax and accounting complexity as a reason. That is about the same share that cite regulation, refunds or price swings. Among businesses that have considered taking bitcoin but haven’t, the figure was 27%.

Consumers pointed to friction, too. Morning Consult surveyed 8,669 U.S. adults who are aware of bitcoin in August. Among those who don’t own it, 29.6% said they would be more likely to pay with bitcoin if it were easier, and 15.7% of that group said they were unsure how it is taxed or regulated.

Block said Congress is weighing a crypto tax package and pointed to a de minimis exemption, which would exempt small gains on qualifying purchases, as one option. Industry groups have pressed lawmakers on crypto tax rules for months, with little movement so far.

The report doesn’t give totals. Block said the number of Square bitcoin payments, the number of sellers receiving them and total bitcoin payment volume are proprietary and not disclosed. Merchant lists like the 425 Los Angeles businesses that accept bitcoin offer a rough sense of reach.

“We think tax policy should account for how people spend bitcoin as well as how they hold it,” Block said.

This post Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

Block tied the data to tax policy. Under current U.S. federal rules, paying with bitcoin generally means calculating a capital gain or loss on every purchase, even a $10 coffee, the company said.

A Morning Consult survey that Block commissioned found that 23.6% of businesses that don’t accept bitcoin cite tax and accounting complexity as a reason. That is about the same share that cite regulation, refunds or price swings. Among businesses that have considered taking bitcoin but haven’t, the figure was 27%.

Consumers pointed to friction, too. Morning Consult surveyed 8,669 U.S. adults who are aware of bitcoin in August. Among those who don’t own it, 29.6% said they would be more likely to pay with bitcoin if it were easier, and 15.7% of that group said they were unsure how it is taxed or regulated.

Block said Congress is weighing a crypto tax package and pointed to a de minimis exemption, which would exempt small gains on qualifying purchases, as one option. Industry groups have pressed lawmakers on crypto tax rules for months, with little movement so far.

The report doesn’t give totals. Block said the number of Square bitcoin payments, the number of sellers receiving them and total bitcoin payment volume are proprietary and not disclosed. Merchant lists like the 425 Los Angeles businesses that accept bitcoin offer a rough sense of reach.

“We think tax policy should account for how people spend bitcoin as well as how they hold it,” Block said.

title: ARK Invest Buys $90M in Anthropic Shares While Trimming Ethereum ETF Holdings
description: Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest made a major move into artificial intelligence during Anthropic’s first day on the Nasdaq, purchasing nearly $91 million worth of shares in the newly listed company. At the same time, the investment firm reduced its exposure to Ethereum and Solana staking exchange-traded funds, highlighting another round of portfolio adjustments across its […]
fullContent:
Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest made a major move into artificial intelligence during Anthropic’s first day on the Nasdaq, purchasing nearly $91 million worth of shares in the newly listed company.

At the same time, the investment firm reduced its exposure to Ethereum and Solana staking exchange-traded funds, highlighting another round of portfolio adjustments across its technology and crypto-related holdings. According to ARK’s latest trading disclosures, the firm acquired 934,968 Anthropic shares across six of its actively managed ETFs on Thursday. Based on the stock’s closing price of $97.17, the position was valued at approximately $90.9 million.

The purchases came alongside sales of $2.9 million in 3iQ Ethereum staking ETF holdings and $1.2 million in its Solana staking ETF. The transactions show ARK adding exposure to the AI sector while reducing selected positions linked to digital assets.

ARK Builds Anthropic Exposure Across Six ETFs

ARK distributed its Anthropic purchases across six funds, with the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) accounting for the largest portion. The fund purchased approximately 60% of the total shares acquired, although the position represented only around 0.4% of ARKK’s overall holdings.

The remaining purchases were spread across ARK’s other actively managed ETFs, including its Next Generation Internet, Autonomous Technology & Robotics, Genomic Revolution, Fintech Innovation, and Space Exploration & Innovation funds.

The investment reflects ARK’s continued activity in emerging technology companies. However, the firm’s disclosures do not provide the exact prices at which the Anthropic shares were purchased. The $90.9 million figure represents their value using Thursday’s closing price rather than a confirmed total purchase cost.

ARK’s portfolio strategy also limits the weight of individual holdings, with the firm generally seeking to prevent any single position from exceeding 10% of a fund. This approach can lead to further adjustments when the value of a holding changes significantly relative to other assets.

Anthropic Shares Deliver a Strong Nasdaq Debut

ARK’s investment coincided with a high-profile stock market debut for Anthropic, the company behind the Claude artificial intelligence model.

Trading under the ticker ANT, shares opened at $111.50, approximately 34% above the initial public offering price of $83. The stock later gave back part of its early gains, closing at $97.17, still 17.1% above the IPO price.

Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83 each, generating approximately $81.3 billion in offering value. The company had initially indicated a price range of $70 to $78 per share and planned to sell fewer shares, making the final offering larger than originally anticipated.

The total could increase to approximately $93.5 billion if underwriters exercise their option to purchase an additional 147 million shares. A separate planned $26 billion private placement involving major technology companies, including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC, would bring the combined total to approximately $107.3 billion before the additional underwriting option.

ARK Reduces Ethereum and Solana Staking ETF Exposure

While increasing its Anthropic position, ARK also trimmed holdings in two crypto-linked investment products.

The firm sold approximately $2.9 million worth of the 3iQ Ethereum staking ETF and another $1.2 million worth of the 3iQ Solana staking ETF. The reductions came through its ARKW Next Generation Internet and ARKF Blockchain & Fintech Innovation funds.

The underlying cryptocurrencies recorded declines during Thursday’s session. Ethereum fell approximately 1.1%, while Solana slipped 0.7%, according to market data. Meanwhile, the 3iQ Ethereum staking ETF closed 0.4% higher at $6.85, while its Solana counterpart ended the session down 0.3%.

The mixed performance highlights the difference between movements in the underlying tokens and those of investment products tied to them.

ARK Continues to Rebalance Its Portfolio

ARK Invest latest transactions form part of its broader approach to managing exposure across technology, artificial intelligence, and digital assets. The firm regularly adjusts fund weightings as individual holdings change in value, while maintaining its diversification strategy.

The Anthropic purchase represents a notable addition to its AI exposure, but the simultaneous reductions in Ethereum and Solana staking ETFs do not, on their own, establish a wider retreat from the cryptocurrency sector. The firm may continue adjusting its positions as market conditions and portfolio weightings evolve. For now, its latest disclosures show a clear increase in exposure to Anthropic alongside smaller reductions in selected crypto-linked products.

Do you think ARK Invest Anthropic purchase signals growing confidence in AI stocks, or is it simply another portfolio rebalancing move? Could its reductions in Ethereum and Solana staking ETFs point to a change in how the firm approaches crypto-related investments?

title: Why Is ARB Down Today? Sellers Ignore a $352M Stablecoin Week on Arbitrum One
description: Arbitrum One led last week's stablecoin inflows, yet ARB keeps falling under both moving averages. Here is why sellers stay in control and where support sits.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • Arbitrum One drew the largest stablecoin inflow among its peers last week, even as the wider stablecoin market shrank.
  • ARB keeps sliding under both key moving averages, and sellers still steer the momentum.
  • Traders are watching one distant support level near 8 cents, with little mapped in between.

Arbitrum One pulled in more fresh stablecoin money than any rival last week, Token Terminal data shows. The network's dollar base kept growing while the broader market contracted.

The ARB token missed the benefit. It fell through the same week, extending a steep autumn decline. Stablecoins parked on a chain do not force anyone to buy its governance token. Traders now want to know whether network demand can ever lift the price.

Arbitrum One Pulls In Fresh Dollars While the Stablecoin Market Shrinks

Token Terminal data shows Arbitrum One, Arc and Aptos added a combined $717 million in stablecoin market cap over the seven days ending Nov 19. The broader stablecoin market contracted slightly over the same stretch.

Arbitrum One led the group with a gain of $352.6 million. Token Terminal and DefiLlama put its total stablecoin supply between $4.03 billion and $4.06 billion. Arc, whose mainnet launched on Sep 16, came second with $246.1 million. Its supply sits near $1.6 billion and is more than 99% USDC. Aptos added $118.3 million, lifting its total to roughly $880 million.

Demand for USDC and USDT drove most of the inflows. Some of that money may have moved between chains instead of coming from new issuance.

That supply keeps Arbitrum One in a heavier weight class than most rivals.

A 37% Monthly Slide Leaves ARB Stranded Under Both Averages

Arbitrum (ARB) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

ARB traded near $0.12 on Thursday, down about 3% in the past day. The token has lost roughly 22% over the week and about 37% over the past month.

A moving average smooths out daily noise by tracking the mean closing price over a set period. ARB now sits below its 50-day average near $0.16. It also trades under its 200-day average near $0.15. Both lines now act as ceilings above the price.

That setup tells a simple story. Every bounce since October has met sellers before it could reclaim those averages. Buyers who stepped in during earlier rallies are now holding losses, and many may sell into any recovery to get out near break-even.

The order of the two averages adds detail. The 50-day line still sits above the 200-day line, a leftover from higher prices earlier in the fall. With ARB now well beneath both, the shorter average is likely to keep falling toward the longer one. That would confirm the damage is recent and spreading.

The weekly drop came as Arbitrum One posted its biggest stablecoin gain among peers. Dollars arrived on the network, and the token kept falling.

Sellers Keep Control Even as RSI Nears Exhaustion

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits at 30 on the daily chart. That reading marks the edge of oversold territory. Selling has run hard and fast, yet buyers have not returned.

Other momentum signals lean the same way. The MACD line remains below its signal line, so momentum is still pointing down. Trend strength readings show a trend taking shape, and sellers are the ones driving it. Together, those signals suggest downside pressure is still building.

Oversold readings can last for weeks when a downtrend gains strength. Prices often grind lower while RSI hovers near or below 30.

A real turn would need RSI to climb back toward the neutral middle of its range. Until that happens, a stretched reading alone gives buyers little reason to step in.

Where Does ARB Find a Floor Below 12 Cents?

The daily chart shows no nearby cushion. The closest support sits near $0.083, roughly 30% below the current price. No mapped level exists beneath it, so a break there would leave ARB without a clear reference point.

That gap creates an air pocket. Thin price history above that support means a selloff could move quickly. Buyers have few obvious spots to defend on the way down.

The upside map is more crowded. The first resistance lines up with the 200-day average, the same ceiling that has capped recent bounces. A daily close back above it would end the immediate slide and show that buyers can hold ground.

A real trend change needs more. Resistance near $0.17 marks the level where the recent breakdown began to pick up speed. Clearing it would put ARB back above both averages and shift control toward buyers.

Two Paths for ARB Over the Next Three Days

Momentum favors sellers, though stretched readings leave room for a short rebound.

  • Bullish: A relief bounce could carry ARB back toward its 200-day average if the new stablecoin dollars draw traders into the token. A daily close back under the current price area would cancel that setup and hand control back to sellers.
  • Bearish: Downside momentum could drag ARB toward its lone mapped support if selling keeps building. A reclaim of the 200-day average would cancel that path and signal that buyers have regained footing.

Network Strength Has Not Reached the Token Yet

Arbitrum One keeps winning the contest for stablecoin deposits, and that supports the network's long-term case. For now, sellers control the token's trend, and the averages overhead still cap every rally.

The bigger risk sits below. With nothing mapped beneath that lone support level, a breakdown could run deeper and faster than most holders expect.

title: Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping
Bitcoin is trading barely above its realized price, the average cost of every coin, and a break below would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023.
This post Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping

Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday.

The price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000. The realized price is a measure of what holders paid, not where the market trades. When bitcoin trades above it, the typical coin is sitting on a gain. Below it, the typical coin is underwater.

The margin is thin. The firm said the MVRV ratio, which compares bitcoin’s market value with its realized value, sits “just above 1.” A reading of 1 means the market price has fallen all the way to the realized price.

What the realized price measures

Realized price values each coin at the price it last moved on the blockchain, then averages across the supply. Look Into Bitcoin describes it as bitcoin’s average cost basis. Because it tracks the price when coins last changed hands, it moves far more slowly than the market.

The MVRV ratio expresses the same idea as a multiple. Above 1, holders are in profit on average. Below 1, they are not. A reading just above 1 means the market price is only a sliver higher than what the average coin cost.

The firm did not give the exact realized price in its post, which included a chart. That leaves the exact cushion between today’s price and the average cost basis unstated. Bitcoin Magazine Pro’s full realized price chart sits behind a login, so the current level could not be confirmed independently for this report.

“The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit,” the firm wrote. “The margin is thin.”

Outflows and liquidations add to the pressure

The slide has come with heavy selling from funds. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost about $541 million on Thursday, its largest one-day outflow since it launched in January 2024, Bloomberg reported. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total that day.

The selling stands out against the buying earlier in the fall. Institutions piled into bitcoin ETFs through the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record, Bitcoin Magazine reported this week.

Leveraged traders took losses too. More than $700 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, and about 86% of them were bets on higher prices. Bitcoin accounted for roughly $200 million of the total.

CoinShares sees range trading through 2027

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop is part of a longer downturn rather than the start of a new one. “I see this as a continuation of the existing bear market rather than the start of another,” he said in a note dated Nov. 18.

The note frames Friday’s price action as a late stage of a decline that began well before November. Butterfill pointed to whale selling that weighed on prices from late 2025, expectations of higher interest rates and weakness in technology stocks, all of which have kept buyers cautious.

“Our base case remains range trading around USD 60k to 90k through much of 2027, until falling inflation gives monetary policy room to ease,” he said. “Geopolitics will have a considerable say in that.”

A move through the realized price would put bitcoin near the bottom edge of that range. The firm said holders as a group have not been in loss since early 2023.

A sustained breakout, Butterfill said, would likely require “a change in the policy outlook, renewed whale participation or both.”

This post Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia
The bitcoin price slipped to near $61,500 on Friday morning, its lowest level since July, as the tech selloff spread to Asia and IBIT posted a record outflow.
This post Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia

The bitcoin price slipped to near $61,500 on Friday morning, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a selloff in technology stocks that followed Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut spread to Asian markets and dragged bitcoin to its lowest level since July.

Bitcoin first broke below $62,000 on Thursday evening, after Thursday afternoon’s report showed it giving back a rebound toward $64,000. The bitcoin price then slid to nearly $61,200 during Asian trading before bouncing back above $61,700. Friday marks a third straight day of losses.

Asian stocks extend the AI rout

The selling started in Asia. South Korea’s Kospi slid more than 5%, with chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics down around 6%. The Korea Exchange halted program selling for five minutes after the drop, while Japan’s Nikkei fell as much as 4.85% to a seven-month low.

U.S. futures pointed lower too. Nasdaq-100 futures fell more than 1.7% and S&P 500 futures dropped 0.8%, Yahoo Finance reported. Gold futures lost 3%. The S&P 500 is pointing to a seventh straight daily decline, its longest losing streak since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

Anthropic shares fell 8% in premarket trading after closing their first session at $97.17, up 17% from the $83 IPO price. Nvidia was down about 2.4% and AMD fell nearly 7%, CNBC reported. Hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment, Reuters said.

ETF outflows and liquidations pressure the bitcoin price

Bitcoin funds are feeling the pressure. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded $541.1 million in net outflows on Thursday, its largest single-day outflow since launch. That topped the previous record of $528.3 million set on Jan. 30. The fund bled $2 billion over nine straight days of outflows earlier this month.

Leveraged traders took heavy losses as the bitcoin price broke support. Bitcoin liquidations hit $712.9 million over 24 hours, with $614 million coming from long positions. Open interest in bitcoin futures fell to $18 billion from $20 billion a week ago, and funding rates flipped broadly negative as traders unwound their bets.

Traders are now watching whether the bitcoin price can hold the $60,000 area. A large pocket of long positions sits in the $60,500 to $60,900 band, just below the current price, and could come into play on a further drop. Bitcoin is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, which would be its second-longest losing streak after nine weeks of declines in 2022.

Crypto stocks slide before the bell

Crypto stocks pointed lower in premarket trading. Strategy (MSTR) traded near $83.90, down about 2.6% from Thursday’s close of $86.13, after the stock fell for a sixth straight day on Thursday. Coinbase (COIN) slipped about 2.7% to near $106.

Bitcoin miners fell harder. IREN (IREN) dropped about 4.4%, CleanSpark (CLSK) lost about 3.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) declined about 3.4%. Riot Platforms (RIOT) was down about 3.3%. IREN has also been under pressure as investors reassess AI infrastructure stocks. Delays in bringing some of its capacity online led Microsoft to spend less with the miner than planned last quarter.

Longer-term buyers have not left entirely. Institutional investors added 49,229 BTC through U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs in the third quarter, lifting their holdings to a record 356,491 BTC. Swiss bank Sygnum called the current downturn the shallowest bear market for bitcoin to date, putting the drawdown at around 54% compared with declines of more than 70% in previous cycles.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $61,800.

Anyway, I’d better get back to working in a very safe and careful manner, as I always do.” At press time, Eckstrom had reportedly scooped up the dead guy and deposited him in the rink’s lost and found.

fullContent:
WASHINGTON—Warning Americans to keep at least 200 yards away from the livestock at all times, federal officials announced Friday that Iran had claimed credit for the hack that turned cattle into apex predators.

“Earlier this week, an Iranian hacker group connected to the Revolutionary Guard Corps broke into the Department of Agriculture’s servers, hijacked our cows’ programming, and turned them into fierce flesh-eating animals,” said agency spokesperson Delia Marchand, who admitted that the security systems of the nation’s cattle had not been updated since the early 2000s. “Cows have now ascended to the top of the food chain, killing deer, bison, and even bears. Worst of all, the group responsible has said our nation’s 85 million cows will prey upon the American people until we end the war with Iran.”

“Our experts have determined this was a complete rewriting of bovine source code,” she continued. “The cows’ eyesight and hearing have sharpened, and they can smell a drop of blood from miles away. Estimates suggest they are now hunting to eat 30 to 40 pounds of meat per day, and they have shown incredible intelligence as pack hunters: A single cow will lure a people in with a cute, calm demeanor, and then the entire herd will descend upon the prey, tearing them to pieces in seconds. Unfortunately, the hackers have locked us out of the cows programming, so we cannot undo the damage. We are looking at the world’s newest and greatest killing machines.”

Marchand added that until the federal government could lock down all remaining vulnerabilities, the nation’s fish and birds would be deactivated to make sure they weren’t similarly corrupted.

title: The Best And Worst Series Finales Of All Time
description:
A good or bad ending can make or break a TV show’s legacy. The Onion takes a look at some of the best and worst series finales ever made. BEST Reading Rainbow, “One More” (2006): The haunting final episode features host LeVar Burton looking straight into the camera and taunting children with the knowledge of […]
The post The Best And Worst Series Finales Of All Time appeared first on The Onion.
fullContent:
A good or bad ending can make or break a TV show’s legacy. The Onion takes a look at some of the best and worst series finales ever made.

BEST

Reading Rainbow, “One More” (2006): The haunting final episode features host LeVar Burton looking straight into the camera and taunting children with the knowledge of a secret 27th letter. 

Planet Earth, “Refineries” (2023): In a jarring tonal shift, the normally staid David Attenborough gives viewers step-by-step instructions on how to blow up oil refineries.

How I Met Your Mother, “Last Forever” (2014): Craig Thomas and Carter Bays thrilled fans by revealing the identity of the mother before promptly killing her off, then killing Ted Mosby, then killing their real-life families, then themselves.

Six Feet Under, “Everyone’s Waiting” (2005): Widely regarded as one of the most moving finales of all time, the drama concludes with a series of poignant flash-forwards through 2025, 2029, 2044, 2049, 2051, and 2085, showing how each character will eventually be buried alive.

The Sopranos, “Made In America” (2007): Though controversial upon initial release, the “cut to black” ending has since garnered praise for its inventive use of darkness to indicate that they didn’t film any more scenes.

Game Of Thrones, “The Iron Throne” (2019): Attention is a form of love. 

WORST

Bionic Woman, “Chiefs At Dolphins” (2007): Heavily impacted by the writers’ strike, this reboot of the ’70s sci-fi adventure series was forced to pad its episodes with NFL games.

M*A*S*H, “Goodbye, Farewell And Amen” (1983): Drawing over 105 million viewers, the two-and-a-half hour finale left factories empty, prisons unguarded, and air traffic control towers unmanned, ultimately resulting in $6 trillion damage across the U.S.

Breaking Bad, “Felina” (2013): After seven years of depicting antihero drug lord Walter White, Bryan Cranston fails to parlay the part into a role in a Marvel movie, an action franchise, a spinoff, or any other kind of career ascension that might actually bring him satisfaction.

The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson, “May 22, 1992” (1992): In his strangely vindictive send-off, the legendary Carson told America, “That’s all from me, and now you will get what you deserve.”

Pretty Little Liars, “Till Death Do Us Part” (2017): What was supposed to be the viewing party to end all viewing parties in Megan’s parents’ finished basement was ruined when Amanda brought along her volleyball friend Marissa, who spent the whole time talking over the TV, bitching about her boyfriend drama, and refusing to eat any M&M’s because she was “dieting.”

Seinfeld, “The Finale” (1998): Fans disliked this hour-long conclusion that left the show’s morally dubious protagonists arrested but unexecuted.

The post The Best And Worst Series Finales Of All Time appeared first on The Onion.

title: Why Are Cyber Attacks Increasing So Fast in 2026?
description:
Cyber attacks go vertical in 2026 as AI tools arm hackers, with incidents doubling since August and crypto hit hardest.
The post Why Are Cyber Attacks Increasing So Fast in 2026? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Estimated cyber attacks have more than doubled in roughly three months, Bridgewater Associates data shows. The jump began when a Chinese AI model with strong hacking skills became free to download.

Bridgewater has not proven the model caused the spike. Still, the fund now prices in a one-in-three chance of an economically destabilizing cyber attack within a year. Banks, payment firms, and crypto exchanges sit closest to that risk.

Why Did Cyber Attacks Go Vertical After August?

Capriole Investments founder Charles Edwards shared the chart on X on Nov. 20. His verdict was three words long, “truly unprecedented times.”

For nearly a decade, Bridgewater’s annualized estimate climbed slowly. It rose from about 1,500 incidents in 2017 to roughly 4,000 by mid-2026, according to the research.

Then the line turned almost straight up, reaching nearly 10,000 by November. The chart marks a single event at the turning point.

That event is the late-August release of GLM 5.3’s weights. GLM 5.3 is a coding model from Beijing-based Z.ai, formerly Zhipu AI, and anyone can download and modify it.

The US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) called it “the most cyber-capable open-weight model released to date” in its assessment.

Separately, the FBI warned on Nov. 13 that hackers have used ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking framework, since at least August. Some intrusions reached privileged access in under three hours, the bureau said. However, it found DeepSeek models, not GLM, most common in attacker setups.

How Fast Are Cyber Attacks Rising Month by Month?

Check Point Research data points the same way, though less steeply. The firm tracks average weekly attacks per organization worldwide.

Growth stayed modest in the first half and even dipped below 2025 levels in March. From July, however, the yearly gap widened each month before peaking in September.

October cooled 9% from September but still ran 32% above last year. Ransomware hit a record 1,063 attacks that month, according to Check Point.

n0n, one of October’s most active ransomware groups, claimed this week’s breach of vendors serving JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard. Attackers accessed customer names and email addresses, Bloomberg reported.

Why Is Crypto Taking the Costliest Hits?

Crypto platforms absorb the largest losses. Binance lost about $6.3 billion on Oct. 29, the biggest crypto theft on record. The breach began with a fake job interview that planted malware on an engineer’s computer.

Before that single incident, DefiLlama had already logged 312 crypto hacks worth $2.4 billion in 2026. Meanwhile, Chainalysis estimates that suspected North Korean groups caused nearly 89% of this year’s hack losses. In 2021, their share was 15%.

Scams add to the toll. US victims reported $11.37 billion in crypto-related fraud losses in 2025, over half of all cybercrime losses tracked by the FBI.

Are Defenders Already Falling Behind?

Experts on BeInCrypto’s Market Intelligence Expert Council argue that AI currently favors attackers. Erica Stanford, a digital assets and AI adviser at law firm CMS and author of Crypto Wars, made that case in a recent discussion.

“It’s 100% helping criminals… anyone with no skills and not even native English or native language can now commit fraud and crimes very very easily because AI helps people do that.”

Patrick Prinz, co-founder of asset recovery firm Recoveris, agreed.

“I think it’s enabling criminals more than it helps right now the law enforcement side.”

Recovery also trails the theft itself. Binance has secured an Abu Dhabi court order over frozen funds, yet most stolen assets remain out of reach.

Prinz expects years to pass before law enforcement fields a matching response. Until then, every exchange, bank, and vendor faces attackers working at machine speed, and Bridgewater’s curve shows no sign of flattening.

The post Why Are Cyber Attacks Increasing So Fast in 2026? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

description:
It is evident BlackRock-linked wallets still move large coin stacks through Coinbase rails. Especially when Bitcoin and Ether leave the same labeled cluster on one day, the custody path matters. For BlackRock, it seems the latest BlackRock Coinbase Prime deposit just moved about 5,400 BTC and 71,597 ETH. A rather big dual-asset transfer, albeit one […]
The post BlackRock Coinbase Prime Deposit Hits $456M in BTC, ETH appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
It is evident BlackRock-linked wallets still move large coin stacks through Coinbase rails. Especially when Bitcoin and Ether leave the same labeled cluster on one day, the custody path matters. For BlackRock, it seems the latest BlackRock Coinbase Prime deposit just moved about 5,400 BTC and 71,597 ETH. A rather big dual-asset transfer, albeit one that is not exactly surprising. The firm still runs the largest US spot Bitcoin and Ether funds.

Lookonchain flagged the transfers around 12:39 UTC on November 20, 2026. The monitor put the Bitcoin leg near $331 million. The Ether leg sat near $125 million, or about $456 million combined. The post pointed readers to Arkham's BlackRock entity map. That map tracks addresses tied to the firm's ETF-linked holdings. On-chain labels can lag or miss a hop. Even so, the size and destination still give crypto ETF readers a live custody signal.

What the BlackRock Coinbase Prime Deposit Signals

This is a very worrisome development for anyone who treats every exchange deposit as a sale, to say the least. Even so, a move into Coinbase Prime was bound to draw eyes sooner or later. On the one hand, Coinbase Custody has long sat inside creation and redemption plumbing for BlackRock's funds. That includes the iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) and iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA). On the other, a Prime deposit can mean inventory rebalancing. It can also mean authorized-participant settlement, or cold-to-hot handoffs that never hit the open book. The chain shows the transfer. It does not show a filled sell order.

A fair few desks still watch these rails as a rough gauge of fund demand. When coins enter Coinbase-linked wallets tied to BlackRock, traders ask two questions. Are creations warming up? Or do redemptions need coins staged for delivery? The reverse path can hint at the opposite flow. Neither reading is certain without the next day's creation and redemption prints. For now, the only hard claim is the size. About 5,400 BTC and 71,597 ETH moved into Coinbase Prime under BlackRock-linked labels.

IBIT and ETHA Stay in the Same Custody Story

It is evident the next check is not the deposit itself, to say the least. A fair few of these moves sit quiet for hours or days. On the one hand, confirmed IBIT or ETHA creations would make the transfer look like buy-side plumbing. On the other, a quiet book after a $456 million dual deposit would leave the sale scare looking thin. Even so, the dual-asset timing is the sharper tell. Bitcoin and Ether arriving together keep both funds in one custody story. That pattern is rarer than a single-coin hop.

For BlackRock, it seems the firm still trusts Coinbase Prime as a working rail for large institutional coin. The wallets Arkham marks as BlackRock remain the public map most monitors use. Until fund flow tables catch up, readers are left with the on-chain receipt. The open question is what that receipt is for. A serious custody move, though not a surprise. These rails already carry ETF-linked coin often enough.

The post BlackRock Coinbase Prime Deposit Hits $456M in BTC, ETH appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
