title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #220
description: SpaceX reusability, Leukemia vaccine (+pancreatic pill), SLAB, Tesla Powercore, Earth AI Gold + TEN Extra Doses
fullContent:
Hi friends 👋,

Happy Friday and welcome back to our 220th Weekly Dose of Optimism!

What a week to be alive. Since we spoke last Friday, GTA 6 is finally out, Anthropic is public, Starships are reusable, leukemia may not be as deadly, we may be able to live on the open seas, and… there’s just so much more. I think we might have both the highest density of great things in the Main Dose and the longest section of Extra Doses to date (there are 10 down there, including Anthropic and new Google models). Almost everything in Extra Dose would have made the top 5 even like 3 months ago.

Plus, I’ve been having a lot of fun building a new notboring.com. You can click on a bunch of the companies on the home page for little Easter Eggs, check Roundup for all of the day’s top not boring-relevant stories, and Scarce Asset Tracker for the completed and upcoming sales relevant to what I wrote in Scarce Assets. I even built a better reading experience for all of our Essays. Enjoy! And let me know what else you’d like to see, so I can tell my agents to build it.

Let’s get to it.

This Week’s Weekly Dose is brought to you by… Runway

If you want to blow your family’s mind over Thanksgiving, bring their ideas to life with Runway.

Runway is building foundational AI for how the world creates. 65M+ people use Runway to generate, edit and produce video, images and audio with 80+ top media models. You can read my essay with co-founder Anastasis Germanidis to learn more on where Runway is headed beyond video.

Nvidia, Amazon, Lionsgate, Chime, and 95%+ of the Fortune 100 are part of a growing community of teams, founders, and independent creators using Runway to make national TV spots, social ads at scale, launch videos and more.

You can also use Runway in ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Cursor, Replit and more via the Runway MCP.

Create any idea with Runway now

(1) SpaceX’s Mechazilla Catches an Orbital Starship

Humanity is one giant leap closer to being multiplanetary.

Over the weekend on Starship Flight 15, Ship 42 launched from Starbase, Texas, reached orbit, deployed a batch of Starlink satellites, spent more than 22 hours in space, survived fiery hypersonic re-entry, flipped upright, and dropped cleanly into Mechazilla’s chopsticks. The SpaceX team made one of the greatest engineering feats in human history look easy.

SpaceX has already caught Super Heavy boosters before, which was already absurd. Catching the orbital upper stage, the part that goes into orbit carrying the payload to complete a mission, was the final boss of rapid, full reusability. The final boss is dead.

While the booster is more expensive at around 70% of Starship’s cost, it is somewhat easier to reuse given that it carries the upper stage up and comes right back. Having proven that the booster is reusable, the upper stage was like 90% of the marginal cost per flight. Having to make a new one each time would leave Starship with a hard floor around $30-40M per launch, but making it reusable means that the marginal cost of launch drops to something like $2-10M per launch, or $20-100/kg versus Falcon 9’s $1,000/kg internal cost.

SpaceX still has plenty of work ahead on heat-shield durability and turnaround time before Starships are flying as repeatably as planes, of course, but the goal is to send up about two a week by the end of 2027, hundreds per year by 2029 ,and multiple per day beyond that. They’ll carry satellites and data centers and drug factories and eventually all sorts of things we’ll need to thrive in space and on other worlds.

For now, just watch the slow-motion footage above and marvel. Humans rock.

(2) Leukemia Vaccine Cuts Risk of Death by 41% in Phase 3 Trial

Video created with Runway

At this point, you know how we feel about cancer here at the Dose. Hate it.

It’s been a big year for us cancer haters, and the streak continues.

On Tuesday, SELLAS Life Sciences and Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center announced positive topline results from the pivotal Phase 3 REGAL trial of galinpepimut-S (GPS), an immunotherapeutic vaccine for acute myeloid leukemia (AML). AML is a brutal blood cancer with roughly a 33% five-year survival rate that kills around 11,500 Americans every year.

The trial followed 126 patients whose AML had relapsed, who had fought their way back into a second (or later) remission, and who weren't eligible for a stem-cell transplant. The patients were a high-risk group with very few options left.

And GPS extended their lives. Patients who received GPS alone (with no chemo alongside it) had a median overall survival of 24.0 months, compared to 14.7 months for patients on investigator's choice of best available treatment. That's more than nine extra months of life and a 41% reduction in the risk of death.

Huge. While it’s not a total cure, we seem to be entering a period in which a number of therapies are able to extend patients’ lives while researchers around the world work to find more permanent cures. Meaning, an extra nine months both nine months and a call option on much longer.

This isn’t the first promising vaccine this year. Back in Dose #207, we covered Merck and Moderna’s personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine that cut recurrence or death by 42% in Phase 3. The exciting thing about GPS isn’t custom-built from an individual tumor like that one, but an off-the-shelf peptide vaccine, which should make it faster, cheaper, and more widely available if approved. Even better, the WT1 protein shows up in a number of blood cancers and solid tumors, so GPS may be effective against more than just AML.

Say it with us… get fucked, cancer!

(2a) Pancreatic cancer pill trial saw tumours vanish

Keep saying it with us. I don’t even know what to say anymore. I got to my computer to wrap up the Dose, opened up X, and the first tweet I saw was one from the BBC saying that there’s a new pill for pancreatic cancer that shrunk tumors in one in 12 patients so completely they were undetectable in scans, and stopped tumor growth in 90% of the 61 patients.

“Experts are calling it the biggest breakthrough in pancreatic cancer treatment for decades,” the BBC reported.

This pill isn’t a cure, either, and doctors aren’t sure yet how long its effects last. But pancreatic cancer has been one of the hardest-to-drug, hardest to catch early, and therefore most deadly cancers known to mankind, and it seems that we now have a way to slow it down at the very least.

And if this year’s pace in cancer treatments is any indication, there will be more where that came from.

GET FUCKED, CANCER.

(3) Palmer Luckey Reveals SLAB, a 1,000-Year Floating Seastead

Well, here’s a happy challenge we might have to deal with. If people live a lot longer, where are we going to but them all?

Bah gaw that’s Palmer Luckey’s music!

Fresh off announcing Warhound and a drumbeat of positive Anduril announcements, Luckey announced on X (to preempt a journalist working on the story) that he’s “developing a seastead called SLAB with a 1,000 year design life.”

To get ahead of people thinking he might just be another guy doing an ocean data center thing (this is “way cooler” than that, Palmer said that he’s actually been privately funding and building SLAB since selling Oculus to Facebook for $2 billion in 2014. He and some friends capitalized it at a $1 billion valuation, and put more money in recently.

The idea is that SLAB will be a massive off-shore floating industrial platform engineered to last a thousand years that’s meant to be cheaper than land while operating outside the regulatory morass that chokes American heavy industry. On SLAB, future Palmers may build factories for metal processing, desalination, oil refining, chemical engineering, and frontier medical research and treatment.

Thousand Year Luckey Empire.

(4) Tesla Unveils Powercore, a 7.4 MW Solid-State Transformer

Tesla announced that it’s doing solid state transformers with its new Powercore.

Ho hum. Another week, another huge chunk of the capability stack that eliminates a big bottleneck and also plays really well with the other pieces of the stack from The Musk Companies. Just look at how much of the future this man controls:

We’ve talked about SSTs in the context of Heron Power, founded by ex-Tesla SVP of Powertrain and Energy Engineering, Drew Baglino many times, in Dose #181, Dose #183, Dose #187, and Thank God for Data Centers. We are fans of both Drew and of SSTs, for their ability to speed up and cost down data center construction today and potentially help stabilize the grid in the future.

I think both Heron and Tesla will do well here. There is a ton of demand, and as I wrote in the America Spins on Westmag:

In the Electric Era, maintaining design leadership without manufacturing leadership is not a coherent strategic position, and one that gets less coherent the better you believe AI will get.

Elon has solved this by building practically everything inside of his own companies. There is a parallel American ecosystem emerging to serve the growing number of electric companies not in the Elonverse.

A few years ago, we barely had one modern industrial base. Now we have two. 🇺🇸

(5) Earth AI Uncovers a 3km Copper-Gold-Platinum System

If those two parallel electric universes do even one-tenth of what they’re planning to do, we’re going to need a lot of metal. Challenge is: the world spends something like $14 billion searching for new mineral deposits, but major discoveries have dropped ~70% over the past decade. We’ve already pulled out the easy stuff, and it’s going to take new technology to get at the harder stuff economically.

Luckily, as you may know, we are in a golden age of technology, and our friends and not boring capital portfolio company Earth AI are using it to find metals.. This week, the company announced that its Alpheus AI model found a continuous copper, gold, and platinum-group metals system stretching more than 3 kilometers at the Fontenoy/Meridian project in New South Wales, Australia. There’s some Tungsten in there too. Roman showed me one of the rocks - the Tungsten shows up as black spots and is easy to mistake for nothing.

Explorers actually drilled the site back in 1969 and again in 1997, but they thought it was just some scattered pockets that wouldn’t have been economical to mind. Back in January, Earth AI turned its models on the old data, and the models recognized that they weren’t looking at discontinuous “black smoker” pockets; they predicted that it was actually a massive magma-filled fault line.

Five weeks later, Earth AI started drilling (it owns its own rigs and labs, so it didn’t have to wait for slow and expensive contractors; vertical integration ftw). It’s drilled 35 holes and traced mineralization from 30m to 478m deep across the 3km seam, with hints that it might actually be 8km long.

As we covered in our Deep Dive on Earth AI, discovery is just the first step in a long process towards getting metal out of the ground, but with its rigs, it’s moving towards feasibility more quickly than other explorers traditionally could.

I think the company has the potential to be one of the world’s most beautiful businesses as these discoveries prove out, sell off, and turn into cash which buys more rigs and allows Earth AI to prove out the other 4,500 targets on its list. This week’s news is a golden step in the right direction.

title: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $62K: What Should You Do?
description:
Bitcoin price falls below $62K, ETF outflows hit $582M, and liquidations mount. Can BTC defend $60K, or is another crash toward $53K coming?
The post Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $62K: What Should You Do? appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
Bitcoin price has fallen below $62,000 for the first time since early July, extending a brutal November selloff as institutional investors pull billions from the market. BTC touched $61,270 just now, before recovering slightly to trade around $61,700.

Bitcoin price has now lost more than 10% over seven days, with selling pressure spreading across equities, precious metals and other risk assets. Yesterday’s $582.2 million outflow from US spot Bitcoin ETFs added another blow, bringing November withdrawals close to $3.5 billion.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest single-day outflow since launching. The same session saw $727 million in crypto liquidations, with bullish traders absorbing most of the damage.

Institutional demand is weakening, leveraged buyers are being forced out, and the Federal Reserve’s increasingly hawkish outlook is making speculative assets less attractive.

Bitcoin is now approaching $60,000, a level that could determine if the correction finds a floor or develops into something uglier.

Xrp (XRP)
24h7d30d1yAll time

Bitcoin ETF Exodus and $727M Liquidations Put Bulls on the Defensive

The ETF withdrawals are arguably the biggest concern for Bitcoin holders right now. Spot Bitcoin ETFs became an important source of institutional demand after launching in January 2024. Their buying helped absorb available supply and gave traditional investors a regulated route into the market.

That demand is now moving in the opposite direction. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost more than $1.1 billion this week alone. November’s cumulative withdrawals have approached $3.5 billion.

The pressure extends beyond ETFs. Rising Treasury yields and expectations of another Federal Reserve rate increase in December have encouraged investors to reduce exposure to assets that offer no regular income.

Meanwhile, derivatives traders are taking heavy losses. CoinGlass data showed more than $700 million in liquidations across crypto markets over 24 hours. Long positions accounted for 86% of the total.

Bitcoin itself recorded nearly $202 million in liquidations, with bullish traders suffering the majority of forced closures.

This creates a difficult environment for buyers. Falling prices trigger liquidations, which create additional selling pressure and push prices lower. The reduction in open interest also suggests excessive leverage is being flushed from the market.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

Bitcoin Price Prediction: $60K Breakdown or Relief Rally?

The immediate battle is around $60,000. Bitcoin needs to reclaim $62,000 and establish support above it before bulls can confidently argue that the latest breakdown was temporary.

There are three possible scenarios:

Scenario 1: Bitcoin loses $60K and heads toward $58K or $53K.

This is the bearish outcome. A decisive break below $60,000 could trigger another wave of stop-loss orders and leveraged liquidations.

The next downside area sits around $58,000, while more aggressive technical projections point toward $53,700.

The daily chart offers little encouragement for bulls. Bitcoin trades below its major moving averages, while bearish momentum continues to dominate. A sustained recovery in ETF flows would become increasingly important to prevent further deterioration.

Scenario 2: Bitcoin stabilizes between $60K and $62K.

This would give buyers time to absorb available supply without immediately reversing the entire November decline.

The liquidation wave has already removed considerable leverage from the market. If ETF withdrawals begin slowing, Bitcoin could establish a trading range before attempting another recovery.

But sideways trading alone would not confirm a bottom. Buyers need to demonstrate that they can defend support through multiple sessions.

Scenario 3: Bitcoin reclaims $62K and launches a relief rally.

A recovery above $62,000 would provide the first meaningful sign that sellers are losing control. A move toward $65,000 would then become possible, followed by resistance around $68,000.

Consistent ETF inflows, improving market sentiment, and a weaker dollar would strengthen this scenario. Without those developments, any rebound risks becoming another opportunity for sellers to exit.

Should Bitcoin Holders Sell, Hold or Buy the Dip?

For existing holders, the decision depends heavily on their entry price, investment horizon, and exposure. Long-term holders who bought substantially below current prices have more room to withstand volatility. Selling simply because Bitcoin crossed a psychological threshold risks locking in profits or losses without knowing whether the broader investment thesis has changed.

However, investors holding leveraged positions face a different problem. Falling prices can trigger forced liquidations regardless of their long-term convictions. Reducing leverage and protecting available capital should take priority over waiting for a rebound.

For buyers, the temptation to buy the dip is understandable. Bitcoin is considerably cheaper than it was just weeks ago, but cheaper does not automatically mean undervalued.

Buying in stages rather than committing an entire allocation around $61,000 offers more flexibility if the market tests $58,000 or even $53,700.

Bitcoin price remains vulnerable to another leg down. The $60,000 level is no longer just a psychological milestone. It is where the next major battle between buyers and sellers.

title: Monero Price Likely to Offer Another Selling Opportunity as XMR1 Holders Lose 99%
description: A wrapped Monero token on Hyperliquid lost 99% in minutes. Native XMR is separate but trades below its 200-day average, with resistance near $500.
fullContent:
Three Things to Know

  • A Wagyu-issued wrapped Monero token on Hyperliquid lost about 99% of its value in roughly half an hour.
  • Native XMR is a separate asset, yet it now trades below both its 50-day and 200-day averages.
  • The nearest ceiling sits near $500, and support lies far below it.

Holders of XMR1, a wrapped Monero token issued by Wagyu, were wiped out on Hyperliquid after the deployer account moved most of the supply to a fresh wallet and sold. Blockchain sleuths flagged the move as suspected theft.

Native Monero held up, though the coin was already sliding and now sits on fragile ground. Traders want to know whether any bounce can hold, or whether it just hands sellers a better exit.

Wrapped Monero Token XMR1 Collapses 99% on Hyperliquid

A wrapped Monero token issued by Wagyu lost almost all of its value on Hyperliquid on Nov 20, 2026. The token, XMR1, slid from about $494 to below $1 in roughly half an hour. That was a drop of 99.8%.

On-chain records show the token's deployer account sent 5.2 million XMR1 to a newly created wallet. The coins moved in three transfers between 04:46 and 05:16 UTC: two of 100,000 and one of 5,000,000. Before the moves, the deployer controlled 93% of supply.

The seller then dumped into thin liquidity. Bitquery data show 363,804 tokens sold for $13.5 million to 388 buyers. A few large buyers accounted for most of the proceeds. About 4.83 million tokens stayed in the wallet.

Next, the proceeds went into ETH through CoW Protocol on Arbitrum, with $13.22 million in USDC swapped. The funds were then bridged out via Socket, Mayan and Stargate. Roughly 4,836 ETH landed in a fresh wallet.

Lookonchain flagged the address, and Scam Sniffer called it suspected theft. Nobody yet knows whether this was a hack or authorized use, since the transfers needed the deployer's main key. That gap raises hard questions about Wagyu's wallet security and what actually backs XMR1.

Spot XMR, a separate asset, traded near $463.86 that day, while Hyperliquid XMR futures sat near $482.

Monero Slips Under Both Averages as Sellers Extend a Monthly Slide

Monero (XMR) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

XMR changed hands near $461 at last check, down about 7% over the past 24 hours.

The bigger problem is where price sits relative to its trend lines. A moving average smooths out daily swings to show the general direction over a set period. XMR trades well below its 50-day average near $551, which now acts as a ceiling. It also slipped just under its 200-day average, around $474, a line many traders treat as the boundary between a healthy and a broken trend.

Losing both averages at once is a bearish setup. It means short-term and long-term buyers are now holding at a loss.

The slide started well before the XMR1 incident. Monero is down about 17% over the past week and roughly 23% over the past month. Sellers were already in control when the wrapped token collapsed.

Wider market weakness adds to the strain. Bitcoin fell about 3.9% to near $61,473, and Ether dropped roughly 4.4% to around $1,733. When the two largest coins retreat, smaller assets like XMR rarely find buyers on their own.

Momentum Nears Exhaustion Without Turning

The daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 31. That reading is weak and close to the oversold line at 30. It has not crossed it, though, so there is no clear signal that selling has run its course.

A dip below 30 would show sellers are tiring, but it would not mark a bottom on its own.

Other gauges point the same way. The MACD, which tracks shifts in momentum, remains below its signal line. In plain terms, downside momentum is still building rather than fading.

Trend strength readings also confirm a real trend, and sellers are leading it. Short bounces in this setup often attract fresh selling instead of new buyers.

Why $500 Caps Any Relief Rally

The first real ceiling sits near $500, the nearest resistance on the daily chart. XMR traded there before this week's drop. Buyers who got in there now have a chance to exit near breakeven, so any bounce into that zone is likely to meet supply.

A close above that level would ease some pressure. Bulls would then need to clear $522 to show the slide has paused. Until both levels fall, rallies look like chances to sell.

The downside picture is more worrying. Nearest support sits far lower, around $169, with the next floor near $145. That leaves a wide gap with few clear levels to slow a decline.

If the 200-day area gives way for good, price could fall quickly through that empty space.

Two Paths for XMR Over the Next Three Days

XMR's direction hinges on how price reacts at first resistance.

  • Bullish: A daily close above first resistance would open a move toward the next barrier overhead. That would show buyers absorbing the supply left from before this week's drop. The setup fails if price slips back under the 200-day average.
  • Bearish: A rejection at first resistance keeps sellers in charge and pushes price deeper below the 200-day line. With support far below, losses could build quickly. A close above the next barrier would cancel this view.

Rallies Remain Selling Opportunities for Now

The trend still favors sellers. Bounces toward resistance look like exits for now. Trimming exposure there makes more sense than chasing a turn.

Risk cuts both ways. The gap down to support is wide, so a breakdown could move fast. Momentum near oversold territory can also spark sharp short squeezes that punish late sellers.

The post XRP Supply Shortage on Binance Tops July Levels, CryptoQuant Analyst Says appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
US spot XRP (XRP) ETFs have gone 15 straight trading days without an inflow, their longest drought since launch. Meanwhile, XRP supply on Binance has tightened past its July level.

Thin exchange supply can limit selling pressure. However, it only supports prices when buyers show up. That puts the spotlight on ETF investors, who have stayed away since late October.

October 29 Was the Last Day XRP ETFs Took In Money

The funds last drew a net inflow of $8.43 million on October 29, SoSoValue data shows. Since then, they have shed $26.29 million. The previous longest dry spell lasted 8 trading days, from March 5 to 16.

The outflows now span 3 straight weeks. The funds lost $6.14 million on November 17 alone. That followed $19.13 million in withdrawals during the week ending November 13, an 8-month weekly high.

Total net assets slid to $1.08 billion by November 19, down from $1.77 billion on September 25.

Still, cumulative net inflows since launch stand near $1.78 billion. Existing holders have largely stayed, while new money has paused.

On Binance, the picture looks different. CryptoQuant’s Supply Shortage Index tracks how scarce XRP is on the exchange.

The index reached 2.4 on November 19, above its July 6 reading of 2.09, analyst Amr Taha noted. Readings above 2 point to severe tightness.

XRP whales have been pulling coins off the exchange too. They withdrew over $127 million net between November 10 and 16, analyst Darkfost reported.

However, Darkfost added that part of that flow may be internal Binance transfers. He saw similar moves after the exchange’s $6.3 billion hack, when it rebuilt reserves.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

Can Tight Supply Lift the XRP Price Without ETF Buyers?

XRP price stood at $0.96581 at press time, according to BeInCrypto Markets data. The token has lost 3.61% over the past week.

Risk-adjusted returns also look weak. XRP’s 30-day Sharpe ratio sits near -0.41. A negative reading means its recent returns have fallen short of the risk its price swings carry.

XRP also trades below its 200-day moving average, which sits near $1.26. Taha said tighter supply could help a recovery if buyers return. On its own, though, it does not confirm a reversal.

Arab Chain pointed to improving Sharpe readings and a reclaim of key technical levels as the signals to watch.

A return of XRP ETF inflows would be the first sign that demand is meeting Binance’s thin supply.

title: Bitrue Black Friday Offers 60,000 USDT and Covers New Users’ First Trade
description:

The post Bitrue Black Friday Offers 60,000 USDT and Covers New Users’ First Trade appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Bitrue covers new users’ first-trade losses in its Black Friday campaign, which runs from Nov. 20 to Dec. 3, 2026, at 8:00 UTC. The campaign, announced by the global cryptocurrency exchange on Friday, combines loss protection for new spot and futures traders with two trading leaderboards and a Black Friday Surprise Box, with total rewards of 60,000 USDT. Full details are available on the campaign page.

The campaign is built around the first trade, which is often the main hurdle for new users. New users can receive up to 400 USDT in combined welcome rewards across spot and futures, while existing traders can compete for leaderboard prizes.

Loss Protection for New Spot and Futures Traders

For spot trading, newly registered users with no prior spot trades who make a first purchase of at least 50 USDT in BTC or ETH, and hold it until the campaign ends, are covered if the price is at least 20% below their purchase price at the end of the campaign. Bitrue covers the actual loss up to 100 USDT, paid as a futures trial bonus, once per user.

For futures trading, new users receive two benefits:

  • Position trial voucher: a 100 USDT position trial voucher after a first futures trade of at least 100 USDT, available on a first-come, first-served basis.
  • Liquidation protection: if a position is liquidated during the campaign, Bitrue compensates the lost margin on the largest single loss, up to 200 USDT. Protection applies once per trader, to BTC, ETH, XRP and SOL positions with leverage of 10x or lower.

Two Leaderboards With 40,000 USDT in Prizes

The campaign also includes two leaderboards ranked by trading volume:

  • Futures leaderboard: the top 100 traders by futures volume share a 30,000 USDT prize pool, with larger shares for higher ranks. Traders need at least 500 USDT in futures volume to qualify. Prizes include enhanced futures trial bonuses and position trial vouchers.
  • Spot leaderboard: traders rank by total spot volume across all pairs, with a minimum of 100 USDT to qualify, for a share of a 10,000 USDT prize pool.

Both leaderboards update every 30 minutes on the campaign page.

Black Friday Surprise Box

Traders who reach a combined 2,000 USDT in spot and futures volume during the campaign can unlock a Black Friday Surprise Box, drawn from a 10,000 USDT reward pool. The boxes contain bonus rewards and physical prizes, including ski gear, a coffee maker and premium headphones. Physical prizes are limited and allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, and are paid out in the equivalent value in USDT.

“The first trade is where many new users hesitate, so this Black Friday we are taking part of that risk off the table,” Bitrue said in a statement. “New users get loss protection on their first spot and futures trades, and active traders have leaderboards and the Surprise Box to compete for.”

Eligibility and Distribution

Participants register through the campaign page. After the campaign ends, Bitrue will confirm eligible users within 10 business days, and rewards and trial bonuses will be credited to their spot and futures accounts. Accounts involved in bulk sign-ups from the same device or IP address, or in wash trading, are not eligible. Final rewards are subject to Bitrue’s review.

Futures trading involves significant risk, and loss protection under the campaign is limited to the conditions and caps set out in the campaign rules.

About Bitrue

Founded in 2018, Bitrue is a trusted global cryptocurrency exchange with over eight years of industry experience, serving more than 40 million users worldwide. Bitrue was the first exchange to list XRP as a base pair and continues to offer one of the broadest selections of XRP trading pairs available on any global exchange, alongside a growing suite of tokenized real-world assets, staking products, Launchpool offerings, and Bitrue AI, its free AI-powered trading bot, visit bitrue.com.

Cryptocurrency trading, especially futures trading, involves significant risk of loss. title: Bitcoin-Backed Lending Goes Live On Sui As Hashi Launches With 20+ Partners
description: Bitcoin holders have a new way to access liquidity without selling their BTC. Hashi, a Bitcoin finance infrastructure protocol built on Sui, has officially launched on mainnet with more than 20 partners supporting lending, custody, and decentralized financial services. The launch marks an important development for Bitcoin-backed lending, transforming a previously experimental system into infrastructure […]
fullContent:
Bitcoin holders have a new way to access liquidity without selling their BTC. Hashi, a Bitcoin finance infrastructure protocol built on Sui, has officially launched on mainnet with more than 20 partners supporting lending, custody, and decentralized financial services.

The launch marks an important development for Bitcoin-backed lending, transforming a previously experimental system into infrastructure supporting live financial applications.

Announced on November 19, the rollout includes institutional custody provider Anchorage Digital, lending protocol Fluid, and asset management platforms HoneyB and Upshift.

More importantly, Bitcoin holders can now use BTC-backed tokens as collateral to borrow stablecoins, potentially unlocking liquidity while maintaining their exposure to Bitcoin.

Bitcoin Lending Moves From Testnet To Mainnet

Hashi’s infrastructure connects Bitcoin with financial applications operating on Sui.

Users deposit Bitcoin through the protocol’s custody and signing arrangements, allowing an equivalent amount of hBTC to be issued on Sui. Each hBTC represents a claim backed by Bitcoin at a 1:1 ratio.

That representation can then be used in decentralized lending markets.

Fluid is among the first platforms offering live Bitcoin-backed borrowing, allowing eligible users to deposit hBTC as collateral and borrow USDC.

This means investors can potentially obtain dollar-denominated liquidity without immediately selling their Bitcoin holdings.

The development follows earlier reports about Hashi’s planned mainnet launch, when the project announced more than $500 million in capital commitments from participating institutions.

However, committed capital should not be confused with actual deposits or lending volume. The launch establishes infrastructure; sustained borrowing activity will determine its commercial significance.

Anchorage Digital And Institutional Partners Expand Bitcoin’s Utility

One of the more significant aspects of Hashi’s launch is the involvement of institutional infrastructure providers.

Anchorage Digital supports access through its Porto self-custody wallet, allowing institutions to interact with hBTC-based financial applications.

The company also plans additional settlement capabilities in early 2027.

Meanwhile, HoneyB has introduced Bitcoin and stablecoin vaults using Upshift’s infrastructure. These products aim to connect digital asset holders with managed financial strategies.

Other participating projects include Bluefin, Cetus, Current, and Suilend, which are developing additional Bitcoin-backed markets.

According to the official Sui Foundation announcement, the ecosystem includes more than 20 participants spanning custody, lending, trading, and asset management.

For Bitcoin, this represents another attempt to extend its usefulness beyond conventional trading and long-term storage.

Could Bitcoin-Backed Loans Reduce Selling Pressure?

The broader implications extend beyond one blockchain launch.

Bitcoin investors traditionally have two straightforward options when they need liquidity: sell part of their holdings or borrow against them through a financial intermediary.

Protocols such as Hashi introduce additional borrowing infrastructure, allowing BTC exposure to support loans and other financial products.

This trend is also emerging in alternative Bitcoin lending models, reflecting growing interest in making Bitcoin useful as productive collateral.

In theory, borrowing against Bitcoin could reduce the need for some holders to sell during periods when they require cash.

However, that outcome is not guaranteed.

Borrowers face interest costs, collateral requirements, liquidation risks, and potential losses from smart contract or cross-chain infrastructure failures.

A sharp Bitcoin price decline could trigger liquidations, creating selling pressure rather than reducing it.

A New Chapter For Bitcoin Finance?

Hashi’s mainnet launch demonstrates how Bitcoin is increasingly becoming collateral for financial services operating beyond its original blockchain.

With more than 20 partners involved, the project has established an ecosystem for borrowing, custody, and managed investment products.

The next important indicators will be the amount of BTC deposited, actual stablecoin borrowing, collateral utilization, and whether institutional participation develops into sustained activity.

For long-term Bitcoin supporters, the opportunity is significant: BTC could become more useful without requiring holders to abandon their underlying investment.

But the strongest evidence of success will come from measurable adoption, not launch announcements alone.

No position ended in profit, and not one even broke even. One trade alone did most of the damage. Inside the Crypto Trader’s Perfect Losing Streak Lookonchain shared the
The post Crypto Trader Goes 0 for 10: Every Single Trade Lost, and $192,500 Vanished appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
One crypto trader just pulled off a rare feat: ten trades, ten losses. According to on-chain tracker Lookonchain, the perfect losing streak wiped out about $192,500.

No position ended in profit, and not one even broke even. One trade alone did most of the damage.

Inside the Crypto Trader’s Perfect Losing Streak

Lookonchain shared the wallet address on X so that anyone can verify the sequence of failed trades. As a result, the record quickly drew attention across the crypto community.

The most brutal trade involved DCTY. The wallet spent about $214,700 accumulating the token. Roughly 20 minutes later, it sold the entire position.

That rapid exit locked in a loss of about $162,800, or nearly 76%. Moreover, that single trade accounted for most of the overall losses. It turned a series of smaller misses into a six-figure hit. The other nine tokens added roughly $29,700 in further losses.

“10 trades 10 losses hurts to even read. the trenches are no joke rn, sizing small is the only way i survive them,” one user said on X.

The speed of the drop shows how quickly capital can vanish in volatile or thinly traded tokens.

Why Do Some Traders Lose on Every Position?

Most traders post mixed results, with wins and losses spread over time. Going ten for ten on the downside is rare, even in crypto.

Such a run usually points to poor timing or aggressive entries into fading narratives. Bad luck, combined with large position sizes, can also play a role.

The same volatile period hurt other traders too. High-profile trader James Wynn got liquidated five times. Still, he holds about $3.14 million in long positions across Bitcoin and S&P 500-linked contracts.

His Bitcoin liquidation level sits near $60,177. While Wynn shows resilience under leverage, the anonymous wallet stands out for its consistent failure.

Ultimately, the episode highlights the risks of fast, high-conviction bets on speculative tokens. Without a clear edge or risk management, short-term trading can backfire.

On public blockchains, those losses also become visible almost instantly. As a result, such trades turn into public case studies for other investors.

The post Crypto Trader Goes 0 for 10: Every Single Trade Lost, and $192,500 Vanished appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Hyperliquid Monero Crashes? Wagyu-Linked XMR1 Collapses, $13.2M Flows Into Ethereum
description:
Wagyu XMR1 Monero crashes 99% in Hyperliquid, 5.2 million tokens move from its deployer account, with $13.2 million converted into ETH.
The post Hyperliquid Monero Crashes? Wagyu-Linked XMR1 Collapses, $13.2M Flows Into Ethereum appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
A Monero token crashed 99% on Friday after 5.2 million XMR1 tokens moved from a wallet tied to its creator, triggering a massive sell-off on Hyperliquid. The token, issued through crypto swap service Wagyu, plunged from around $494 to below $1 in 35 minutes. The wallet receiving the tokens sold enough to generate $13.22 million in USDC before converting the proceeds into 7,467 ETH.

Wagyu’s wallet security and the backing behind its wrapped Monero product are being questioned. And the sell-off also sent shockwaves through the Monero market, although native XMR remained a separate asset from the collapsing XMR1 market.

Wagyu-Linked Wallet Moves 5.2 Million XMR1 Before Crash

The incident began this morning when the account responsible for deploying XMR1 transferred tokens to a newly created wallet. Blockchain intelligence firm Bitquery identified three separate transfers between 04:46 and 05:16 UTC. Two transactions moved 100,000 XMR1 each, followed by a much larger transfer of 5 million tokens.

The receiving wallet had been created that morning. It began selling shortly after receiving the tokens, overwhelming buyers on Hyperliquid’s order book. XMR1 had traded near $500 throughout the previous week. Its price then collapsed to $1 within 30 minutes, leaving holders with almost nothing.

Bitquery traced 363,804 tokens sold for $13.5 million. The remaining 4.83 million tokens stayed in the receiving wallet during its investigation. The sell-off also exposed how concentrated XMR1’s supply had been. Before the transfers, its deployer account still controlled 93% of the token’s supply.

Hyperliquid transfers require signatures from the account’s own key, rather than an ordinary trading API wallet. This means whoever authorized the transfers likely had access to the deployer’s main key. Whether someone stole that access or used it legitimately remains unknown.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

388 Buyers Pay $13.5 Million as Proceeds Move Into Ethereum

The damage extended beyond traders watching XMR1 collapse on their screens. It matched the seller’s transactions against 388 accounts that purchased the dumped tokens. One buyer alone paid $3.56 million, while 27 large buyers accounted for 77% of the total proceeds.

The wallet did not leave the money sitting in USDC. It began moving funds through Hyperliquid’s bridge into Arbitrum shortly after selling.

On Arbitrum, the wallet exchanged $13.22 million in USDC for 7,467 ETH through CoW Protocol. It then routed much of the Ethereum through Socket, Mayan, and Stargate. 6,810 ETH then arrived on Ethereum after those bridge transactions. Approximately 4,836 ETH landed in a newly created wallet that had not sent any funds onward.

The investigation also identified 7,348 ETH across three wallets during its tracking window. That left a substantial amount of the proceeds sitting outside the original trading account.

Native Monero Avoids Collapse as Wagyu and Hyperliquid Face Security Questions

Monero (XMR)
24h7d30d1yAll time

The incident has put Wagyu’s bridge infrastructure under scrutiny. XMR1 itself is Monero on Hyperliquid, but through Wagyu’s bridging service. Users can move native XMR into the service and receive XMR1 for trading. They can also reverse the process to recover their Monero.

Native XMR did not suffer the same collapse. Monero continued trading around $470–$482, while XMR1 lost virtually all its market value.

Holders now face a difficult question: Can they still exchange their remaining XMR1 for native Monero?

The incident also comes weeks after Wagyu disclosed a separate data leak on October 28. Researchers identified exposed records potentially linking crypto deposits, Monero receiving addresses, and customer IP addresses.

Wagyu previously said customer funds remained unaffected by that incident. No established connection links the October leak to Friday’s wallet transfers.

The latest investigation also uncovered another potential concern. The same deployer account controls 99.97% of ZEC1, a separate token representing Zcash on Hyperliquid.

title: EU Warns Spain, Czechia on Crypto Tax Data
description:
Summary Commission escalated both DAC8 cases to reasoned opinions Czech DAC8 bill still awaits final approval Foreign platforms still report […]
The post EU Warns Spain, Czechia on Crypto Tax Data appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Summary

  • Commission escalated both DAC8 cases to reasoned opinions
  • Czech DAC8 bill still awaits final approval
  • Foreign platforms still report Spanish and Czech residents
  • Reported totals are not the same as gains

The European Commission sent reasoned opinions to both countries on November 19, the second formal step in its infringement procedure over DAC8, the EU directive that makes crypto platforms report customer activity to tax authorities.

Twelve countries were warned in January; two were escalated

The Commission sent letters of formal notice to twelve member states in January for failing to bring DAC8 into national law on time. Spain and Czechia are the two it has now moved to the next stage, stating that both still fail to fully implement the directive.

A reasoned opinion is the Commission’s formal finding that a country is breaching EU law. Each government now has two months to respond and adopt the missing measures. If they don’t, the Commission can refer the cases to the Court of Justice of the European Union and ask for financial sanctions. Under the EU treaties, a country that fails to notify how it has transposed a directive can face fines in the first court ruling, without the second round of proceedings usually required.

The deadline applies to governments. Investors in either country have nothing to file because of it.

Two countries, two different delays

Spain is not starting from zero. Crypto providers based there already file information returns with the tax agency, covering balances and transactions under forms 172 and 173. The government sent its DAC8 bill to parliament in June 2025, and the finance ministry published a draft royal decree a month later to set out the due-diligence and reporting detail. Seventeen months after the bill went to parliament, Brussels still considers the job unfinished.

Czechia has further to go. The government sent its bill to the Chamber of Deputies on February 5, 2026, after the directive’s January 1 deadline had already passed, as the finance minister told deputies. In October, the Chamber’s bill record listed it at second reading. It still needs a final vote, Senate approval and the president’s signature. The Czech Financial Administration has treated 2026 as the first reporting year regardless, but providers still have no adopted law to report under.

The Commission’s announcement does not list which provisions each country is missing.

Why the gap sits on the outgoing side

DAC8 assigns reporting to the country where a platform is authorised, not the country where its customer lives. That design determines which flows the Spanish and Czech delays can disrupt.

Inbound: largely unaffected

A Spanish resident trades on a platform authorised in Ireland. The platform reports to Ireland’s Revenue, which passes the data to Spain under existing automatic-exchange arrangements. Ireland has transposed DAC8, so Spain’s unfinished law does not stop this flow.

Outbound: where the uncertainty is

A German resident trades on a platform authorised in Spain or Czechia. That platform owes its DAC8 report to Madrid or Prague. Without complete national rules, its legal duty to collect tax residence details and report is less certain. So is the data Germany expects to receive.

That’s why delays in two countries are an EU-wide problem. Every other member state counts on Spanish and Czech authorities to send data about its residents.

The coverage also extends beyond EU platforms. DAC8 is the EU’s version of the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, and the directive requires operators from outside the EU that serve EU customers without authorisation under MiCA, the EU’s crypto-markets regulation, to register in one member state and report there.

The DAC8 calendar

  1. January 1, 2026 – first year of reportable crypto activity begins
  2. January 2026 – formal notices to twelve member states
  3. November 19, 2026 – reasoned opinions to Spain and Czechia
  4. Mid-January 2027 – two-month response window closes
  5. May 31, 2027 – filing deadline for Irish-authorised providers; other countries set their own
  6. September 30, 2027 – first exchanges of 2026 data between EU tax authorities, per the Commission

A €10,000 report, a €2,000 gain

When the data arrives, it comes as totals. Revenue’s reporting guidance lists the fields: the customer’s name, address, tax residence and tax identification number, plus aggregate amounts, units and transaction counts for each crypto-asset, split by purchases, sales and transfers.

Take an investor who bought Bitcoin for €8,000 and sold it for €10,000. The report shows €10,000 of gross sale proceeds. The gain is €2,000 before fees. If the purchase was made on a different platform, possibly years before DAC8 existed, the selling platform has no record of the €8,000 cost. The tax authority sees the larger number unless the investor supplies the smaller one.

The directive leaves the tax itself to each country. Coindoo’s look at Greece’s proposed 10% rate and €500 exemption shows the choices national governments still make on rates, cost basis and losses. A DAC8 report feeds those rules but replaces none of them.

READ MORE:

Is Bitcoin Dead? Jack Mallers Points to Its History

Wallet withdrawals leave a trace, not a trail

Moving coins into self-custody does not remove them from the report. The directive requires platforms to report the aggregate value and units of transfers to blockchain addresses not known to belong to another crypto provider or financial institution.

The record stops at the withdrawal. DAC8 does not follow coins after they leave the platform, establish who controls the receiving address, or give authorities access to private keys. A withdrawal to an investor’s own hardware wallet and a payment to a stranger can therefore look the same in the report. Only the investor’s records show which one it was.

Records that explain a reported transfer

  • Purchase confirmations showing price paid and fees
  • Withdrawal transaction IDs matched to the receiving deposit
  • A list of the wallet addresses you control
  • Annual statements from every platform you used

The UK’s tax authority deals with the same reconciliation problem under its own rules, as Coindoo’s UK crypto tax explainer shows.

What to watch in January

By mid-January, Spain and Czechia must either tell the Commission their transposition is complete or risk a referral to the EU Court of Justice. For Czechia, that depends on the bill clearing both chambers in time. For Spain, it depends on finishing both the law and the royal decree that puts it into practice.

Investors in both countries are already covered on the inbound side by every platform authorised elsewhere in the EU. What remains open is how fully Spanish and Czech platforms will report their 2026 activity, and what Madrid and Prague can send to the rest of the bloc when the first exchanges are due.

title: Michael Saylor Explains When Strategy Buys Bitcoin — And Why It Sometimes Chooses STRC Instead
description: Michael Saylor has offered a closer look at how Strategy decides between buying more Bitcoin and repurchasing its preferred shares, revealing a capital allocation approach that goes beyond accumulating BTC whenever prices fall. In a November 20 post on X, the Strategy executive chairman shared highlights from the company’s latest investor Q&A, featuring CEO Phong […]
fullContent:
Michael Saylor has offered a closer look at how Strategy decides between buying more Bitcoin and repurchasing its preferred shares, revealing a capital allocation approach that goes beyond accumulating BTC whenever prices fall.

In a November 20 post on X, the Strategy executive chairman shared highlights from the company’s latest investor Q&A, featuring CEO Phong Le and host Natalie Brunell. The discussion addressed Bitcoin per share, shareholder value, preferred-stock repurchases, and the company’s ability to meet financial obligations during prolonged market downturns.

The timing is particularly interesting. As institutional Bitcoin exposure continues to attract attention, Strategy is demonstrating that managing its financial obligations can be just as important as expanding its Bitcoin treasury.

How do we decide when to buy Bitcoin and when to buy back $STRC?

Why Strategy Sometimes Chooses STRC Over Bitcoin

During the investor discussion, Saylor and Le examined the conditions under which Strategy issues equity, purchases Bitcoin, or repurchases STRC, its variable-rate preferred stock.

The distinction matters because each transaction serves a different purpose.

Purchasing Bitcoin expands Strategy’s exposure to the digital asset. Repurchasing STRC, particularly when shares trade below their $100 stated amount, can reduce outstanding preferred obligations and improve the company’s financial flexibility.

Strategy’s latest disclosures illustrate the difference.

Between November 9 and November 15, the company purchased 485 BTC while spending approximately $228.1 million repurchasing STRC shares. The Bitcoin acquisition cost roughly $33.4 million.

That means Strategy allocated substantially more capital to preferred-stock repurchases than direct Bitcoin purchases during that reporting period.

However, this does not necessarily indicate declining confidence in Bitcoin. Instead, the company appears to be balancing long-term BTC accumulation with the financial structure supporting that strategy.

Similar questions about corporate Bitcoin holdings have become increasingly relevant as investors examine how companies manage their digital asset treasuries.

Michael Saylor Highlights Bitcoin Per Share

Another important topic from the November 20 discussion was Bitcoin per share, a metric Strategy uses to evaluate how its financing decisions affect shareholders.

Saylor distinguished between gross and net Bitcoin per share, explaining why investors with different time horizons may interpret the measures differently.

Gross Bitcoin per share reflects the company’s Bitcoin exposure relative to its assumed diluted share base, while net Bitcoin per share accounts for relevant financial claims and liabilities.

The broader question is whether Strategy can increase the economic value attributable to shareholders through its capital-market activities, rather than relying entirely on Bitcoin price appreciation.

This is particularly relevant when the company issues new shares to finance acquisitions or repurchases.

Although additional Bitcoin purchases can increase total holdings, issuing equity also changes the ownership denominator. As a result, the number of BTC held by Strategy is not the only metric investors should monitor.

Growing institutional Bitcoin positions reinforce the importance of understanding how different financial structures provide exposure to BTC.

Can Strategy Keep Buying Bitcoin During A Downturn?

Strategy’s financial resilience was another central theme of the Q&A.

According to its latest reporting, the company held 850,849 BTC as of November 15, alongside approximately $4.9 billion in US dollar assets.

Its dollar reserves and other liquid assets are intended to help support preferred dividends, debt obligations, and broader treasury management.

The company has also reported approximately 3.4 years of coverage for interest and dividend obligations at prevailing rates.

These financial considerations are detailed in Strategy’s official third-quarter 2026 financial results, which provide additional context for its Bitcoin treasury and capital-market activities.

That liquidity provides a buffer against prolonged Bitcoin weakness, although future financing conditions, dividend rates, and market volatility remain important considerations.

For Bitcoin investors, the central takeaway is that Strategy’s accumulation model is becoming more sophisticated.

Rather than treating every available dollar as an automatic Bitcoin purchase, management is weighing the benefits of increasing BTC holdings against strengthening the financial instruments that support those holdings.

Saylor’s latest remarks suggest that Strategy still sees Bitcoin as its core long-term asset, while capital management is playing an increasingly important role in determining how the company expands its exposure.

title: Two New Ways to Borrow Against Bitcoin
description:
DeFi lender Aave voted on 9 November to add a market where users can lock native bitcoin and borrow USDt and other stablecoins on Ethereum. The incoming vault keeps coins…
The post Two New Ways to Borrow Against Bitcoin appeared first on Bitfinex blog.
fullContent:
DeFi lender Aave voted on 9 November to add a market where users can lock native bitcoin and borrow USDt and other stablecoins on Ethereum. The incoming vault keeps coins on the Bitcoin network locked in a vault with no custodian.

The technology comes from bitcoin infrastructure provider Babylon, which calls the product Trustless Bitcoin Vaults. Babylon says it aims to launch late 2026, starting with a restricted phase that limits users and volume. Aave’s DAO vote drew 76 voters carrying about 357,000 AAVE tokens of voting power with none opposed.

Institutions Get a Regulated Custodial Route

Soon after, on 16 November, crypto lender Abra announced dollar loans to institutions against bitcoin, ether and solana in partnership with Intercontinental Exchange, owner of the New York Stock Exchange. The coins are deposited to a segregated wallet at ICE Digital Trust, a trust company chartered in New York. They are not re-pledged or lent on and leave only under controls agreed by borrower, lender and custodian.

“Historically, borrowing against Bitcoin meant trusting your lender with the asset. That model is done,” said Bill Barhydt, Founder and CEO of Abra. “With ICE Digital Trust, the collateral sits with a qualified custodian. … This is what digital assets for institutions are supposed to look like.”

The two products are evidence of the crypto market’s increasing sophistication as teams develop products tailored to the needs of institutional and individual investors. For the former, fully regulated solutions are rolling out in partnership with professional custodians, and, for those staying true to the self-custody ethos, decentralised markets are improving their own custody models. 

Lending Recovers While Custody Models Diverge

Crypto lending has already been through one collapse and recovery. After peaking in 2021 at $69.37 billion, the market plunged in 2022 after the bankruptcies of centralised lenders like Celsius and BlockFi, which had engaged in opaque and risky lending practices.  

Galaxy Research noted in a report released in August 2026 that a new peak was reached in crypto-backed lending in the third quarter of 2025, of $78.69 billion in loans, however since then the market has declined reaching $56.16 billion by June 2026.

Tether, the largest centralised lender in Galaxy’s tally, reported $14.18 billion of secured loans at the end of September, up from $13.45 billion in June. Onchain and centralised lenders are close in size. Galaxy puts on-chain venues at 59 percent of crypto-backed lending at the end of June and centralised lenders at 41 percent.

ICE and Abra offer institutions a regulated custodian, a credit approval and a written contract. Abra says it and its predecessors have facilitated more than $2 billion of digital asset loans since 2021. Naturally, the borrower must depend on a third party to reliably fulfil its obligations.

On the new Aave market, a depositor locks BTC in a Taproot UTXO on the Bitcoin network — a type of transaction output which applies programmable rules to an amount of unspent bitcoin. “Redemption is governed by on-chain rules (e.g., the depositor repaid their loan) and settles directly to a Bitcoin UTXO controlled by the redeeming party,” according to Babylon. 

Once everyone has signed, the owner activates the vault. The coins stay on Bitcoin. A matching record appears on Ethereum, and it is erased when the vault is withdrawn or liquidated.

However, people are still involved. An approved group of arbitrageurs settle liquidations. Two groups of signers using a 4-of-7 and a 3-of-5 multisig sit over Babylon’s contracts and can pause them at once, which shuts the exits. 

These human interventions can prove useful in the case of bad actors attempting to break the system. While none of these parties holds the coins or can move them individually, there is a certain amount of trust still at work. 

For bitcoin holders, the question has increasingly become which risk they want to be paid for. Borrowers now face the same choice. One model asks them to trust a regulated custodian and a contract. The other asks them to trust code and operators working within well-defined limits. 

Neither model requires them to trust the lender with the coins, which is what failed in 2022. The custodial version is open to institutions today and has the potential to offer a route to crypto lending traditional capital requires. Onchain solutions continue to innovate, however, and Babylon’s native bitcoin market on Aave has the potential to provide DeFi solutions to a new user base. 

The post Two New Ways to Borrow Against Bitcoin appeared first on Bitfinex blog.

title: How Bitcoin Treasury Companies Reach Income Investors
description:
In 2025, as bitcoin breached $125,000 and hit a new all-time high, some equity managers were not able to get exposure. Their remits didn’t allow them to hold coins directly…
The post How Bitcoin Treasury Companies Reach Income Investors appeared first on Bitfinex blog.
fullContent:
In 2025, as bitcoin breached $125,000 and hit a new all-time high, some equity managers were not able to get exposure. Their remits didn’t allow them to hold coins directly or own a bitcoin ETF.

Instead, some gained exposure by buying shares in bitcoin treasury companies. Demand was strong enough to allow the largest bitcoin treasury company, Strategy, to raise $25.3 billion, which it says made it the largest issuer of US equity that year, with about eight percent of the total.

But there was another pool of investors that couldn’t access treasury company stock either — fixed-income allocators. It is this market that is now being targeted by bitcoin treasury companies as they exit a turbulent 2026.

“What’s Next for Bitcoin Treasury Companies” panel at the Future of Capital Markets Summit in Lugano. From left: Jesse Knutson (Bitfinex Securities), Alexandre Laizet (Capital B), Matt Cole (Strive), Richard Byworth (BYZ Partners), Raphael Zagury (Twenty One Capital) and Sean Bill (former Co-Founder BSTR).

Preferred Stock Opens the Fixed-Income Market

Fixed income funds generally can’t buy equity and may not be able to buy convertible bonds. Strategy’s Stretch (STRC), launched in 2025, is a dividend-paying preferred stock with a variable annual dividend rate currently set at 12 percent, giving this pool of capital an instrument within their remit.

The premiums on treasury company common stock narrowed during the 2026 downturn but, thanks to the popularity of the preferred instruments, some were able to keep accumulating. Strive raised $630 million in October through a new preferred equity issuance, and STRC has traded close to its $100 par value.

At the 2026 Future of Capital Markets Summit in Lugano, Switzerland, Jesse Knutson, Head of Operations at Bitfinex Securities, chaired a panel in which executives from the sector set out how they are offering bitcoin-style returns, without the volatility. 

Offering new bitcoin-based investments brings more capital into the bitcoin market, which allows treasury companies to issue more common stock. And, as the market for their instruments grows, they become eligible for more investors. The risk is that this virtuous circle depends on bitcoin returning more than the dividend yield pays. In a down year, the flow can reverse. 

As bitcoin fell from above $126,000 last October to below $60,000 in 2026, treasury companies came under pressure. By 24 July VanEck’s Matthew Sigel had counted at least nine that had liquidated or abandoned their strategies. And, by 21 September only four of the 20 largest digital asset treasury companies traded above the value of their holdings. 

The companies that survived came out with stronger balance sheets, cash to cover more than a year of dividend payments and even more bitcoin in their treasury. Strategy has a cash reserve of approximately $4.75 billion and continues bitcoin purchases. In another example, in August, H100 Group more than tripled its holdings to 3,506 bitcoin by acquiring two Norwegian treasury companies in an all-share deal. 

Byworth said the continued interest in bitcoin treasury companies is due to identifying a new gap in the fixed income markets. Investors are resisting yields of around five percent on government debt when they are able to access  large technology company debt at seven to nine percent. Perpetual preferred stock issued by treasury companies pays between 12-13 percent, and the proceeds are used to buy bitcoin. “What the people across this stage are doing is providing the first proper digital credit tool for the fixed-income market”, Byworth said.

“What’s Next for Bitcoin Treasury Companies” panel at the Future of Capital Markets Summit in Lugano.

Tokenisation Reaches Investors Outside US Markets

But what if you could offer these products in a tokenised manner? Preferred stock opened bitcoin exposure to allocators whose mandates ruled out holding bitcoin. Through tokenisation they can be offered to investors who cannot easily reach US-listed securities at all. 

The barriers are geographical and financial. Martin Baumann, co-founder of bitcoin investment firm CMCC Global, said its funds had previously only been open to professional investors, with a minimum subscription of $1 million. 

Bitcoin treasury companies and professionally managed bitcoin strategy companies were recently listed on Bitfinex Securities where they can be bought in fractions of a share. “It gives access to people who otherwise just simply wouldn’t be able to participate,” Baumann said. Offering digital credit products taps one pool of investors barred from participating in bitcoin and tokenising them taps a global pool of investors who can subscribe “with a click of a mouse button”. 

A year after they were among the market’s most watched sectors, bitcoin treasury companies have been through what Byworth called “the first cycle”. It stripped away the premiums that funded their early growth and exposed the companies that had no other way to raise capital. 

The ones still accumulating found one. Digital credit gave Strategy and Strive access to fixed-income allocators who could not hold bitcoin or common stock, and tokenisation is starting to open the same instruments to investors outside US markets. Whether that grows the sector depends on the arithmetic underneath it. 

Preferred stock paying between 12 and 13 percent adds value only if bitcoin returns more than that over time. If it does, every new pool of investors brings more capital into bitcoin, and the companies that came through this year are well positioned for the next wave.

The post How Bitcoin Treasury Companies Reach Income Investors appeared first on Bitfinex blog.
