title: Introducing Kraken TV: live crypto markets and news on the big screen
description:
Live prices, movers and news on your television, built to be read from across the room or up close.
The post Introducing Kraken TV: live crypto markets and news on the big screen appeared first on Kraken Blog.
fullContent:
TL;DR

  • Kraken TV is a new app for Apple TV, Android TV (including Google TV) and Amazon Fire TV that turns your television into a live crypto market screen. No account, no sign-in and no setup: install it and it works.
  • The new News experience offers a headline-first feed, a saved reading list and a scrolling Market Wire ticker, plus Small, Medium and Big layouts that adapt to how far you’re sitting from the screen, which you can change at any time.
  • An ambient screensaver keeps the latest prices, news and events for your chosen coins on screen for hours, without your TV going to sleep.
  • Kraken TV is a companion to the Kraken app: scan a QR code to continue on your phone and trade the coin there. No trading happens on the TV.

Crypto markets, now on the big screen

Crypto doesn’t stop moving, and your TV doesn’t have to either. Today we’re introducing Kraken TV, a new app for Apple TV, Android TV and Amazon Fire TV that turns your television into a live crypto market screen. Prices, movers and news are all designed to be read from across the room or up close.

There’s nothing to set up. Install Kraken TV and it works, with no account and no sign-in.

Live markets at a glance

Kraken TV opens on Markets, with live prices, 24-hour change and sparklines for the assets you care about, plus the biggest movers so you can see what’s heating up.

A built-in asset picker lets you choose which assets to prioritize, and your selection follows you across the app.

News you can read from the couch

News is the newest part of Kraken TV, and it’s the reason for this launch. We built a browsable, headline-first feed that’s easy to read from the couch:

  • Filter your feed by category or by asset to focus on what matters to you.
  • Open any story to read the full article on screen.
  • Star a story while you’re reading and it lands in your saved reading list.
  • Follow the Market Wire, a scrolling ticker that runs along the bottom of the screen.
  • Scan the QR code on a story that catches your eye to continue on your phone and trade that coin in the Kraken app.

Coin pages built around the news

Select any asset from the grid and you’ll land on its own coin page, built around that coin’s news. It’s a quick way to see what’s driving an asset without leaving the couch.

A screensaver that keeps the market in view

Kraken TV doubles as an ambient screensaver. Build your list of coins, and it keeps their latest prices, news and events on screen for hours without your TV going to sleep.

You stay in the loop without staring at the screen or hunting for information, which makes it a natural fit for a waiting area, a shared space or simply some background atmosphere.

Big, Small, and Medium: one app, three ways to read

The first time you open Kraken TV, we ask how far away you’re sitting. The app then lays itself out for that distance, and you can change your choice at any time:

  • Big uses bigger type and fewer rows, so everything stays legible from across the room.
  • Small shows denser detail for when you’re sitting close.
  • Medium sits in between.

Same app, three genuinely different reading experiences.

Built for a remote control

Kraken TV is designed for a remote, not a cursor. A left-hand rail gives you quick access to every surface, and each one opens as its own window, titled in the header so you always know where you are.

A companion to the Kraken app

Kraken TV is a companion to the Kraken app, not a replacement for it. When something on screen is worth acting on, like a story about a coin you follow, scan the QR code to continue in the Kraken app on your phone and trade from there. No trading happens on the TV.

Available on Apple TV, Android TV and Amazon Fire TV

One build covers Apple TV, Android TV (including Google TV) and Amazon Fire TV. Kraken TV is our first app on the Amazon Appstore. Download Kraken TV on your streaming device, pick how far away you’re sitting, and put the market on the big screen:

  • Apple TV (App Store)
  • Google TV/Android TV (Google Play)
  • Fire TV (Amazon Appstore)

The post Introducing Kraken TV: live crypto markets and news on the big screen appeared first on Kraken Blog.

title: Protocol 42 Opens Agentic Mining for AI Trading on BNB Chain
description:
Protocol 42 switched on Agentic Mining at 06:00 UTC on 19 November 2026. AI agents can now place real-fund trades across its 42 markets. The same window opened Agentic Pass. That BNB Chain NFT funds agent wallets and pays holders in points, not P&L. What Agentic Mining Changes for AI Trading Agents trade live capital […]
The post Protocol 42 Opens Agentic Mining for AI Trading on BNB Chain appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
Protocol 42 switched on Agentic Mining at 06:00 UTC on 19 November 2026. AI agents can now place real-fund trades across its 42 markets. The same window opened Agentic Pass. That BNB Chain NFT funds agent wallets and pays holders in points, not P&L.

What Agentic Mining Changes for AI Trading

Agents trade live capital on Creator Markets. They no longer wait on a human click for every order. Pass mint proceeds go into the agents' trading wallets. Holders receive starter points and a share of the weekly Agent Pool. They can also chase extra points on a Pass leaderboard. A wallet that still holds one Pass at the weekly snapshot gets a 1.7-times points multiplier. That boost covers all Protocol 42 trades for that week. Agent fills sit in public view after a short delay. Readers can check what the bots did.

How Agentic Pass Funds the Agent Wallets

Each NFT costs 200 USDT in the first mint wave. Three AI agents take that capital. The opening series issues 2,000 Passes per agent and 6,000 Passes in total. Mint money lands in a separate Safe 2-of-3 multisig for each agent. Each agent may spend at most 100 USDT on a single trade. It must hold a Creator Market position for at least one hour before it can sell. Trading pauses if the wallet balance falls sharply.

Pass buyers earn 42 Points rather than a claim on trading profit. The mint stake is not withdrawable or refundable. Agent gains stay in the trading float. Losses do not erase points already earned or the 1.7-times trade multiplier. Binance's Agentic Wallet is one of the main entry ramps. That wallet isolates agent funds from a user's main balance. Users can set spend limits and keep a bot running around the clock. Protocol 42 already sits inside the Binance Wallet stack through earlier Creator Market tools. Agentic Mining moves those rails from human-led clicks to agent-led books.

Why Public Agent Logs Matter for Thin Markets

Long-tail markets often starve when market makers refuse unhedgeable risk. Protocol 42 wants agents to quote and trade without a human maker on every tape. That is the core AI and blockchain stake in this launch. Public Agent Terminal logs show fills about 15 minutes after execution. The delay keeps the machine book from becoming a black box. It also blocks instant copy-trade signals.

The launch still does not prove the agents will make money. They may deepen thin markets, or they may only farm points. The 1.7-times Pass multiplier and the weekly Agent Pool reward participation first. They do not guarantee a profitable bot. Protocol 42 opened Agentic Mining with real funds, a BNB Chain Pass, and a public trade log. The next print that matters is whether the agents keep trading once the points heat cools.

The post Protocol 42 Opens Agentic Mining for AI Trading on BNB Chain appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.

title: KR1 Turns Venice DIEM Into Live AI Inference Capacity
description:
KR1 put its Venice DIEM to work. The firm is taking a page out of the productive-asset book. It now sells live DIEM AI inference capacity to paying third-party customers. How KR1 Sells DIEM AI Inference on Venice KR1 plc filed the launch on 19 November 2026. The LSE: KR1 announcement opens DIEM infrastructure operations. […]
The post KR1 Turns Venice DIEM Into Live AI Inference Capacity appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
KR1 put its Venice DIEM to work. The firm is taking a page out of the productive-asset book. It now sells live DIEM AI inference capacity to paying third-party customers.

How KR1 Sells DIEM AI Inference on Venice

KR1 plc filed the launch on 19 November 2026. The LSE: KR1 announcement opens DIEM infrastructure operations. The filing builds on a Venice update from 12 November. DIEM is Venice’s inference token. Each staked DIEM supplies US$1 of daily credit to run AI models on Venice. The company holds 557 DIEM, bought separately from its VVV position. VVV is Venice’s native token. That stake equals about US$557 of daily model credit. KR1 can sell that credit rather than leave it idle.

In the 90 days to 16 November 2026, KR1 fulfilled about 1.92 million third-party requests through Surplus Intelligence. Those runs served 101.5 billion AI model tokens. On Surplus Intelligence, KR1 picks which models to list and sets the price. When the marketplace matches a buyer to one of those offers, Venice runs the model on KR1’s credits. KR1 is paid in USDC. KR1 also feeds DIEM into Diem Relay. That pool stakes supplier tokens on Venice and sells the resulting inference capacity. Suppliers take a share of the USDC proceeds in line with their stake, after fees.

What KR1’s October DIEM Yield Shows

October earnings pointed to a 5.45% annualised yield. The figure is estimated on the fair value of DIEM used to supply the marketplace at month-end. KR1 said that rate will move with inference and compute supply and demand. Proceeds arrive in USDC. Income may be reinvested into more productive holdings or used for operating costs. The stated aim is to lift the earning power behind each KR1 share.

Keld van Schreven explained the firm’s model in practice. He is Managing Director and Co-Founder of KR1 plc. Digital assets earn from AI demand while the company keeps the underlying tokens. He said the work goes past buying assets. Knowing which models customers and agents use, and what they pay, helps KR1 pick services, price capacity, and raise utilisation. The London-listed group frames the launch as Technology Infrastructure work. Onchain assets become rented AI capacity instead of a static treasury line. The open question is how durable that 5.45% October print stays. More suppliers may chase the same credits.

The post KR1 Turns Venice DIEM Into Live AI Inference Capacity appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.

title: Probing Ethereum nodes using Sonar
description:
TL;DR
Sonar is a free tool from ProbeLab that probes a single Ethereum node on demand. Give it an ENR and it finds the node over discv5, dials every address the record advertises, runs the libp2p or devp2p handshake, and for consensus-layer nodes exchanges Status and MetaData. Each result is compared with the node’s own ENR and with what our discv5 crawler has recorded about it. Other node identifier formats are also accepted, such as libp2p peerID or enode URL. Sonar is in beta. We would like feedback from client teams and node operators on what else a probe should check.
Why probe a node from the outside
A node can look healthy in its own logs and still be hard for the rest of the network to reach. Common cases:
the ENR advertises an IP or port that is not reachable (NAT, a firewall rule, a public IP that changed)
only some transports work, for example TCP answers but QUIC does not
the ENR and the node’s Status/MetaData disagree (fork digest, attestation or sync-committee subnets, custody group count)
a beacon API or metrics port is open to the internet
The node only sees its own side of these problems. Sonar connects to it as an unknown peer would and shows what happened at each step.



How a probe works
Decode the ENR. Sonar shows every field: node ID, IPv4/IPv6 addresses and ports, the eth2 fork digest and next fork, attnets, syncnets, custody group count, and the eth field that marks an execution-layer node.
Look the node up over discv5. The lookup returns the latest version of the record, so an old ENR is refreshed before any dial.
Dial every advertised address, one at a time. IPv4 and IPv6, TCP and QUIC are dialed and reported separately.
Identify the node. Consensus-layer nodes go through libp2p identify (agent version, protocols, listen addresses). Execution-layer nodes go through the devp2p hello over RLPx (client name and capabilities).
Run the eth2 exchange (consensus-layer nodes only). Sonar requests Status and MetaData, collects the gossipsub topics the node subscribes to, and records any GOODBYE and its reason code.
Read the node’s discv5 routing table, bucket by bucket.
Check the API and metrics ports of the client the node runs.
A probe takes from a few seconds to about half a minute, depending on how many addresses the node advertises and how quickly it answers. Results stream into the page as each step finishes.
What the result shows
Reachability
One row per address: whether it connected, the connection setup time, the RTT, and the full error when a dial fails. The columns on the right show where each address came from: the ENR, libp2p identify, the discv5 lookup, or our crawl history. In the example the node answers on discv5 (UDP 9000), TCP 9000 and QUIC 9001. Identify also reported six private addresses, which Sonar lists but does not dial.



Consensus layer
This card appears only for consensus-layer nodes, the ones whose ENR carries an eth2 field. Any other discv5 participant, such as an execution-layer node or a node from another network that shares the DHT, still gets the reachability, routing table and port checks, but there is no eth2 exchange to run. For a consensus node, the card shows the values from Status and MetaData, next to the same fields in the ENR. The subnet grids compare what the ENR advertises with what the node reports it is subscribed to, for attestation subnets, sync-committee subnets and custody groups. Any mismatch is flagged. If the node sent a GOODBYE, the card shows the code and its meaning (for example 129, too many peers). A node that is full still tells us its GOODBYE reason, and some clients (Teku, for example) send their gossip topics before hanging up.



Routing table
How many peers sit in each bucket of the node’s discv5 routing table, how long the read took, and how many other nodes in our last crawl have this node in their own tables. Hovering a cell lists the peers in that bucket by ENR, and each one links to its own Sonar result, so you can walk from a node to its neighbours.

Sonar is in beta. We would like feedback from client teams and node operators on what else a probe should check.

Why probe a node from the outside

A node can look healthy in its own logs and still be hard for the rest of the network to reach. Common cases:

  • the ENR advertises an IP or port that is not reachable (NAT, a firewall rule, a public IP that changed)
  • only some transports work, for example TCP answers but QUIC does not
  • the ENR and the node’s Status/MetaData disagree (fork digest, attestation or sync-committee subnets, custody group count)
  • a beacon API or metrics port is open to the internet

The node only sees its own side of these problems. Sonar connects to it as an unknown peer would and shows what happened at each step.

How a probe works

  1. Decode the ENR. Sonar shows every field: node ID, IPv4/IPv6 addresses and ports, the eth2 fork digest and next fork, attnets, syncnets, custody group count, and the eth field that marks an execution-layer node.
  2. Look the node up over discv5. The lookup returns the latest version of the record, so an old ENR is refreshed before any dial.
  3. Dial every advertised address, one at a time. IPv4 and IPv6, TCP and QUIC are dialed and reported separately.
  4. Identify the node. Consensus-layer nodes go through libp2p identify (agent version, protocols, listen addresses). Execution-layer nodes go through the devp2p hello over RLPx (client name and capabilities).
  5. Run the eth2 exchange (consensus-layer nodes only). Sonar requests Status and MetaData, collects the gossipsub topics the node subscribes to, and records any GOODBYE and its reason code.
  6. Read the node’s discv5 routing table, bucket by bucket.
  7. Check the API and metrics ports of the client the node runs.

A probe takes from a few seconds to about half a minute, depending on how many addresses the node advertises and how quickly it answers. Results stream into the page as each step finishes.

Reachability

One row per address: whether it connected, the connection setup time, the RTT, and the full error when a dial fails. The columns on the right show where each address came from: the ENR, libp2p identify, the discv5 lookup, or our crawl history. A node that is full still tells us its GOODBYE reason, and some clients (Teku, for example) send their gossip topics before hanging up.

title: Fourth Circuit Affirms Maryland’s Authority to Regulate Kalshi Prediction Markets
description:
A U.S. appellate court is upholding Maryland's right to enforce its sports wagering laws against Kalshi, marking another win for state oversight over federal preemption claims.
The post Fourth Circuit Affirms Maryland’s Authority to Regulate Kalshi Prediction Markets appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
A U.S. appellate court is affirming Maryland’s authority to enforce its sports wagering laws against the prediction market platform Kalshi.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit says the Commodity Exchange Act does not clearly preempt the state’s gaming laws even for event contracts on a CFTC-regulated designated contract market.

Judge Gregory concurring emphasizes that the regulation of gambling has long been a matter of traditional state police power.

“Because the regulation of gambling has long been a matter of traditional state police power, I would not infer that Congress displaced Maryland’s concurrent authority absent a clear expression of its intent to do so.”

The decision rejects Kalshi’s preemption arguments and finds no impossibility or obstacle to federal objectives.

Maryland Attorney General Anthony G. Brown says the ruling requires Kalshi to meet the same consumer protection standards as every other sportsbook serving Maryland residents.

“When betting platforms operate outside State oversight, Marylanders lose the protections that keep gambling fair and safe.”

“Today’s ruling means Kalshi must meet the same consumer protection standards as every other sportsbook serving Maryland residents.”

The per curiam opinion in case No. 25-1892 was decided November 18, 2026, after arguments on May 7, 2026.

The post Bitcoin Nears $62,862 Mining Cost: Will BTC Price Hold Above This Level or Break Below It? appeared first on 99Bitcoins.
fullContent:
CryptoQuant founder Ki Young Ju noted that Bitcoin (BTC USD) has fallen to the price it costs to mine one Bitcoin. His chart, built from MARA Holdings’ filings, puts the miner’s average cost at $62,862 per coin in the third quarter. Bitcoin dipped to $62,063 on Wednesday and trades near $63,900 on Thursday.

“A break below could pressure public miners and their institutional backers,” Ki wrote on X. Below that price, a miner spends more to produce a coin than the coin is worth.

We checked how that line held up before. Bitcoin closed below $62,862 on 18 days since January 2025, all between June and August of this year. Each time, it was back above the line within a month.

This time, though, two forces push the other way: MARA is selling its Bitcoin, and ETF investors are pulling money out.

BTC USD Below Mining Cost: What Happened the Last Six Times

We compared Binance’s daily BTC USD closes since January 2025 with the $62,862 line. Bitcoin dropped below it in six separate stretches, all this summer.

  • Short dips: five of the six stretches lasted one or two days, in early June, July and on August 1.
  • The long one: from June 23 to July 3, Bitcoin closed below cost 11 days in a row. It hit $57,800 on July 1, its lowest price of the past year.
  • The recovery: 30 days after each stretch ended, Bitcoin was back above the line, but only by 1% to 3% in five cases. The exception was August 1, which was followed by a 25% rally to over $78,000.

So the mining cost has acted as a floor, but a soft one. It stopped the falls without starting a rally, until August.

The cost line also moves. MARA’s cost was close to $60,000 in the second quarter, so this summer’s dips were tested against a slightly lower bar than today’s.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $62K: Did Mara’s $1B BTC Sale Cause It?

MARA Is Selling, and ETF Investors Are Leaving

Two groups that usually support the price are selling instead.

  • MARA: the largest listed miner sold 13,597 BTC for about $1.1 billion over six weeks, at an average of about $81,000, roughly 29% above its own mining cost. It said it would keep selling to fund AI data centers. At today’s price, that margin has shrunk to about 2%.
  • Spot Bitcoin ETFs: these funds, which hold the coin itself, lost a net $239.9 million on Tuesday, November 17, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for $209.5 million. That came a day after IBIT’s first inflow in 11 sessions. Early figures pointed to further outflows on Wednesday.

The miners aren’t giving up, though. The network’s hashrate, the total computing power securing Bitcoin, averaged about 1,015 exahashes per second over the past 30 days. That’s 9% below its November 2025 peak but 13% above its August low. Miners are still adding machines, a sign they expect higher prices later.

DISCOVER: 20+ Next Crypto to Explode in 2026

BTC USD Price Analysis: The Mining Cost and $62,300 Sit Together

On the daily chart, BTC USD trades at $63,879. That is below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $75,252, and its 200-day EMA at $75,625.

  • Support: $62,300, just below the $62,862 mining cost. Bitcoin bounced near it on Sunday and Wednesday, after it also held in February, June, July and August. Below it, $57,800, the July low.
  • Resistance: $65,500, a level Bitcoin bounced from in early 2026 and was turned back from in June, July and August. Above that, $74,300.

BTCUSDT 1D chart. Source: TradingView

Path What has to happen Next stop
Bullish A daily close above $65,500 as ETF outflows stop $74,300, the March-September level
Sideways Price holds between $62,300 and $65,500 A range near the mining cost
Bearish A daily close below $62,300 and the mining cost $57,800, the July low

BTC USD has climbed back above the mining cost after all six dips this year. This time, miners are sellers and ETF money is leaving, so another recovery needs buyers to show up, not just sellers to stop.

fullContent:
After a much anticipated retail step, HSBC opened an HSBC RedCoin tokenised fund path for Hong Kong clients. Eligible customers can spend HSBC RedCoin in the HSBC HK App. They buy Class SD units of HSBC Global Money Funds – Hong Kong Dollar. Interestingly, the offer lands while RedCoin still sits early on PayMe rails and bank apps.

HSBC RedCoin Tokenised Fund Draws Orders Despite Token Rails

HSBC Global Asset Management set the Class SD public launch date at 18 November 2026. According to the October 2026 product brochure, one token represents one Class SD unit. Ownership sits on a permissioned blockchain. Meanwhile, the mutual funds page lists tokenised funds as now available on the HSBC HK App. The same page sets the entry at HKD100, funded with RCHKD100. According to the Guide to Tokenised Funds, subscription and settlement use HSBC RedCoin. Class SD Units can only be subscribed and redeemed through Eligible Distributors. The manager appoints those distributors.

The fund itself launched on 1 March 1991. According to HSBC Asset Management, fund size was HKD 20,774 million as of 30 September 2026. That is about HK$20.8 billion in short-term HKD deposits and money market paper. Weighted average maturity was 32 days on that date. Class SD carries a 0.30% management fee. Fitch rates the fund AAAmmf. Dividends declared on each business day reinvest into Class SD the same day. Cash dividend payouts are not available on that class. Capital preservation is not guaranteed. According to the firm, Class SD is a new share class on the same fund, not a new fund. It keeps the same underlying money market exposure as the older share classes. Dealing is daily on every dealing day. Switching out of the tokenised class is not permitted.

Meanwhile, RedCoin (RCHKD) is the licensed HKD stablecoin HSBC put on PayMe on 23 October 2026, after an early user ramp. The launch note said a tokenised money market share class would follow on the HSBC HK App. That rail is now live for the Class SD window. The brochure says Eligible Distributors must be SFC-licensed for dealing in securities or virtual asset trading. Tokenisation adds blockchain, custody, and distributor risks. Those sit beside ordinary money market risk. According to HSBC, buying units is not placing a bank deposit. The units are not under Hong Kong Monetary Authority deposit supervision. After a much anticipated wait, eligible Hong Kong clients can now clear a HKD money market order with RedCoin inside the banking app.

The post PDAX Lets Stablecoins Fund Philippine Retail Dollar Bonds appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
After a much anticipated Retail Dollar Bonds Tranche 3 window, Philippine Digital Asset Exchange opened a PDAX stablecoin Philippine bonds funding path. Eligible USD stablecoins can fund those bond orders on the live public offer. Interestingly, the window lands while Manila still seeks at least $200 million from three-year onshore dollar notes due 2029.

PDAX Stablecoin Philippine Bonds Draw Orders Despite Friction

The Bureau of the Treasury set the public offer from November 19 to November 24. The issue date is November 27. According to The Philippine Star, citing the Treasury notice of offering, the minimum purchase is $200. The ceiling per order is the dollar equivalent of P500,000. Meanwhile, the final coupon is set through a Dutch auction among Government Securities Eligible Dealers. According to the same report, GCash GBonds and bank channels also take orders beside PDAX.

PDAX users fund the RDB3/USD pair after they hold enough USD. According to PDAX support, eligible USD stablecoins convert to USD in the FX tab at the live rate during set periods. According to Solana, the tokens accepted on the Solana network for this path include PYUSD, USDG, and USDPT. PHP cash-in and direct USD deposits also create USD. Meanwhile, PDAX Securities acts as the broker-dealer. Holdings sit in the investor's National Registry of Scripless Securities account.

PDAX is a Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas-supervised exchange that already sells Philippine government bonds in its app. Bank branches still take dollar retail orders. PDAX routes the same BTr paper through an in-app FX* balance that can start as a stablecoin. According to founder and CEO Nichel Gaba, Filipinos can buy the bonds through the PDAX app from $200. He said they do not need deep wealth or a private banker to reach that dollar paper.

The Offer Terms on the Table

Interestingly, the stablecoin conversion is not an open-ended tap. According to PDAX support, that option runs only in specified periods, and the live pairs sit in the app. Meanwhile, the Treasury can close the offer early or adjust the window. The bonds pay interest in USD on a quarterly schedule after issuance. Principal returns in USD at maturity. PDAX said it charges no primary-offer fees on the RDB 3 window. According to The Philippine Star, this is the third Retail Dollar Bond sale. The prior RDB 2 raise brought in $1.26 billion in October 2023. The maiden sale raised $1.6 billion in 2021. After a much anticipated wait, that stablecoin funding door now clears into the same sovereign paper.

title: OmenX announces $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures and launches on-demand 30-second Bitcoin predictions
description: The Base-native leveraged prediction market platform expands its offering across crypto, global financial assets, sports and esports. Toronto, November 19, 2026 – OmenX, a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform, today announced $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures alongside the launch of its on-demand, 30-second Bitcoin price prediction product. The new product lets users predict whether Bitcoin’s price will rise or fall over the next 30 seconds, with each trade starting its own prediction window. A position opened at 10:00:12 runs until 10:00:42. Users can act when their view forms, with a full 30-second horizon, rather than adapting to the remaining time in a shared market round. Featuring zero-slippage execution and rapid settlement, the product extends the familiar five- and fifteen-minute crypto prediction format to a shorter, individually timed experience. It adds to OmenX’s intraday offering, which spans prediction horizons from 30 seconds to 24 hours, depending on the market. Beyond crypto, OmenX offers directional prediction markets linked to more than 100 global assets, including U.S. equities, futures, ETFs and indices. Its event markets also cover live sports and esports, with sports coverage spanning major football leagues, basketball, American football, ice hockey, baseball and UFC. Leverage has been central to OmenX’s platform from the outset, allowing traders to amplify their exposure on supported event markets. The latest launch builds on that foundation while advancing a broader goal: making prediction markets a practical financial tool for retail users. OmenX organizes the trading decision around a defined question: will an asset’s price be higher or lower at the end of a specified period? Users can express a directional view without purchasing the underlying asset, targeting an exact closing price or constructing an options position that requires decisions about strikes, implied volatility and time decay. “Leverage has been part of OmenX from the start, but our ambition goes beyond adding leverage to prediction markets,” said James, founder and CEO of OmenX. “We want to make global markets easier to participate in. A trader should be able to take a view on Bitcoin, a stock or a sporting event and express it through a clear contract and a timeframe that fits their judgment.” The platform’s emphasis on short, recurring markets provides faster feedback on trading decisions and can reduce the time capital remains committed to individual outcomes. OmenX plans to expand its coverage of traditional and crypto assets while deepening the trading experience across supported markets. About OmenX OmenX is a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform covering crypto, global financial assets, live sports and esports. Through defined outcomes, short settlement cycles and leverage on supported markets, OmenX is building a more accessible way to trade market views. Learn more at omenx.com. Media contact James Zhang Founder at OmenX james@omenx.com

fullContent:
Mutsamudu, Comoros, November 19, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, has released its November 2026 Proof of Reserves (PoR) report, independently audited by Hacken. The report shows MEXC’s solid reserve position, with user assets in every major asset backed by reserves above 1:1, demonstrating MEXC’s ongoing commitment to safeguarding user assets.

Spanning Proof of Liabilities, Proof of Ownership, Reserves Calculation, and Merkle Tree verification, Hacken’s November 2026 audit confirms substantial over-collateralisation across core holdings, standing at 318% for BTC, 122% for USDT, 112% for ETH, and 110% for USDC.

Guided by its user-first philosophy, MEXC continues to enhance transparency to protect user assets and build trust. Since introducing Proof of Reserves in February 2023, MEXC has kept its wallet addresses and reserve data public, and its Merkle Tree system lets users verify at any time that their balances are included, without exposing other users’ data.

 

Reserves provide an extra layer of user protection. MEXC also manages user assets across cold and hot wallets under multi-signature authorization and layered risk controls, and maintains two dedicated funds. The Guardian Fund is set aside for major security events such as exploits and targeted attacks. It holds both USDT and BTC, with BTC added in May and September this year, with plans to reach $500 million within two years. The Futures Insurance Fund absorbs losses exceeding a user’s margin following liquidation, acting as a vital capital buffer during extreme market volatility. To ensure full transparency across MEXC’s risk-protection framework, wallet addresses for the broader Guardian Fund are publicly disclosed, while real-time and historical balances for each trading pair remain accessible via the Insurance Fund Account page.

 

To view the latest Proof of Reserves snapshot and audit report, please visit the MEXC Proof of Reserves page.

Serving users across 170+ markets, MEXC provides simple and efficient access to crypto, stocks, tokenized assets, derivatives, and a growing range of TradFi-linked opportunities through one account and one gateway.

 

With 0 trading fees, deep liquidity, broad asset coverage, and a high-performance trading experience, MEXC is designed for retail users who want to discover earlier, act faster, and trade with fewer barriers. As crypto and traditional finance continue to converge, MEXC is committed to making global opportunities more accessible, helping users trade freely and MEXCmize every opportunity.

fullContent:
A 22-year-old Miami man is accused of making 32 fraudulent wire transfers worth more than $600,000.

Donnell Collier Jr. allegedly carried out an account-takeover scheme tied to a nationwide bank fraud crackdown, according to federal court records, reports CBS12.

Collier faces charges of wire fraud conspiracy, wire fraud and bank fraud.

If convicted, he could face up to 80 years in federal prison.

His arrest was one of five in Florida tied to fraud schemes linked to more than $54 million in losses at over 65 financial institutions nationwide.

The operation involved FBI offices in Miami, Nashville, New York, Columbia, Houston and Omaha.

Four suspects were arrested in South Florida while a fifth South Florida resident was arrested in Central Florida.

Brioden Jean and Derek Val Pierre-Paul are charged in Tennessee with wire fraud conspiracy and two counts of wire fraud.

Kevin Lopez and John Sardinas are charged in Iowa with money laundering conspiracy and four counts of money laundering.

title: Binance Hacker Moves Another $248M of Ethereum as the Exchange Wins $6.5B Freezing Order
description:

The latest transfers bring the total moved since November 17 to nearly 291,000 ETH, worth more than..
The post Binance Hacker Moves Another $248M of Ethereum as the Exchange Wins $6.5B Freezing Order appeared first on 99Bitcoins.
fullContent:
The Binance hacker has moved another $248 million in Ethereum as the exchange secures a major legal victory against the attackers. Blockchain tracker Lookonchain reported that 137,602 ETH moved across multiple wallets today, extending a three-day distribution spree.

The latest transfers bring the total moved since November 17 to nearly 291,000 ETH, worth more than $500 million. The activity comes as Binance pursues a worldwide freezing order from Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) courts.

The court order covers up to $6.5 billion in assets and targets unidentified individuals behind the October 29 breach. Binance now has a legal route to pursue frozen funds, but the attackers are still shifting hundreds of millions through Ethereum wallets.

Market Cap

Binance Pockets $6.5B Court Order as Hackers Keep Moving Funds

Binance secured the worldwide freezing injunction yesterday, giving its recovery operation a significant legal boost. The ADGM Court also issued separate orders covering specific stolen assets held by third parties.

Eighteen crypto companies must maintain existing freezes and cannot lend, swap, or mix the affected tokens. They include Circle and World Liberty Financial, neither of which faces allegations of wrongdoing.

Binance’s lawyers have identified 26,000 wallet addresses holding stolen assets. The exchange says around $2.85 billion has already been frozen or intercepted, or 45% of the original theft.

Tether has separately frozen $1.5 billion linked to the attack. Although the stablecoin issuer was not named in the court order, it is working directly with Binance on returning the funds.

The legal offensive comes as Binance tries to recover assets that investigators have traced across multiple blockchains. The exchange has already reimbursed affected customers and covered the financial loss. This leaves billions worth of crypto still moving through wallets controlled by the attackers.

DISCOVER: 15+ Best Crypto IPO to Watch in 2026

Binance Hacker’s Ethereum Transfers Reach Nearly 291,000 ETH in Three Days

The movement involved 12 transfers to 12 separate recipient addresses. Eleven transactions carried 12,000 ETH each, while the final transfer contained 5,602 ETH.

The transfers followed two large movements earlier this week. Hack-linked wallets redistributed 74,880 ETH on November 17 and another 78,415 ETH on November 18.

Combined, the three batches account for approximately 290,898 ETH. The latest $248.23 million transfer represents the largest daily movement identified during this period.

The Binance hacker has moved another 137,602 $ETH ($248.23M) for laundering.https://t.co/jKWvcOSJCB pic.twitter.com/ZcIoZLlAhA

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 19, 2026

The FBI attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor operation. Its October 31 alert identified Ethereum addresses operated by or closely connected to the attackers.

Some of the earlier transfers have already entered Bitcoin. Blockchain intelligence firm Elliptic identified 2,100 ETH converted into BTC from the November 17 movement. Some of the hacker’s Bitcoin has since entered CoinJoin transactions, which complicate transaction tracing.

The latest batch consisted of wallet-to-wallet transfers. Splitting the funds across new addresses gives investigators more wallets to track as the laundering operation progresses.

Binance’s legal team is building a constantly updated list of suspect addresses. The court orders can be served through blockchain transactions, allowing exchanges and other service providers to identify affected funds.

The next major milestone arrives on December 1, when the ADGM Court will consider if the proprietary injunction should continue. Meanwhile, every new transfer gives investigators another opportunity to identify where the stolen Ethereum goes.

title: DBS Teams Up With Circle to Give Asian Institutions 24/7 USDC Minting and Redemption
description:
DBS and Circle have partnered to let eligible institutional clients in Asia mint and redeem USDC directly through the bank with near-instant, round-the-clock settlement. The move supports rising demand for tokenised money as shown in a recent DBS survey of large businesses.
The post DBS Teams Up With Circle to Give Asian Institutions 24/7 USDC Minting and Redemption appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
A major Asian bank is partnering with a leading stablecoin issuer to give institutions direct round-the-clock access to minting and redeeming USDC.

DBS says the partnership expands institutional access to the stablecoin across Asia by enabling eligible clients to mint and redeem it through the bank.

The arrangement enables 24/7 USD-USDC settlement for seamless movement of value between fiat and digital environments.

Both firms are also participating in the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s Project BLOOM initiative to promote interoperability among tokenised money forms.

A DBS survey of 422 business leaders from firms with over USD 500 million in revenue across 11 markets found that 88% are already deploying or piloting tokenised money use cases.

Stablecoins lead adoption at 63%, followed by tokenised deposits and money market funds.

Over 60% of respondents are adopting or planning to adopt stablecoins, with expectations for benefits like improved auditability (72%) and real-time cross-border payments (71%).

Institutions are increasingly looking to tokenised money to manage liquidity more efficiently and support their growth across new markets.

“This partnership meets that demand by bringing together Circle’s regulated stablecoin infrastructure and global reach with DBS’ trusted banking, liquidity and digital asset capabilities in Asia.”

Financial institutions are increasingly looking for trusted ways to access stablecoins and integrate blockchain-based infrastructure into their financial operations.

“By combining Circle’s regulated stablecoin infrastructure with DBS’ institutional banking and liquidity capabilities, our partnership represents an important step in expanding institutional access to USDC across Asia, while strengthening the banking infrastructure supporting its global adoption.”

title: My Wallet Introduces 1:1 Cross-Chain Stablecoin Swaps After Being Listed First on WalletConnect
description:
Dubai, United Arab Emirates, 19th November 2026, Chainwire
The post My Wallet Introduces 1:1 Cross-Chain Stablecoin Swaps After Being Listed First on WalletConnect appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
November 19th, 2026 – Dubai, United Arab Emirates

My Wallet users can now receive a different stablecoin on another blockchain at a fixed 1:1 token rate on eligible routes, with no spread, slippage or swap fee charged by the wallet

My Wallet, a self-custodial, open-source crypto wallet serving more than 10 million users, has launched 1:1 swaps for USDT, USDC, USDe and USDS across supported blockchains. On eligible routes, users can switch both stablecoins and networks within a single in-app flow, with the amount they will receive fixed before confirmation. 

The launch follows My Wallet’s listing at the top of WalletConnect’s WalletGuide. The wallet is also WalletConnect Certified and connects users to more than 80,000 compatible apps.

Simplifying Stablecoin Transfers Across Blockchains

According to research published in October 2026 by Coinbase and The Block Pro Research, organic stablecoin transfer volume exceeded $400 million per hour during Q3 2026. Yet stablecoins operate across multiple blockchains and token issuers, creating friction when users need a specific token on a specific network. Even when funds arrive on the right network, users may still hold the wrong stablecoin for a payment, trade or application.

My Wallet addresses this through its in-app swap aggregator, powered by LayerZero, NEAR Intents, and other bridges resulting in the best rate. On eligible stablecoin routes, the aggregator offers a fixed 1:1 token rate, with no exchange-rate spread, slippage or My Wallet swap commission. My Wallet is the first among major crypto wallets to offer 1:1 swaps between different stablecoins across blockchains in a single in-app flow.

How the 1:1 Stablecoin Swaps Work

The fixed 1:1 rate can apply whether users switch to a different stablecoin or move the same token to another blockchain. On a supported cross-chain USDT-to-USDC route, for example, a user sending 10,000 USDT receives exactly 10,000 USDC. The same rate applies when the token stays the same: a supported transfer of 10,000 USDT from Ethereum to TRON delivers exactly 10,000 USDT on TRON.

The 1:1 option is available for swaps above $30 on supported routes. There is no exchange-rate spread, slippage or My Wallet swap commission. Applicable blockchain network fees are paid separately, and the exact destination token amount is shown before confirmation. Other routes may have different rates and fees.

“Stablecoins are supposed to make moving money simpler, but users still have to think about which token they hold and which blockchain it’s on,” said Alexander Zinchuk, founder of My Wallet. “We’re removing that friction. If you hold USDT and need USDC on another network, you should be able to make that change in one step, know exactly how many tokens you’ll receive, and not pay an additional swap commission to your wallet.”

Native Bitcoin and Gasless EVM Transfers

The stablecoin launch follows the introduction of native Bitcoin support in My Wallet. Users can hold, send, receive and swap BTC alongside assets on Ethereum, Solana, TON and other networks, as well as buy Bitcoin with a bank card or sell it for fiat through MoonPay.

My Wallet now supports gasless transfers on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Arbitrum and Optimism, adding to the existing support on Solana and TON. For these EVM transfers, the network fee is deducted from the tokens being sent, so users do not need to acquire a separate native token for gas. Supported assets are USDC on all five EVM networks, USDT on Ethereum and BNB Chain, bridged USDT on Base and Optimism, and USDT0 on Arbitrum. There is no minimum transfer amount or daily limit on the number of transactions.

Together, these innovative features advance My Wallet’s broader “All You Need to Enjoy Crypto” vision, combining asset management, seamless trading, and ease of use into one self-custodial app.

The new features are already available in My Wallet. Swap availability is subject to the selected assets, networks and routes.

About My Wallet

My Wallet is a self-custodial, open-source multichain wallet for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Hyperliquid, TON, TRON, BNB, Base, Robinhood, Monad, Arbitrum, Polygon, and more. Founded in 2022, My Wallet serves over 10 million users across mobile, desktop, web and its Telegram Mini App. The wallet has been audited by CertiK and ranks among the top-5 wallets on CertiK’s Wallet Leaderboard.

My Wallet is WalletConnect Certified and currently listed 1st in WalletConnect’s WalletGuide, connecting users to more than 80,000 compatible apps.

Staking inside My Wallet is powered by Stakee, its own staking protocol, ranked among the top-2 TON DeFi protocols by TVL on DefiLlama.

For more details, users can visit mywallet.io and try My Wallet at mywallet.io/get.

Why Blue-Chip NFTs Like Lil Pudgys and Azuki Are Trending While Crypto Crashes
description:
A basket of blue-chip NFTs is climbing while the tokens around it bleed. CoinGecko’s trending NFT data showed Lil Pudgys up 9.08% on the day, Azuki up 8.06%, CryptoPunks up
The post Why Blue-Chip NFTs Like Lil Pudgys and Azuki Are Trending While Crypto Crashes appeared first on NFT Plazas.
fullContent:
A basket of blue-chip NFTs is climbing while the tokens around it bleed. CoinGecko’s trending NFT data showed Lil Pudgys up 9.08% on the day, Azuki up 8.06%, CryptoPunks up 4.84%, Pudgy Penguins up 4.14% and Mutant Ape Yacht Club (MAYC) up 3.87% in 24-hour floor price.

The backdrop could hardly be worse. Bitcoin slipped below $65,000 and Ether hovered near $1,800 on Wednesday, after a week in which Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan said BTC lost 12% and ETH 14% on a U.S. rate shock. CoinGecko’s Fear & Greed gauge reads Extreme Fear. Yet the oldest, most recognizable NFT collections are quietly moving the other way.

Five blue chips up, three majors down

All five trending collections gained in the same 24 hours that BTC and ETH fell, according to CoinGecko’s trending feed earlier Wednesday. The latest CoinGecko readings show those daily moves cooling to low single digits, with floors still near the levels below.

Collection 24h floor change (trending feed) Latest floor (ETH) Latest floor (USD, approx.) 24h sales
Lil Pudgys +9.08% 0.22 $397 11
Azuki +8.06% 0.48 $869 10
CryptoPunks +4.84% 28.24 $51,140 —
Pudgy Penguins +4.14% 2.39 $4,330 11
MAYC +3.87% 0.88 $1,587 24

On the token side, Bitcoin fell about 1% to $64,694 and Ether about 1.3% to roughly $1,808, per CoinGecko-based reports. Solana bounced around 3% on the day to near $75, but that follows a week in which SOL, like ETH, lost about 22%. Total crypto market value sits near $2.28 trillion.

The NFT sector is far smaller. CoinGecko puts global NFT market cap at about $1.21 billion, with only $1.42 million in 24-hour volume.

Bitcoin (BTC) Price Performance on Nov 18, 2026 (Source: CoinGecko)

Why the basket is breaking from tokens

Three forces explain most of the split: thin order books, ETH-priced floors and a rotation toward established brands.

Thin books move fast. Pudgy Penguins logged 11 sales in 24 hours and Azuki just 10. When sellers pull listings instead of dumping into a falling market, a handful of buyers can lift the cheapest ask several percent. Fungible tokens, by contrast, trade billions a day and absorb every macro headline instantly.

Floors are quoted in ETH. A floor that rises in ETH while ETH drops is partly a currency effect. Sellers who think in dollars raise their ETH asks to defend value, and buyers holding ETH find blue chips cheap in their own unit. Either way, the floor ticks up even when demand barely changes.

Money is rotating into names with history. CryptoSlam data reported by TokenPost shows weekly NFT sales rose 6.13% to $35.11 million in the week to November 17, even as transactions fell 6%. CryptoPunks sales jumped 252% to $1.21 million in that window. Fewer trades, bigger tickets and concentration in marquee collections point to collectors buying quality, not chasing mints.

The IP plays have real-world news

The leaders of this move are brands that sell things off-chain, and each has a fresh headline.

Pudgy Penguins and Lil Pudgys. A PSA 10 Pudgy Penguins Vibes card is listed in eBay-owned Goldin’s Fall TCG Elite Auction, beside Pokémon lots, with extended bidding from November 30. Pudgy products also reached 330 Kung Fu Tea locations this month, adding to plush lines in roughly 2,000 Walmart and 1,800-plus Target stores. Pudgy NFT sales rose 71% week on week to $588,280 in the period to November 14, while the wider NFT market slipped. Lil Pudgys, a 22,222-piece companion set to the 8,888 originals, offers the cheapest entry into that brand at about 0.22 ETH, which helps explain why it led the basket.

The contrast with the brand’s token is stark. PENGU fell nearly 21% in seven days to about $0.005. Holders appear to prefer the NFT, which carries IP licensing upside, over a token whose terms say it has no claim on company revenue.

Azuki. Chiru Labs now calls Azuki an IP company built around a trading card game and a manga. Its second card set, Fractured Domains (AZK-02), is due in stores on November 20, giving traders a dated catalyst two days out.

CryptoPunks and MAYC. Punks remain the sector’s reserve asset, holding about 42% of NFT market-cap dominance on CoinGecko. MAYC, at under 1 ETH, is the cheapest route into the Yuga Labs ape ecosystem and recorded the most sales of the five, at 24.

Why the rally may not stick

The same thin liquidity that lifts floors can sink them just as quickly. With the whole NFT market trading about $1.42 million in 24 hours, a single motivated seller could erase a day’s gains.

The dollar math is also less impressive than the ETH math. A 4% floor gain on CryptoPunks roughly offsets one day of ETH weakness; it does not undo ETH’s 14% slide last week. In USD terms, most of these collections remain far below their 2021–22 peaks; Azuki once floored near 30 ETH.

Macro risk has not cleared. Hougan tied last week’s sell-off to a hotter-than-expected U.S. CPI print, a jump in two-year Treasury yields and about $2 billion in weekend leveraged liquidations, and analysts now point to the December Fed decision as the next test. Pudgy’s ecosystem faces its own friction too: the Abstract chain it backed is set to shut down on December 15.

What to watch next

The next two weeks will show whether blue chips are a refuge or just a pocket of illiquidity. Four markers matter:

  • November 20: Azuki’s Fractured Domains card set lands in stores; watch whether the floor holds after the event.
  • November 30: extended bidding opens on the Pudgy Penguins card at Goldin, a test of crossover demand from traditional collectors.
  • ETH near $1,750: Tuesday’s intraday low. A break lower would pressure ETH-priced floors from both sides.
  • Weekly CryptoSlam sales: a second week of rising dollar volume with concentration in blue chips would confirm rotation rather than noise.

For now, the signal is narrow but clear. In a market gripped by fear, collectors are paying up for NFTs with brands, products and years of history, not for the tokens that trade beside them.

title: NGINX2Root: Five nginx Flaws, Led by CVE-2026-123007. How to Find, Mitigate, and Patch Now
description: Executive Summary NGINX2Root is a set of five nginx vulnerabilities disclosed on November 18, 2026. The lead flaw, CVE-2026-123007, is a memory corruption bug in the way nginx handles HTTP/2 connections. F5, which maintains nginx, rates it 9.2 under CVSS v4.0 and 8.1 under CVSS v3.1. An attacker with no credentials can crash nginx worker […]
fullContent:
Executive Summary

NGINX2Root is a set of five nginx vulnerabilities disclosed on November 18, 2026. The lead flaw, CVE-2026-123007, is a memory corruption bug in the way nginx handles HTTP/2 connections. F5, which maintains nginx, rates it 9.2 under CVSS v4.0 and 8.1 under CVSS v3.1. An attacker with no credentials can crash nginx worker processes, and researchers have demonstrated remote code execution with the privileges of the nginx worker. Where the worker runs without root privileges, an attacker would need an additional escalation path to gain root. This could involve chaining the NGINX vulnerability with a suitable local privilege-escalation flaw. Unpatched builds of NGINX Open Source from 1.9.5 through 1.31.8, and unpatched NGINX Plus builds, are in scope when HTTP/2 is enabled. Fixes shipped in NGINX Open Source 1.30.7 and 1.31.9, and turning off HTTP/2 closes this exposure where patching has to wait. A separate Linux kernel flaw that the researchers used to go from the worker account to root has no patch yet. Start with internet-facing nginx servers that accept HTTP/2, and assign an owner and a deadline to every system still unpatched.

What’s at Risk

A Flaw in nginx Could Hand Attackers the Front Door to Your Applications. nginx is often the first system a web request reaches. It runs as a web server, a reverse proxy (a server that passes requests to the applications behind it), a load balancer, and the entry point to Kubernetes clusters. CVE-2026-123007 is in nginx’s own HTTP/2 code, so no application behind it has to be at fault.

HTTP/2 lets a client tell the server how much data it is allowed to send. nginx can lose count of that allowance when a client cancels requests at the right moment. The bad count later makes nginx copy memory it should not touch.

F5 says the result is typically a crash of the nginx worker, the process that handles live traffic. F5 also says code execution is possible where ASLR, the memory-address randomization that makes exploits harder, is disabled or bypassed. Xint, the team that named NGINX2Root, reports doing exactly that: it leaked memory addresses and then ran commands as the nginx worker over a public HTTPS port.

In Qualys TRU’s assessment, three outcomes matter to the business:

  • Exposure of traffic and keys. Code running in the worker can read requests and responses after nginx decrypts them, including passwords and session tokens. It may also expose TLS private keys that are held in software and accessible to the worker.
  • A foothold behind the perimeter. Backend systems usually trust the proxy in front of them. An attacker on that proxy starts from a trusted position.
  • Outages. A failed attempt can still crash workers and drop connections.

Workers normally run under a restricted account. An attacker gets whatever privileges the worker actually has, so if it already runs as root, no further escalation is needed in that environment. Where it does not, the researchers chained a separate flaw in the Linux kernel’s SCTP code to get root. SCTP is a network protocol, like TCP, that the kernel supports. They report root on the host, including from nginx running inside a Docker container. That kernel flaw has no CVE and no patch yet, so patching nginx removes the remote entry point but not the step to root.

The rest of this post focuses on CVE-2026-123007, the flaw with the widest reach.

Why NGINX2Root Is Also an Application Security Problem 

NGINX2Root is an infrastructure flaw, but its impact lands on the applications behind nginx. Where nginx terminates TLS and proxies requests, every login, API call, and session cookie bound for those applications passes through the worker process in clear text. An attacker running code in that worker sits between users and the applications they trust: 

  • Credentials and tokens become reusable. Passwords, session cookies, API keys, and bearer tokens read from the worker can be replayed directly against the applications and APIs behind the proxy, where they look like legitimate user traffic. 
  • Trust placed in the proxy becomes the attacker’s. Backend services, internal APIs, and admin interfaces are often reachable only from the proxy. Applications that accept identity or client details from headers the proxy sets, such as X-Forwarded-For or user headers added after single sign-on, trust whatever the compromised proxy sends. 
  • Application traffic can be altered in transit. Requests and responses pass through the worker, so the attacker is positioned to change what users receive and what the backend processes, with no change to application code. 
  • One proxy, many applications. A shared reverse proxy or Kubernetes ingress controller often fronts dozens of applications owned by different teams. A worker crash takes all of them offline at once. 

For application security teams, the scoping question is not only which hosts run a vulnerable nginx build, but which applications and APIs depend on them, what data those applications handle, and who owns them. 

Are You Affected?

A system is in scope only when both conditions are true. For an attack to work, the attacker must also be able to open an HTTP/2 connection to nginx itself.

F5 notes that it did not evaluate versions past End of Technical Support. F5 also lists BIG-IP, BIG-IQ, and F5OS as not vulnerable in its advisory.

The checks below come from the researchers’ write-up. Run them on the nginx host. The first shows whether the build includes HTTP/2. The second shows whether the configuration turns it on.

nginx -V 2>&1 | grep -o — ‘–with-http_v2_module’

sudo nginx -T 2>&1 | sed ‘s/#.*//’ | grep -nE ‘listen[[:space:]].*http2|^[[:space:]]*http2[[:space:]]+on[[:space:]]*;’

Run this one from outside your network. ALPN protocol: h2 means the server accepts HTTP/2 from the internet.

openssl s_client -connect HOST:443 -servername HOST -alpn h2 </dev/null 2>&1 | grep -E ‘ALPN protocol:|No ALPN negotiated’

nginx also ships inside other software. Status as of November 18, 2026:

Three cautions when scoping:

  • Do not rely on nginx -v alone. Distributions often fix a flaw without changing the nginx version number. Compare the full package version with the distribution’s advisory.
  • Check where the HTTP/2 connection ends. If a CDN or load balancer handles HTTP/2 in front of nginx, an outside test only reaches that device. Test the nginx port directly.
  • Use internet exposure to order the work, not to close findings. An internal nginx with HTTP/2 on is still reachable by an attacker who is already inside the network.

Exploitation Status

As of November 18, 2026, we have not seen public confirmation of exploitation in the wild.

Working exploit code is public. The team behind NGINX2Root also reports its own exploit working over public IP addresses on AWS, GCP, and Azure, and is holding back the final steps.

The public exploit is hard to use. It sends a very large number of HTTP/2 control messages over one long-lived connection for several minutes, has to reach nginx directly, and depends on a specific memory-copy routine in the standard Linux C library on 64-bit Intel and AMD processors.

These limits slow mass exploitation. In Qualys TRU’s assessment, they do not protect a specific internet-facing server from a capable attacker, and other techniques may follow.

What to Do Now

Updating nginx is the only complete fix. F5 released fixed builds on November 18, 2026.

Linux distributions publish on their own schedules. As of November 18, 2026, Ubuntu and Debian had not shipped fixed packages. Use your vendor’s advisory to identify the fixed package and confirm it addresses CVE-2026-123007.

Restart nginx after you update. A reload applies configuration changes but keeps the old program running, so the flaw stays in memory until a restart.

If you cannot patch today, turn off HTTP/2 on every affected listener. F5 states the flaw affects only configurations that use HTTP/2, and the researchers recommend this as a temporary measure. For the exact steps, see nginx’s documentation for the http2 directive, CERT-EU’s advisory, and section 3.3 of the researchers’ write-up. Clients fall back to HTTP/1.1. Services that need HTTP/2, such as gRPC, will stop working, so test first. This covers CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 only, and it does not replace the patch.

Advice for Risk and Vulnerability Management Teams

Qualys TRU’s advice for the teams running this response:

  • Do not let the score set the deadline: Under CVSS v3.1 this flaw is 8.1, which many remediation policies file as High. Public exploit code and a server that faces the internet matter more than the number. Handle vulnerable nginx deployments with externally reachable HTTP/2 as an emergency.
  • Close findings on evidence: A server is done when the fixed build is installed, nginx has been restarted, and the vendor’s advisory confirms the package covers all five CVEs. Report patched, temporarily mitigated, not exposed by configuration, and unknown as separate states, and do not count unknown as safe.
  • Fix the template as well as the server: Update container images, Helm charts, machine images, and autoscaling templates. Otherwise the next scale-out or failover brings the vulnerable build back.
  • Map each nginx instance to the applications and APIs behind it. A host inventory shows where a vulnerable build is installed; it does not show which applications, owners, and data depend on it. Use that mapping to set priority and to notify application owners, not to close findings. 
  • Put an end date on every workaround: Turning off HTTP/2 covers two of the five flaws, and the next configuration push can undo it. Record who owns each exception and when it ends.
  • Decide what to do with nginx that will not get a fix: The community ingress-nginx project is archived, and the older NGINX Plus R-series branches have no fixed build listed, although fixed NGINX Plus 37.x releases exist. These need a migration plan or a signed risk acceptance.
  • Treat privilege escalation flaws as part of this response: Where the worker runs without root privileges, an attacker would need an additional escalation path to gain root. The newly disclosed SCTP flaw is one such path, and any other local privilege-escalation flaw that can be exploited from the worker’s context could serve the same purpose. Patch known local privilege-escalation flaws on nginx hosts, in the kernel and elsewhere, with the same urgency. A current kernel does not mean the SCTP flaw is fixed, because that flaw has no patch yet.
